title: 弘治二年江西鄉試錄
text:
江西鄉試錄序
聖天子龍飛之又明年是為弘治
己酉大比興賢之歲四方岳
牧祗奉
明詔舉行舊章而江西所司尤慎
重焉前事禮部以廷議申飭
諸藩酌簡惟宜時鎮守太監
===
鄧原巡按監察御史趙炯洎
藩臬重臣僉議江右人繁士
衆惟提學副使敖山所選來
者率由以容庶無遺才哉乃
如制圍棘三試之内而提調
監試則左布政使秦民悅按
察使魏富左參政李蕙僉事
punctuated:
江西鄉試錄序

聖天子龍飛之又明年，是為弘治己酉，大比興賢之歲。四方岳牧祗奉明詔，舉行舊章，而江西所司尤慎重焉。前事禮部以廷議申飭諸藩，酌簡惟宜。時鎮守太監鄧原、巡按監察御史趙炯洎藩臬重臣僉議：江右人繁士衆，惟提學副使敖山所選來者，率由以容，庶無遺才哉！乃如制圍棘，三試之。内而提調、監試，則左布政使秦民悅、按察使魏富、左參政李蕙、僉事
translation_en:
Preface to the Record of the Jiangxi Provincial Examination

In the second year after the sagely Son of Heaven ascended the throne, the jiyou year of the Hongzhi reign [1489], the triennial examination was held to advance worthy men. Regional authorities everywhere reverently obeyed the imperial edict and implemented the established regulations; the responsible officials in Jiangxi exercised particular care. Previously, the Ministry of Rites [?], acting on court deliberations, had reiterated instructions to the provincial administrations that they exercise due judgment in selection. At that time, the Regional Defender, Grand Eunuch Deng Yuan, the Regional Inspector, Investigating Censor Zhao Jiong, and the senior officials of the Provincial Administration and Surveillance Commissions jointly deliberated: “Jiangyou has a large population and many scholars. Let all those selected and sent here by Ao Shan, the Education Intendant and Surveillance Vice Commissioner, be admitted [?], so that, we hope, no talented man will be overlooked!” Accordingly, as prescribed, they enclosed the examination grounds with thorn branches and examined the candidates in three sessions. Within the grounds, those responsible for proctoring and supervising the examination were Qin Minyue, Left Provincial Administration Commissioner; Wei Fu, Surveillance Commissioner; Li Hui, Left Administration Vice Commissioner; and the Surveillance Assistant Commissioner …

title: 弘治二年江西鄉試錄
text:
張〔淮〕外而防範則右布政使
張〔琳〕右參政陳〔道〕副使錢〔山〕
張〔璁〕左參議朱〔文〕諸讓右
參議李〔魁〕僉事江〔源〕羅〔九鼎〕
陳〔祥〕趙〔艮〕汪〔舜民〕諸凡執事
皆遴選以充而內外綜理則
御史〔炯〕寔監臨之〔瑛〕繆膺校
===
閱矢心協力惟明惟公得文
理俱優者九十有五人遵定
額也爰錄諸執事洎中式者
氏名并擇其文之可觀者為
賢書以獻于
天府〔瑛〕謹敘其端恭惟
皇明誕膺隆眷奄有天下自我
punctuated:
張〔淮〕。外而防範，則右布政使張〔琳〕、右參政陳〔道〕、副使錢〔山〕、張〔璁〕、左參議朱〔文〕、諸讓、右參議李〔魁〕、僉事江〔源〕、羅〔九鼎〕、陳〔祥〕、趙〔艮〕、汪〔舜民〕。諸凡執事，皆遴選以充，而內外綜理，則御史〔炯〕寔監臨之。〔瑛〕繆膺校閱，矢心協力，惟明惟公，得文理俱優者九十有五人，遵定額也。爰錄諸執事洎中式者氏名，并擇其文之可觀者，為賢書，以獻于天府。〔瑛〕謹敘其端。
恭惟皇明誕膺隆眷，奄有天下，自我
translation_en:
…Zhang Huai. Responsibility for security outside the examination compound fell to Right Provincial Administration Commissioner Zhang Lin; Right Administration Vice Commissioner Chen Dao; Surveillance Vice Commissioners Qian Shan and Zhang Cong; Left Administration Assistant Commissioners Zhu Wen and Zhu Rang [?]; Right Administration Assistant Commissioner Li Kui; and Surveillance Assistant Commissioners Jiang Yuan, Luo Jiuding, Chen Xiang, Zhao Gen, and Wang Shunmin. All personnel were carefully selected to fill their posts. Censor Jiong exercised overall supervision of affairs both inside and outside the compound, serving as Supervising Official.
I, Ying, unworthily received the charge of examining the papers. We pledged our wholehearted cooperation, seeking only discernment and impartiality, and selected ninety-five men whose writing and reasoning were both excellent, in accordance with the established quota. We therefore recorded the names of the examination personnel and successful candidates, and selected noteworthy examples of the latter’s writing to compile a record of worthy men for presentation to the imperial repository. I, Ying, respectfully set forth these introductory remarks.
Reverently considering how our august Ming dynasty received Heaven’s abundant favor and came to possess all under Heaven, beginning with our …

title: 弘治二年江西鄉試錄
text:
太祖高皇帝創制垂統以歲戊申
建元洪武
聖子神孫繼繼繩繩百二十載至
今上皇帝英明聰哲敬
天法祖紀元弘治歲復戊申
天運載周景命維新百度咸舉而
命卿論秀先務攸急萬邦黎
===
獻咸有帝臣之頌而江右東
南大藩賢才淵海自昔傑魁
譽髦乘時彙興駿功顯烈後
先相望矧素荷
祖宗菁莪之化今際
聖明維新之運固宜揚眉吐氣呈
奇發粹彬彬顒顒袂聯武蹟
punctuated: 太祖高皇帝創制垂統，以歲戊申建元洪武，聖子神孫繼繼繩繩，百二十載。至今上皇帝，英明聰哲，敬天法祖，紀元弘治，歲復戊申。天運載周，景命維新，百度咸舉，而命卿論秀，先務攸急。萬邦黎獻咸有帝臣之頌，而江右，東南大藩，賢才淵海，自昔傑魁譽髦，乘時彙興，駿功顯烈，後先相望。矧素荷祖宗菁莪之化，今際聖明維新之運，固宜揚眉吐氣，呈奇發粹，彬彬顒顒，袂聯武蹟，
translation_en:
…Emperor Taizu Gao established the institutions and handed down the dynastic succession, inaugurating the Hongwu era in the wushen year. His sagely sons and divine grandsons continued the succession unbroken for 120 years. Now our reigning emperor, brilliant, discerning, intelligent, and wise, reveres Heaven and takes his ancestors as his models. He inaugurated the Hongzhi era, and the year was once again wushen. Heaven’s cycle had come full circle, and the great mandate was renewed. All affairs of government were set in motion, with the appointment of high ministers and the appraisal of outstanding talent accorded particular urgency among the foremost tasks.
The worthy men of every region all sing praises of serving as the emperor’s ministers. Jiangyou, a great bulwark of the southeast and a deep reservoir of worthy talent, has from antiquity seen outstanding and renowned men arise together as opportunity offered. Those distinguished by great achievements and illustrious deeds have followed one another in succession. Moreover, this region has long benefited from the ancestral emperors’ nurturing of scholars, celebrated in the “Luxuriant Mugwort” ode, and now encounters the renewing fortunes of our sagely and enlightened sovereign. Surely its scholars should raise their brows and breathe freely, display their exceptional gifts and bring forth their finest qualities, cultivated and dignified, their sleeves touching and their footsteps following one another…

title: 弘治二年江西鄉試錄
text:
厥盛臻茲哉雖然盛不于其
衆而于其大昔孟子論士有
一鄉之士有一國之士有天
下之士小大固有間矣然天
下之士必有所居之國所生
之鄉未可謂一鄉一國之士
而非天下士也今諸上子秀
===
舉鄉闈名登賢書宴歌鹿鳴
拔出乎一鄉一國之中方縣
次續食計偕以升將與天下
之士爭先角捷於春官以進
于
天子之庭以備夫天下國家之用
盍亦思以天下為己任哉其
punctuated: 厥盛臻茲哉！雖然，盛不于其衆，而于其大。昔孟子論士，有一鄉之士，有一國之士，有天下之士，小大固有間矣。然天下之士，必有所居之國、所生之鄉，未可謂一鄉一國之士而非天下士也。今諸上子秀舉鄉闈，名登賢書，宴歌《鹿鳴》，拔出乎一鄉一國之中，方縣次續食，計偕以升，將與天下之士爭先角捷於春官，以進于天子之庭，以備夫天下國家之用。盍亦思以天下為己任哉！其
translation_en:
…Their flourishing has reached such heights! Yet flourishing lies not in their numbers but in their greatness. In discussing scholars, Mencius distinguished scholars of a single village, scholars of a single state, and scholars of all under Heaven: there are indeed differences of lesser and greater scope. Nevertheless, a scholar of all under Heaven must have a state in which he resides and a village in which he was born. One cannot say that a scholar of a village or a state is therefore not a scholar of all under Heaven.

Now you gentlemen [?], selected for your excellence in the Provincial Examination, have had your names entered in the register of worthies and have attended the banquet at which “The Deer Call” was sung. You have distinguished yourselves among the men of your villages and your province. You are now about to travel to the capital, receiving provisions at successive county stages and accompanying the tribute mission. You will compete with scholars from all under Heaven for precedence and success at the Ministry of Rites, and thereby advance to the Son of Heaven’s court, ready to serve the realm and the state. Should you not also think of taking all under Heaven as your own responsibility? Surely you…

title: 弘治二年江西鄉試錄
text:
必隨所任使無崇卑無内外
無險夷匪躬匪懈始終弗渝
補衮職於
一人沛膏澤於萬姓弘治化於無
疆先天下之憂而憂如宋范
希文身繫天下安危如唐裴
太師自任天下之重如商之
===
阿衡斯則尚友乎古人不徒
為天下士烜赫章大度越尋
常天下後世必將指而稱之
曰此江右清淑所鍾之傑
龍飛第一科鄉舉之士豈惟有
裨於
國家亦且有光於科目增重於
punctuated: 必隨所任使，無崇卑，無内外，無險夷，匪躬匪懈，始終弗渝，補衮職於一人，沛膏澤於萬姓，弘治化於無疆。先天下之憂而憂，如宋范希文；身繫天下安危，如唐裴太師；自任天下之重，如商之阿衡。斯則尚友乎古人，不徒為天下士，烜赫章大，度越尋常。天下後世必將指而稱之曰：「此江右清淑所鍾之傑，龍飛第一科鄉舉之士。」豈惟有裨於國家，亦且有光於科目，增重於
translation_en: …must, whatever duties they are assigned, whether high or low, within the capital or outside it, perilous or peaceful, neither spare themselves nor slacken, remaining steadfast from beginning to end. They must remedy shortcomings in the sovereign’s discharge of his duties, lavish beneficence upon the myriad people, and extend the transforming influence of good government without limit. They should grieve before all others under Heaven grieve, like Fan Xiwen of the Song; make their own persons pivotal to the security or peril of all under Heaven, like Grand Preceptor Pei of the Tang; and take upon themselves the weight of all under Heaven, like the Aheng of the Shang. Thus they would befriend the ancients across the ages, becoming more than merely scholars of the realm: illustrious and eminent, surpassing the ordinary. People throughout the realm and in later generations will surely point to them and say: “These are the outstanding men in whom the pure and благоприятные influences of Jiangyou are concentrated, the provincial graduates of the first examination following the emperor’s accession.” Not only will they benefit the state; they will also bring glory to the examinations and add prestige to…

title: 弘治二年江西鄉試錄
text:
鄉國不亦偉歟予不佞滦有
望於諸君子其懋哉
直隷保定府祁州滦澤縣儒
學教諭傅瑛謹序
punctuated:
鄉國，不亦偉歟？予不佞，滦有望於諸君子，其懋哉！
直隷保定府祁州滦澤縣儒學教諭傅瑛謹序。
translation_en:
…to your native region—is this not magnificent? Though I am untalented, I have great hopes for you gentlemen [the character 滦 is doubtful]. Strive diligently!
Fu Ying, Instructor in the Confucian School of Luanze County [?], Qizhou, Baoding Prefecture, in the directly administered region, respectfully writes this preface.

第壹場

四書

非禮勿視，非禮勿聽，非禮勿言，非禮勿動。

博學之，審問之，愼思之，明辨之，篤行之。有弗學，學之弗能，弗措也；有弗問，問之弗知，弗措也；有弗思，思之弗得，弗措也；有弗辨，辨之弗明，弗措也；有弗行，行之弗篤，弗措也。人一能之，己百之；人十能之，己千之。

王者之民皞皞如也。

文明以健，中正而應，君子正也。唯君子爲能通天下之志。

易

王用享于帝，吉。

聖人立象以盡意，設卦以盡情僞，繫辭焉以盡其言，變而通之以盡利，鼓之舞之以盡神。

天地之大德曰生。
translation_en:
First Session

Four Books

Do not look at anything contrary to ritual propriety; do not listen to anything contrary to ritual propriety; do not say anything contrary to ritual propriety; do not do anything contrary to ritual propriety.

Study broadly, inquire carefully, reflect thoughtfully, discriminate clearly, and put what you learn earnestly into practice. One may refrain from studying, but once one studies, one must not stop until one has mastered it; one may refrain from asking, but once one asks, one must not stop until one understands; one may refrain from reflecting, but once one reflects, one must not stop until one grasps the matter; one may refrain from discriminating, but once one discriminates, one must not stop until the distinctions are clear; one may refrain from acting, but once one acts, one must not stop until one carries it out earnestly. What others can accomplish with one effort, accomplish with a hundred; what others can accomplish with ten efforts, accomplish with a thousand.

The people of a true king are tranquil and contented.

Cultured and enlightened, yet strong; central and correct, and meeting with a response: this is the correctness of the gentleman. Only the gentleman can comprehend the aspirations of all under Heaven.

Book of Changes (Yi)

The king makes an offering to the Supreme Lord. Auspicious.

The sages established images to express their meaning fully, set out the hexagrams to express fully the genuine and the false, and appended statements to give full expression to their words. They transformed things and enabled them to proceed, thereby realizing their benefits fully; they stirred and animated them, thereby fully manifesting their numinous efficacy.

The great virtue of Heaven and Earth is called giving life.

translation_en:
Book of Documents

Be discerning and single-minded; sincerely hold fast to the mean.

His renown and instruction reached throughout the Four Seas.

The people of antiquity would instruct and admonish one another, protect and show kindness to one another, and teach and counsel one another.

When the statements concerning the five kinds of offenses have been examined and found credible, determine the appropriate one of the five punishments. Where a case does not warrant one of the five punishments upon examination, determine the appropriate one of the five fines. Where the five fines do not fit, determine which of the five judicial errors applies.

Book of Odes

The woman says, “The cock is crowing.” The man says, “It is only daybreak. Rise and look at the night sky: the morning star shines brightly. The birds will soon be soaring and flying; shoot the wild ducks and geese with your corded arrows.” When your arrows strike them, I will prepare them with you. We shall drink wine together, and I shall grow old with you. With zithers large and small at hand, all is peaceful and harmonious. Knowing that you come to me, I give you assorted girdle pendants; knowing your kindness toward me, I offer you assorted pendants; knowing your love for me, I repay you with assorted pendants.

There are men to rely upon and men to lend support, men of filial devotion and virtue, to guide and assist. The gracious and easygoing lord is a model for the four quarters. Dignified and lofty, like jade tablets, gui and zhang! Of excellent reputation and standing, the gracious and easygoing lord is the guiding cord of the four quarters. Phoenixes fly, their feathers rustling; together they gather and alight here. In abundant numbers the king has worthy men; they are employed by the lord and cherish the Son of Heaven.

In autumn, in the ninth month, Jing defeated the army of Cai at Shen and returned with Xianwu, Marquis of Cai. 〔Tenth year of Duke Zhuang.〕
An envoy from Jing came on a diplomatic visit. 〔Twenty-third year of Duke Zhuang.〕 In autumn, Jing attacked Zheng. 〔Twenty-eighth year of Duke Zhuang.〕
The men of Chu attacked Zheng. 〔First year of Duke Xi.〕 In autumn, the Duke of Song, the Viscount of Chu, the Marquis of Chen, the Marquis of Cai, the Earl of Zheng, the Baron of Xu, and the Earl of Cao met at Yu. They seized the Duke of Song and used him in attacking Song. 〔Twenty-first year of Duke Xi.〕 In the eleventh month, the duke went to Chu. 〔Twenty-eighth year of Duke Xiang.〕 Shusun Bao met Zhao Wu of Jin, Prince Wei of Chu, Guo Ruo of Qi, Xiang Xu of Song, Qi E of Wei, Prince Zhao of Chen, Gongsun Guisheng of Cai, Han Hu of Zheng, and representatives of Xu and Cao at Guo. 〔First year of Duke Zhao.〕
In summer, the duke met the chief minister, the Duke of Zhou, the Marquis of Qi, the Viscount of Song, the Marquis of Wei, the Earl of Zheng, the Baron of Xu, and the Earl of Cao at Kuiqiu. 〔Ninth year of Duke Xi.〕
Zheng abandoned its army. 〔Second year of Duke Min.〕 In summer, on the jisi day of the fourth month, the Marquis of Jin and the armies of Qi, Song, and Qin fought the men of Chu at Chengpu. The army of Chu suffered a crushing defeat. 〔Twenty-eighth year of Duke Xi.〕
In spring, on the renzi day of the second month according to the royal calendar, Hua Yuan of Song, commanding an army, fought Prince Guisheng of Zheng, also commanding an army, at Daji. The army of Song suffered a crushing defeat, and they captured …

title: 弘治二年江西鄉試錄
text:
宋華元〔宣公二年〕
冬十有一月叔孫僑如會晉士燮齊高無
咎宋華元衛孫林父鄭公子鰌邾人會
吳于鍾離〔成公十五年〕
禮記
君天下曰天子朝諸侯分職授政任功曰
予一人
陰陽和而萬物得
聖人南面而聽天下所且先者五民不與
焉一曰治親二曰報功三曰舉賢四曰
使能五曰存愛五者一得於天下民無
不足無不贍者
明則有禮樂幽則有鬼神
===
第貳場
論
聖人一視同仁
詔誥表〔內科壹道〕
擬漢定元功位次詔〔高帝六年〕
punctuated:
宋華元。〔宣公二年〕
冬十有一月，叔孫僑如會晉士燮、齊高無咎、宋華元、衛孫林父、鄭公子鰌、邾人，會吳于鍾離。〔成公十五年〕
禮記
君天下曰天子，朝諸侯、分職授政、任功，曰予一人。
陰陽和而萬物得。
聖人南面而聽天下，所且先者五，民不與焉。一曰治親，二曰報功，三曰舉賢，四曰使能，五曰存愛。五者一得於天下，民無不足、無不贍者。
明則有禮樂，幽則有鬼神。
第貳場
論
聖人一視同仁。
詔誥表〔內科壹道〕
擬漢定元功位次詔。〔高帝六年〕
translation_en:
… Hua Yuan of Song.〔Second year of Duke Xuan〕
In winter, in the eleventh month, Shusun Qiaoru met with Shi Xie of Jin, Gao Wujiu of Qi, Hua Yuan of Song, Sun Linfu of Wei, Prince Qiu of Zheng, and a representative of Zhu to meet with Wu at Zhongli.〔Fifteenth year of Duke Cheng〕

Record of Rites
When ruling All under Heaven, he is called the Son of Heaven; when receiving the regional lords at court, assigning offices and delegating governance, and entrusting responsibilities according to merit, he calls himself “I, the One Man.”
When yin and yang are in harmony, all things attain their proper condition.
When the sage faces south and attends to the affairs of All under Heaven, there are five matters to which he gives priority; the common people are not included among them. The first is regulating relations with kin; the second, rewarding merit; the third, promoting the worthy; the fourth, employing the capable; and the fifth, preserving loving regard. Once these five are all realized throughout All under Heaven, none among the people will lack sufficiency or adequate provision.
In the visible realm there are rites and music; in the unseen realm there are ghosts and spirits.

Second Session
Discourse
The sage regards all alike and treats all with benevolence.

Imperial Edicts, Proclamations, and Memorials〔One topic within this category [?]〕
Compose an imperial edict in the manner of the Han dynasty establishing the order of precedence among those of foremost merit.〔Sixth year of Emperor Gao〕

title: 弘治二年江西鄉試錄
text:
擬唐以房玄齡杜如晦為僕射魏徵守秘
書監參預朝政誥〔貞觀三年〕
擬宋復以朱熹為秘閣脩譔謝表〔紹熙二年〕
判語〔五條〕
增減官文書
私借官車船
詐冒給路引
威力制縛人
造作不如法
===
第叄場
策五道
問古之君天下者必立言以垂教明刑以
弼教如唐虞之敷五教明五刑是已洪
惟我
太祖高皇帝膺天明命奠我中夏
御製大誥三編大明律令即唐虞敷教明刑
之意也迨
太宗文皇帝之為善陰隲孝順事實
punctuated:
擬唐以房玄齡、杜如晦為僕射，魏徵守秘書監、參預朝政誥〔貞觀三年〕。
擬宋復以朱熹為秘閣脩譔謝表〔紹熙二年〕。
判語〔五條〕：增減官文書；私借官車船；詐冒給路引；威力制縛人；造作不如法。

第叄場
策五道
問：古之君天下者，必立言以垂教，明刑以弼教，如唐虞之敷五教、明五刑是已。洪惟我太祖高皇帝膺天明命，奠我中夏，御製《大誥》三編、《大明律令》，即唐虞敷教明刑之意也。迨太宗文皇帝之《為善陰隲》《孝順事實》
translation_en:
Compose, as if for the Tang court, a proclamation appointing Fang Xuanling and Du Ruhui as Vice Directors of the Department of State Affairs, and Wei Zheng as acting Director of the Palace Library, participating in the administration of court affairs.〔Third year of Zhenguan.〕
Compose, as if for the Song court, a memorial of thanks for the reappointment of Zhu Xi as Compiler in the Secret Archives.〔Second year of Shaoxi.〕
Legal judgments〔five items〕: Adding to or deleting from official documents; privately borrowing government carts or boats; fraudulently obtaining travel permits through impersonation; forcibly restraining and binding a person; manufacturing articles contrary to prescribed standards.

Third Session
Five Policy Questions
Question: Those who ruled all under Heaven in antiquity invariably set forth pronouncements to transmit moral instruction and made punishments clear to support that instruction. Such were the dissemination of the five teachings and the clarification of the five punishments under Tang and Yu. We reverently reflect that our Emperor Taizu Gao received Heaven’s illustrious mandate and firmly established our central realm. His imperially composed Grand Pronouncements, in three compilations, and the Laws and Ordinances of the Great Ming embody precisely the intention of Tang and Yu in disseminating instruction and clarifying punishments. Coming down to Emperor Taizong Wen’s Doing Good and Receiving Hidden Blessings and True Accounts of Filial Obedience…

title: 弘治二年江西鄉試錄
text:
宣宗章皇帝之五倫書
英宗睿皇帝之大明一統誌
憲宗純皇帝之續資治通鑑綱目咸欲闡揚
祖訓以建
皇極其間敷教明刑之要可得而悉聞與
祖宗以來重熙累洽教化覃被固宜家詩書而
人禮樂矣然而遠聲教者不能無邪枉
之民罹典刑者時或有奸究之輩是又
何與伊欲黎民於變刑期無刑以比隆
===
唐虞之治者果何行而可諸士子懷抱
利器方將進用以佐
聖天子維新之化請條陳之以觀所學
問忠孝立而後臣子之事備學者所當熟
講而究心者試以古人有聲於忠孝者
與諸士子評之有楚執其母而脅以背
漢者有賊執其母而招以城降者事漢
死敵而殺母則不孝歸楚降城而全母
則不忠此忠孝之難兩全也而善處之
punctuated:
宣宗章皇帝之《五倫書》、英宗睿皇帝之《大明一統誌》、憲宗純皇帝之《續資治通鑑綱目》，咸欲闡揚祖訓，以建皇極。其間敷教明刑之要，可得而悉聞與？祖宗以來，重熙累洽，教化覃被，固宜家詩書而人禮樂矣。然而遠聲教者，不能無邪枉之民；罹典刑者，時或有奸究之輩，是又何與？伊欲黎民於變，刑期無刑，以比隆唐虞之治者，果何行而可？諸士子懷抱利器，方將進用，以佐聖天子維新之化，請條陳之，以觀所學。

問：忠孝立而後臣子之事備，學者所當熟講而究心者。試以古人有聲於忠孝者，與諸士子評之。有楚執其母而脅以背漢者，有賊執其母而招以城降者。事漢死敵而殺母，則不孝；歸楚降城而全母，則不忠。此忠孝之難兩全也，而善處之
translation_en:
…Emperor Zhang of the Xuanzong reign’s Book of the Five Relationships; Emperor Rui of the Yingzong reign’s Comprehensive Gazetteer of the Great Ming; and Emperor Chun of the Xianzong reign’s Continuation of the Outline and Details of the Comprehensive Mirror for Aid in Government—all sought to elucidate and propagate the ancestral instructions and thereby establish the imperial standard. May we hear in full the essentials they contain concerning the dissemination of moral teaching and the clarification of punishments? Since the time of the imperial ancestors, successive reigns have enjoyed prosperity and peace, and moral instruction has spread far and wide. Surely every household should cultivate the Odes and Documents, and every person rites and music. Yet among those beyond the reach of imperial influence and instruction, there are inevitably wicked and perverse people; and among those subjected to statutory punishments, there are still sometimes treacherous wrongdoers [?]. Why is this so? If one wishes to transform the common people and employ punishments with the aim of making punishments unnecessary, thus matching the flourishing rule of Yao and Shun, what measures would actually accomplish this? You candidates possess talents ready for use and are about to enter service to assist the sagely Son of Heaven’s work of renewal. Please set out your proposals point by point, so that we may assess your learning.

Question: Only when loyalty and filial piety are established are the duties of subjects and sons fulfilled. These are matters that students should discuss thoroughly and examine with utmost care. Let us consider with you candidates some men of antiquity renowned for loyalty and filial piety. There was one whose mother was seized by Chu, which threatened him to make him betray Han; there was another whose mother was seized by rebels, who sought to induce him to surrender his city. To serve Han and fight the enemy to the death, thereby causing one’s mother to be killed, would be unfilial; to join Chu or surrender one’s city and thereby preserve one’s mother would be disloyal. Here lies the difficulty of fulfilling both loyalty and filial piety. Yet the means of handling this properly…

title: 弘治二年江西鄉試錄
text:
術安在有因征伐四出而欲父子同死
南越者有因都督太桁而父子同死王
事者以子死父之孝無不同以臣死君
之忠無或異若忠孝之兼盡也而得失
之議何歸陳情乞養志則孝矣移孝為
忠可也何以固郤徵辟之勤攀百揣泣
孝則得矣揚名顯親亦可也何以不恤
絜身亂倫之誚奉檄而喜小人奔競富
貴之常態也何不見譏於時絶裾而去
===
君子慷慨立功之大節也何以取刺於
衆之數君子之所以為忠孝者未必無
得失之可言也夫子不曰殺身成仁守
死善道諸子積學待用久矣設以身處
數子之地必有善處之術以求忠孝之
兩全也幸為我明言之〔毋讓〕
問識時務者在俊傑諸生育于學校皆以
俊傑自負久矣然窮之所養乃達施之
地先聖不曰如或知爾則何以哉試以
punctuated:
術安在？有因征伐四出而欲父子同死南越者，有因都督太桁而父子同死王事者。以子死父之孝，無不同；以臣死君之忠，無或異。若忠孝之兼盡也，而得失之議何歸？陳情乞養，志則孝矣；移孝為忠，可也，何以固郤徵辟之勤？攀百揣泣，孝則得矣；揚名顯親，亦可也，何以不恤絜身亂倫之誚？奉檄而喜，小人奔競富貴之常態也，何不見譏於時？絶裾而去，君子慷慨立功之大節也，何以取刺於衆？之數君子之所以為忠孝者，未必無得失之可言也。夫子不曰「殺身成仁」、「守死善道」？諸子積學待用久矣，設以身處數子之地，必有善處之術，以求忠孝之兩全也。幸為我明言之〔毋讓〕。
問：識時務者在俊傑。諸生育于學校，皆以俊傑自負久矣。然窮之所養，乃達施之地。先聖不曰「如或知爾，則何以哉」？試以
translation_en:
…where is the method for handling this well? There was one who, because military expeditions were being dispatched in every direction, wished that father and son might die together in Nanyue; there was another who, while commanding at Ta heng [?], died together with his sons in service to the throne. In the filial devotion of a son dying for his father, they were alike; in the loyalty of a subject dying for his ruler, they did not differ. It would seem that both loyalty and filial devotion were fully fulfilled; yet how should their merits and failings be judged?
One set forth his circumstances and begged leave to care for his elder: his intention was filial indeed. Yet he could have transferred his filial devotion to loyal service. Why, then, did he firmly reject repeated efforts to summon him to office? Another clung to a tree and wept [?]: in filial devotion he succeeded. Yet he could also have won renown and brought honor to his parents. Why, then, did he disregard the reproach that, by keeping himself pure, he disrupted the human relationships? Rejoicing upon receiving an official summons is the usual behavior of petty men scrambling for wealth and rank. Why did this draw no criticism in his own time? Tearing off one's robe-skirt and departing displays the great resolve of a gentleman determined to accomplish deeds of merit. Why did this invite public censure?
In the ways these gentlemen [?] practiced loyalty and filial devotion, there may well be merits and failings to discuss. Did the Master not say, “Sacrifice one's life to fulfill humaneness,” and “Hold fast to the good Way unto death”? You gentlemen have long accumulated learning while awaiting employment. Were you to put yourselves in the positions of these men, you would surely have a sound method of handling their circumstances, seeking to fulfill both loyalty and filial devotion. Please explain it clearly to me. 〔Do not demur.〕
Question: Those who understand the affairs of their times are outstanding men. You students have been nurtured in the schools and have long prided yourselves on being outstanding men. Yet what one cultivates while out of office is the foundation for what one puts into practice upon attaining office. Did the sage of old not say, “If someone were to recognize your abilities, what would you do?” Try, taking …

title: 弘治二年江西鄉試錄
text:
時政之大者舉其一二商確之科目賢
才所由進也古今之法詳矣何者為至
當考課治道所由興也古今之法備矣
何者為至要教化之原在乎士習何法
而可以息奔競之風民俗之害起於左
道何法而可以袪異端之惑夫舉賢才
隆治道敦教化善風俗時政無大於此
者幸斟酌其法之合於古而宜於今者
為我言之將採而獻于
上焉
===
問三代將相才德兼全勳庸表著者固無
容議矣漢唐而下或得或失其間豈無
三代之英乎請舉其大者與諸生評之
人稱長者坐鎮雅俗與忠義奮發奉身
清儉者其德優矣其才何所見乎身兼
數器慷慨論事與敵稱飛將人稱鐵山
者其才優矣其勲何所見乎誅呂安劉
應變成務與戰勝攻取擲貽立實者其
punctuated:
時政之大者，舉其一二商確之。科目，賢才所由進也，古今之法詳矣，何者為至當？考課，治道所由興也，古今之法備矣，何者為至要？教化之原在乎士習，何法而可以息奔競之風？民俗之害起於左道，何法而可以袪異端之惑？夫舉賢才、隆治道、敦教化、善風俗，時政無大於此者。幸斟酌其法之合於古而宜於今者，為我言之，將採而獻于上焉。

問：三代將相才德兼全、勳庸表著者，固無容議矣。漢唐而下，或得或失，其間豈無三代之英乎？請舉其大者，與諸生評之。人稱長者、坐鎮雅俗，與忠義奮發、奉身清儉者，其德優矣，其才何所見乎？身兼數器、慷慨論事，與敵稱飛將、人稱鐵山者，其才優矣，其勲何所見乎？誅呂安劉、應變成務，與戰勝攻取、擲貽立實者，其
translation_en:
…take one or two of the major matters of current government and examine them carefully. The examination system is the means by which worthy and talented men advance. Its methods, ancient and modern, have been elaborated in detail: which are most appropriate? Performance evaluations are the means by which good government flourishes. Their methods, ancient and modern, are fully developed: which are most essential? The source of moral instruction lies in the conduct of scholars: by what methods can the fashion for scrambling after advancement be quelled? Harm to popular customs arises from heterodox practices: by what methods can the delusions of heterodox teachings be dispelled? Promoting worthy and talented men, advancing good government, strengthening moral instruction, and improving customs—no matters of current government are greater than these. Please weigh the methods that accord with antiquity and suit the present, and explain them to me. I shall select from them and present them to His Majesty.

Question: There is certainly no room for dispute concerning those generals and chief ministers of the Three Dynasties who possessed both talent and virtue in full measure and whose meritorious achievements were manifest. From the Han and Tang onward, some succeeded and some failed; yet were there not among them outstanding men comparable to those of the Three Dynasties? Let me cite the most prominent for you candidates to assess. Those whom people called venerable elders, whose presence kept both the refined and the common in order, and those inspired by loyalty and righteousness, who conducted themselves with integrity and frugality, excelled in virtue. Where, then, was their talent displayed? Those who combined several abilities in one person and discussed affairs with impassioned conviction, and those whom enemies called the Flying General or people called Iron Mountain, excelled in talent. Where, then, were their meritorious achievements displayed? Those who destroyed the Lü clan and secured the Liu house, responding to crises and bringing affairs to completion, and those who won battles and captured objectives, ‘casting aside what was left and establishing substance’ [?]—their…

title: 弘治二年江西鄉試錄
text:
勲偉矣其德果克稱乎若夫以謹信守
管鑰終不能免夫嗜利之誚頷白首死
邉事卒不能保夫晚節之全恤難勤王
之緩師者或忠勤似諸葛或戰功齊子
儀克伐怨欲之必行者或收復乎京城
或制御乎藩鎮志在恢復乃不如諸葛
之忠慎守法度或有馮道之比若是者
才德勲庸亦皆槩見矣而何每不滿於
君子之所望乎豈春秋之法責備賢者
===
抑瑕瑜不掩後世之公論自定乎以王
者之佐而短於將畧為社稷之臣而窮
於奢欲纂述主德謟諛所為也而繫國
輕重者甘為之盡革弊政勢未可行也
而思濟斯民者獨專之以一身保障江
淮而來食人之謗再决策以安社稷而
有不忠之名或負天下之望也而無救
於帝轅之北狩或為金人所服也而不
能還故物於中原若是者才德勲庸亦
punctuated: 勲偉矣，其德果克稱乎？若夫以謹信守管鑰，終不能免夫嗜利之誚；頷白首死邉事，卒不能保夫晚節之全；恤難勤王之緩師者，或忠勤似諸葛，或戰功齊子儀；克伐怨欲之必行者，或收復乎京城，或制御乎藩鎮；志在恢復，乃不如諸葛之忠；慎守法度，或有馮道之比。若是者，才德勲庸亦皆槩見矣，而何每不滿於君子之所望乎？豈《春秋》之法責備賢者，抑瑕瑜不掩，後世之公論自定乎？以王者之佐而短於將畧，為社稷之臣而窮於奢欲。纂述主德，謟諛所為也，而繫國輕重者甘為之；盡革弊政，勢未可行也，而思濟斯民者獨專之。以一身保障江淮，而來食人之謗；再决策以安社稷，而有不忠之名；或負天下之望也，而無救於帝轅之北狩；或為金人所服也，而不能還故物於中原。若是者，才德勲庸亦
translation_en:
…their achievements were great indeed, but did their virtue truly match them? As for those who guarded the keys to the treasury [?] with care and trustworthiness, yet could not escape the reproach of greed for gain; those who, white-haired [?], died in service on the frontier, yet ultimately could not preserve their integrity in their final years; those who were slow to dispatch troops to relieve calamity and aid the sovereign, some resembling Zhuge Liang in loyal diligence, others equaling Ziyi in military achievement; those who insisted on giving rein to competitiveness, boasting, resentment, and desire, some recovering the capital, others bringing the regional military commands under control; those intent on restoring lost territory, yet falling short of Zhuge Liang’s loyalty; and those scrupulously observing laws and regulations, yet sometimes compared to Feng Dao: in such men, talent, virtue, merit, and achievement are all broadly apparent. Why, then, do they so often fail to fulfill the expectations of the exemplary man? Is it that the principles of the Spring and Autumn Annals demand perfection of the worthy? Or is it that neither flaws nor excellences obscure the other, and the impartial judgment of later generations will settle the matter of itself?

There were those who assisted a true king yet fell short in military strategy, and those who served the altars of soil and grain yet went to extremes in luxury and desire. Compiling accounts of the ruler’s virtues is the work of flatterers, yet men whose actions determined the fortunes of the state willingly undertook it. Completely abolishing corrupt policies was not feasible under the circumstances, yet men intent on aiding the people insisted on undertaking it on their own. One man single-handedly safeguarded the Jiang-Huai region, yet incurred the slander that he ate human flesh; another twice made decisive plans that secured the state, yet acquired a reputation for disloyalty. Some bore the hopes of all under Heaven, yet could do nothing to avert the imperial carriage’s “northern hunt”—the emperor’s captivity in the north. Others commanded the respect of the Jin, yet could not restore the former possessions in the Central Plain. As for such men, their talent, virtue, merit, and achievement likewise …

title: 弘治二年江西鄉試錄
text:
可無愧矣而何每不理於衆人之口乎
豈君子所為衆人不識抑成敗在天或
者執此而論人物乎諸生通經學古將
以致用也使他日出而當此位遇此時
果以何人為法乎請詳陳之毋曰君子
思不出其位
問江右為天下巨藩襟帶江湖控制閩粤
寔東南一都會地也古人所謂地靈人
傑試與諸士子言之昔堯制五服禹蒴
===
五服周改為九服茲在何服而服之同
異可詳言歟舜置十二州禹改為九州
茲屬何州而州之分合可得聞歟秦又
更天下為三十六郡是將何隷漢又分
天下為十三部是將誰領其在唐分十
道此非江南西道歟而分道之意何取
其在元又分十二省此非江西行省歟
而行省之由何謂此皆地理之沿革者
然惟山川靈長故其人物秀發其閒若
punctuated:
可無愧矣，而何每不理於衆人之口乎？豈君子所為衆人不識，抑成敗在天，或者執此而論人物乎？諸生通經學古，將以致用也。使他日出而當此位、遇此時，果以何人為法乎？請詳陳之，毋曰君子思不出其位。

問：江右為天下巨藩，襟帶江湖，控制閩粤，寔東南一都會地也。古人所謂地靈人傑，試與諸士子言之。昔堯制五服，禹蒴五服，周改為九服，茲在何服，而服之同異可詳言歟？舜置十二州，禹改為九州，茲屬何州，而州之分合可得聞歟？秦又更天下為三十六郡，是將何隷？漢又分天下為十三部，是將誰領？其在唐分十道，此非江南西道歟？而分道之意何取？其在元又分十二省，此非江西行省歟？而行省之由何謂？此皆地理之沿革者。然惟山川靈長，故其人物秀發，其閒若
translation_en:
…they could indeed be without shame. Why, then, do they so often fail to receive justice in what people say of them? Is it that ordinary people do not understand what gentlemen do? Or, although success and failure lie with Heaven, do some judge historical figures by these outcomes? You students master the Classics and study antiquity with the intention of putting your learning into practice. If, in future, you enter public service, occupy such positions, and encounter such circumstances, whom would you actually take as your model? Please explain in detail, and do not say, “A gentleman’s thoughts do not go beyond his position.”

Question: Jiangyou is a great bulwark of the realm. Girdled by rivers and lakes, it commands Min and Yue and is indeed a metropolitan center of the southeast. Let us discuss with you candidates what the ancients meant by “a land of spiritual potency and outstanding people.” In antiquity, Yao established the five zones of submission; Yu [reorganized?] the five zones [?]; and the Zhou changed them to nine zones. In which zone did this region lie, and can you explain in detail the similarities and differences between these systems? Shun established twelve provinces, and Yu changed them to nine. To which province did this region belong, and may we hear how those provinces were divided and combined? The Qin then reorganized the realm into thirty-six commanderies: under which did this region fall? The Han further divided the realm into thirteen regions: which administered it? When the Tang divided the realm into ten circuits, was this not Jiangnan West Circuit? What was the rationale for dividing the circuits? When the Yuan further divided it into twelve provinces, was this not the Jiangxi Branch Secretariat? How do you explain the origins of the branch secretariats? These are all matters of historical changes in administrative geography. Yet it is precisely because the spiritual potency of its mountains and rivers endures that outstanding people arise here. Among them are such figures as…

title: 弘治二年江西鄉試錄
text:
盱江之十賢廬陵之四忠一節皆表表
者可歷陳歟潯陽之三隱臨江之二劉
三孔皆錚錚者可兼舉歟下太守之榻
著高風足以動人之傾仰致之何由締
膠漆之盟者雅誼足以起人之敬慕處
之何道此皆人物之秀發者諸生生長
名藩覽山川而悉其沿革之由景仰先
哲考言行而得其人物之實願為我言
之毋隱
punctuated: 盱江之十賢、廬陵之四忠一節，皆表表者，可歷陳歟？潯陽之三隱、臨江之二劉三孔，皆錚錚者，可兼舉歟？下太守之榻，著高風，足以動人之傾仰，致之何由？締膠漆之盟者，雅誼足以起人之敬慕，處之何道？此皆人物之秀發者。諸生生長名藩，覽山川而悉其沿革之由，景仰先哲，考言行而得其人物之實，願為我言之，毋隱。
translation_en:
…the Ten Worthies of Xujiang and the Four Loyal Men and One Man of Integrity of Luling—all were eminent figures. Can you recount them individually? The Three Recluses of Xunyang and the Two Lius and Three Kongs of Linjiang—all were outstanding figures. Can you also name them? The man for whom the prefect lowered his couch displayed a lofty character sufficient to inspire admiration: how did he attain this? Those who formed a bond as firm as glue and lacquer possessed a noble friendship sufficient to inspire respect and admiration: by what principles did they conduct their relationship? These are all examples of outstanding individuals.

You students were born and raised in this renowned province. In surveying its mountains and rivers, you have fully understood the reasons for its historical changes; in revering its earlier worthies and examining their words and deeds, you have come to understand what these men were truly like. I ask you to tell me about these matters, withholding nothing.

title: 弘治二年江西鄉試錄
text:
第壹場
四書
非禮勿視非禮勿聽非禮勿言非禮勿動
江淙
同考試官教諭陳　批〔能以人心爲主立說是破羣疑可取〕
同考試官教諭林　批〔布帛菽粟之文辭氣自別吾當爲子刮目矣〕
同考試官教諭張　批〔不戾本旨〕
考試官教諭高　批〔發明勝私復禮之意最切〕
考試官教諭傅　批〔理明辭達〕
===
隨己之私而皆制之於心則仁在是矣盖視聽
言動莫非心爲之主也或有私焉而能制之則
仁豈外是哉昔夫子因顔淵之問而告之若曰
爲仁之功固在於克復克復之機不外乎一心
彼視司於目聽司於耳所以視聽者心也視聽
而非禮則己私之生於心者有未勝不可謂之
仁矣必自視聽一念將萌者而禁止之勿視勿
punctuated:
第壹場

四書

非禮勿視，非禮勿聽，非禮勿言，非禮勿動。

江淙

同考試官教諭陳，批〔能以人心爲主立說，是破羣疑，可取。〕
同考試官教諭林，批〔布帛菽粟之文，辭氣自別，吾當爲子刮目矣。〕
同考試官教諭張，批〔不戾本旨。〕
考試官教諭高，批〔發明勝私復禮之意最切。〕
考試官教諭傅，批〔理明辭達。〕

隨己之私而皆制之於心，則仁在是矣。盖視聽言動，莫非心爲之主也。或有私焉而能制之，則仁豈外是哉？昔夫子因顔淵之問而告之若曰：「爲仁之功，固在於克復；克復之機，不外乎一心。彼視司於目，聽司於耳，所以視聽者，心也。視聽而非禮，則己私之生於心者有未勝，不可謂之仁矣。必自視聽一念將萌者而禁止之，勿視勿
translation_en:
First Session

Four Books

“Do not look at what is contrary to ritual propriety; do not listen to what is contrary to ritual propriety; do not say what is contrary to ritual propriety; do not do what is contrary to ritual propriety.”

Jiang Cong

Associate Examiner Chen, Instructor, comments: “He can construct his argument with the human mind as its governing principle. This dispels the many doubts and merits acceptance.”
Associate Examiner Lin, Instructor, comments: “This is writing like cloth, silk, beans, and grain—essential to daily life. Its diction and tone are distinctive. I shall have to regard you with new eyes.”
Associate Examiner Zhang, Instructor, comments: “It does not depart from the original purport.”
Examiner Gao, Instructor, comments: “It elucidates most aptly the meaning of overcoming selfishness and returning to ritual propriety.”
Examiner Fu, Instructor, comments: “The reasoning is clear and the expression effective.”

As one’s selfish impulses arise, if one restrains them all within the mind, benevolence lies in this. For seeing, hearing, speaking, and acting are all governed by the mind. If selfishness should enter into them and one can restrain it, how could benevolence lie outside this? Formerly, in response to Yan Yuan’s question, the Master instructed him, as if saying: “The work of practicing benevolence assuredly lies in overcoming the self and returning to ritual propriety; the key to overcoming and returning lies nowhere beyond the mind alone. Seeing is the office of the eyes, and hearing the office of the ears, but that by which one sees and hears is the mind. If one sees or hears what is contrary to ritual propriety, then some selfishness arising within the mind remains unconquered, and this cannot be called benevolence. One must check and forbid it at the very point when a thought of seeing or hearing is about to sprout: do not look, do not…”

title: 弘治二年江西鄉試錄
text:
聽可也言出諸口動形諸身所以言動者心也
言動而非禮則己私之發於心者有未去而不
可謂之仁矣必自言動一念將發者而禁止之
勿言勿動可也是則非禮勿視聽則視聽之私
於此勝非禮勿言動則言動之私於此勝私勝
則動容周旋無不中禮而日用之間莫非天理
之流行矣克己復禮之目何以加於此哉大抵
聖賢之學心學也而四勿乃其傳授心法切要
之言夫子獨以告顏子者豈非以其至明能察
吾心理欲之機至健能致吾心勝私之決者乎
與舜之告禹人心惟危道心惟微同一意也厥
後曾子子思皆以慎獨為言益可見道學之傳
有自來矣
===
博學之審問之慎思之明辨之篤行之有
弗學學之弗能弗措也有弗問問之弗知
弗措也有弗思思之弗得弗措也有弗辨
辨之弗明弗措也有弗行行之弗篤弗措
也人一能之己百之人十能之己千之
punctuated:
聽可也。言出諸口，動形諸身，所以言動者，心也。言動而非禮，則己私之發於心者有未去，而不可謂之仁矣。必自言動一念將發者而禁止之，勿言勿動可也。是則非禮勿視聽，則視聽之私於此勝；非禮勿言動，則言動之私於此勝。私勝，則動容周旋無不中禮，而日用之間莫非天理之流行矣。克己復禮之目，何以加於此哉？大抵聖賢之學，心學也，而四勿乃其傳授心法切要之言。夫子獨以告顏子者，豈非以其至明能察吾心理欲之機，至健能致吾心勝私之決者乎？與舜之告禹「人心惟危，道心惟微」同一意也。厥後曾子、子思皆以慎獨為言，益可見道學之傳有自來矣。

博學之，審問之，慎思之，明辨之，篤行之。有弗學，學之弗能，弗措也；有弗問，問之弗知，弗措也；有弗思，思之弗得，弗措也；有弗辨，辨之弗明，弗措也；有弗行，行之弗篤，弗措也。人一能之，己百之；人十能之，己千之。
translation_en:
…not listen: this is what one should do. Speech issues from the mouth, and action takes form in the body, but what enables speech and action is the mind. If speech and action violate ritual propriety, selfish impulses arising in the mind have not yet been eliminated, and this cannot be called benevolence. One must restrain them just as a thought of speaking or acting is about to emerge: one must neither speak nor act upon it. Thus, by neither looking nor listening when it is contrary to ritual propriety, one overcomes selfishness in looking and listening; by neither speaking nor acting when it is contrary to ritual propriety, one overcomes selfishness in speaking and acting. Once selfishness is overcome, every movement, expression, and turn of the body accords with ritual propriety, and everything in daily life becomes the flowing operation of Heavenly principle. What further particulars could be added to these for overcoming the self and returning to ritual propriety? Broadly speaking, the learning of sages and worthies is learning of the mind, and the four prohibitions are the essential words through which they transmit their method of cultivating the mind. Was it not because Master Yan possessed the utmost clarity to discern the incipient distinction between principle and desire within the mind, and the utmost strength to carry through the mind’s resolve to overcome selfishness, that Confucius imparted these words to him alone? Their meaning is identical to Shun’s words to Yu: “The human mind is precarious; the mind of the Way is subtle.” Later, Zengzi and Zisi both spoke of vigilance when alone, making it still clearer that the transmission of the learning of the Way has a longstanding source.

Study broadly, inquire closely, reflect carefully, distinguish clearly, and practice earnestly. If there is anything you have not studied, once you study it, do not set it aside until you have mastered it. If there is anything you have not asked about, once you inquire into it, do not set it aside until you understand it. If there is anything you have not reflected upon, once you reflect upon it, do not set it aside until you have grasped it. If there is anything you have not distinguished, once you examine its distinctions, do not set it aside until they are clear. If there is anything you have not practiced, once you practice it, do not set it aside until your practice is earnest and steadfast. What others can accomplish with one effort, accomplish yourself with a hundred; what others can accomplish with ten efforts, accomplish yourself with a thousand.

title: 弘治二年江西鄉試錄
text:
汪俊
同考試官教諭廖　批〔以知仁勇立意最是〕
同考試官教諭丘　批〔融會傳註成文當是作者〕
同考試官教諭鄭　批〔辭不泛而理不雜〕
考試官教諭高　批〔得旨〕
考試官教諭傅　批〔文足以達理〕
中庸論誠之之事一知仁勇而已盖學問思辨
為知篤行為仁而困知勉行者勇也三者兼盡焉
誠之之功執有要於此哉且夫誠者固本於自
===
然而誠之者必由乎學問學焉而傳則有以備
事物之理故能參伍之以得所疑而有問問焉
而審則有以盡師友之情故能反復之以發其端
而可思思之容可以不謹乎思之謹則精而不
雜故能有所自得而可以施其辨辨之容可以
不明乎辨之明則斷而不差故能無所疑惑而
可以見於行行之篤必身體力行而不事乎虛
文躬行必得而不尚乎徒説此學問思辨所以
擇善而為知學而知也篤行所以固執而為仁
punctuated:
汪俊
同考試官教諭廖批〔以知仁勇立意最是〕。
同考試官教諭丘批〔融會傳註成文，當是作者〕。
同考試官教諭鄭批〔辭不泛而理不雜〕。
考試官教諭高批〔得旨〕。
考試官教諭傅批〔文足以達理〕。
中庸論誠之之事，一知仁勇而已。盖學問思辨為知，篤行為仁，而困知勉行者勇也。三者兼盡焉，誠之之功，執有要於此哉？且夫誠者固本於自然，而誠之者必由乎學問。學焉而傳，則有以備事物之理，故能參伍之以得所疑而有問。問焉而審，則有以盡師友之情，故能反復之以發其端而可思。思之容可以不謹乎？思之謹則精而不雜，故能有所自得而可以施其辨。辨之容可以不明乎？辨之明則斷而不差，故能無所疑惑而可以見於行。行之篤，必身體力行而不事乎虛文，躬行必得而不尚乎徒説。此學問思辨所以擇善而為知，學而知也；篤行所以固執而為仁
translation_en:
Wang Jun

Associate Examiner Liao, Instructor, comments: 〔Making wisdom, benevolence, and courage the central idea is most apt.〕
Associate Examiner Qiu, Instructor, comments: 〔He integrates the commentarial tradition into a coherent composition; he surely is an accomplished writer.〕
Associate Examiner Zheng, Instructor, comments: 〔The language is not diffuse, and the reasoning is not confused.〕
Examiner Gao, Instructor, comments: 〔He grasps the essential meaning.〕
Examiner Fu, Instructor, comments: 〔The writing adequately conveys the principles.〕

The Doctrine of the Mean discusses the work of making oneself sincere: it comes down to wisdom, benevolence, and courage alone. Learning, questioning, reflection, and discrimination constitute wisdom; earnest practice constitutes benevolence; and gaining knowledge through difficulty and exerting oneself in practice constitute courage. When all three are fully realized together, what could be more essential to the work of making oneself sincere than this [?]?

Sincerity itself is indeed rooted in what is naturally so, but making oneself sincere must proceed through learning and questioning. When one learns and transmits what one has learned [?], one has the means to encompass the principles of affairs and things. Thus one can compare and cross-check them, discover points of doubt, and raise questions. When one's questioning is searching, one can fully elicit what teachers and friends have to impart. Thus one can go over it repeatedly, uncover its beginnings, and have material for reflection. How could reflection fail to be careful? Careful reflection is precise and free from confusion; thus one can attain understanding for oneself and bring discrimination to bear upon it. How could discrimination fail to be clear? Clear discrimination is decisive and free from error; thus one can be without doubts or perplexity and manifest one's understanding in practice.

Earnest practice requires personally embodying and vigorously carrying out what one has learned, without occupying oneself with empty forms; it requires attaining it through one's own conduct, without valuing mere talk. This is how learning, questioning, reflection, and discrimination enable one to choose the good and constitute wisdom: this is knowing through learning. Earnest practice enables one to hold firmly to the good and constitutes benevolence …

title: 弘治二年江西鄉試錄
text:
利而行也然知仁固所以知而體之矣使非勇
以強之抑何以至於成耶故有弗學學則已
而學之弗能問之弗知亦弗措也有弗思思
則已而思之弗得辨之弗明亦弗置也然學問有
所得者而行之不篤固不可半途而廢思辨有
所得者而為之不力亦不可中道而止彼或以
一而能也我則倍之以百而必造其極焉彼或
以十而能也我則倍之以千而務要其成焉此
困而知勉而行者勇之事也誠之之功本乎知
===
仁勇如此豈不足以明善而誠其身哉抑考中
庸二十章子思引夫子荅哀公問政之言以繼
大舜文武周公之後正以明列聖相傳之一致
也使哀公果能因夫子之言而致此誠之之功
則由賢而聖自人而天如上文所謂達道達德
九經之屬沛然行之而無難矣夫何身之不脩
而政之不舉哉惜乎哀公聞其言而不能行之
也噫
王者之民皡皡如也
punctuated:
利而行也。然知仁固所以知而體之矣，使非勇以強之，抑何以至於成耶？故有弗學，學則已，而學之弗能、問之弗知，亦弗措也；有弗思，思則已，而思之弗得、辨之弗明，亦弗置也。然學問有所得者，而行之不篤，固不可半途而廢；思辨有所得者，而為之不力，亦不可中道而止。彼或以一而能也，我則倍之以百，而必造其極焉；彼或以十而能也，我則倍之以千，而務要其成焉。此困而知、勉而行者，勇之事也。誠之之功，本乎知仁勇如此，豈不足以明善而誠其身哉？抑考《中庸》二十章，子思引夫子荅哀公問政之言，以繼大舜、文武、周公之後，正以明列聖相傳之一致也。使哀公果能因夫子之言而致此誠之之功，則由賢而聖，自人而天，如上文所謂達道、達德、九經之屬，沛然行之而無難矣。夫何身之不脩而政之不舉哉？惜乎哀公聞其言而不能行之也！噫！

王者之民皡皡如也。
translation_en:
…acting because one recognizes its benefit. Yet although wisdom and benevolence enable one to understand and embody it, without courage to strengthen them, how could one bring the undertaking to completion? Thus there may be no studying; if one studies, one stops [?]. Yet if study has not brought mastery, or inquiry has not brought understanding, one still does not set the task aside. There may be no reflection; if one reflects, one stops [?]. Yet if reflection has yielded no insight, or discrimination has brought no clarity, one still does not abandon the task. Even when study and inquiry have yielded some understanding, if one’s practice is not steadfast, one must certainly not give up halfway. Even when reflection and discrimination have yielded some insight, if one’s efforts to put it into practice are insufficient, one must not stop midway. If others succeed with one effort, I multiply my efforts a hundredfold, determined to reach the utmost attainment. If others succeed with ten efforts, I multiply mine a thousandfold, intent on bringing the undertaking to completion. Coming to know through difficulty and acting through strenuous effort: these are the work of courage. The effort to make oneself sincere rests upon wisdom, benevolence, and courage in this way. Is this not sufficient to understand goodness and make oneself sincere?

Now, examining chapter twenty of the Doctrine of the Mean, we find that Zisi quotes the Master’s reply to Duke Ai’s question about government after his accounts of the great Shun, Kings Wen and Wu, and the Duke of Zhou, precisely to reveal the unity of what the successive sages transmitted. Had Duke Ai truly followed the Master’s words and fully accomplished this work of making himself sincere, he would have advanced from worthiness to sagehood, and from the human to the heavenly. Such things as the universally applicable Way, the universally applicable virtues, and the nine guiding principles mentioned above would then have been put into practice abundantly and without difficulty. How could his person have remained uncultivated or his government have failed to function? Alas, Duke Ai heard these words but could not put them into practice! Ah!

The people of a true king are expansive and at ease.

title: 弘治二年江西鄉試錄
text:
呂世忠
同考試官訓導陳　批〔形容廣大自得之意殆盡其浩蕩〕
王化之深者與
同考試官學正洪　批〔發揮王道如天斯民不識不知之〕
妙甚得旨意可取
考試官教諭高　批〔文理俱到可嘉〕
考試官教諭傅　批〔理明詞暢允宜錄出〕
論盛世之民安自然之化甚矣王化感人之深
也彼其化而忘其化非盛世之民其能然乎且
===
王者之民果何以見其皡皡如耶蓋王者有聖
人之德居天子之位生殺順民情之好惡而善
政之涵養也深輔翼因民性之自然而善教之
甄陶也久是以民之出作入息者惟知衣而桑
麻食而穀粟怡然於自生自育之天其所以衣
所以食初不知誰之使然也民之遷善斂德者
惟知親而父子義而君臣熙然於遵道遵義之
域其所以親所以義初不知誰之所為也際鳳
儀獸舞之治浩浩乎其廣大豈可以言語求之
punctuated:
呂世忠。

同考試官訓導陳批〔形容廣大自得之意，殆盡其浩蕩〕王化之深者與！

同考試官學正洪批〔發揮王道如天、斯民不識不知之〕妙，甚得旨意，可取。

考試官教諭高批〔文理俱到，可嘉。〕

考試官教諭傅批〔理明詞暢，允宜錄出。〕

論盛世之民安自然之化，甚矣，王化感人之深也！彼其化而忘其化，非盛世之民，其能然乎？且王者之民果何以見其皡皡如耶？蓋王者有聖人之德，居天子之位，生殺順民情之好惡，而善政之涵養也深；輔翼因民性之自然，而善教之甄陶也久。是以民之出作入息者，惟知衣而桑麻，食而穀粟，怡然於自生自育之天；其所以衣、所以食，初不知誰之使然也。民之遷善斂德者，惟知親而父子，義而君臣，熙然於遵道遵義之域；其所以親、所以義，初不知誰之所為也。際鳳儀獸舞之治，浩浩乎其廣大，豈可以言語求之
translation_en:
Lü Shizhong.

Associate Examiner Chen, Assistant Instructor, comments: “His portrayal of expansiveness and contentment almost exhausts their vast scope. How profound is the transforming influence of a true king!”

Associate Examiner Hong, Instructor, comments: “He develops the subtle meaning of the kingly Way being like Heaven, with the people unaware and unknowing. He captures the intended meaning very well; this merits selection.”

Examiner Gao, Instructor, comments: “Both literary composition and reasoning are fully accomplished. Commendable.”

Examiner Fu, Instructor, comments: “The reasoning is clear and the language fluent. It certainly deserves to be transcribed for inclusion.”

I maintain that the people of a flourishing age rest content in a transformation that comes naturally. How profoundly the transforming influence of a true king moves people! They are transformed yet forget that transformation: could anyone but the people of a flourishing age be like this? And how, indeed, can we see that the people of a true king are so expansive and at ease? A true king possesses the virtue of a sage and occupies the position of the Son of Heaven. In granting life or imposing death, he accords with the likes and dislikes of the people's hearts, and the nurturing influence of his good government is profound. In assisting and guiding them, he follows what is natural to their innate dispositions, and the molding influence of his good instruction is enduring. Thus, as the people go out to work and return to rest, they know only to cultivate mulberry and hemp for clothing, and grain and millet for food. They dwell happily beneath a Heaven where they live and grow of themselves; they have no idea who has enabled them to be clothed and fed. As the people advance toward goodness and gather virtue within themselves, they know only affection between father and son and righteousness between ruler and minister. They dwell joyfully in a realm of following the Way and righteousness; they have no idea who has brought about their affection and righteousness. Living under a government in which phoenixes appear in stately array and beasts dance, they are boundlessly expansive. How could words encompass this …

title: 弘治二年江西鄉試錄
text:
哉鳶飛魚躍之化休休乎其自得又豈可以
形容盡之哉此王道之所以為大也與大抵王
者至公無我故政無迹而德不顯功無形而民
罔知豈若伯者違道干譽以忌之淺近致民之
驩虞者可同日語耶孟軻氏立王伯之論嚴理
欲之分為世道慮至深遠矣有志於堯舜君民
者宜於此盡心焉
易
文明以健中正而應君子正也唯君子為
能通天下之志
===
賴汶
同考試官訓導陳　批〔易經此題本平易正大場中作者究理不精多不知通天下之志乃爲利也作多失旨得旨〕
〔之中此作唯純故用録出〕
同考試官學正洪　批〔發明君子之貞所以爲利深合同人之旨〕
考試官教諭高　批〔講貫詳明是見經學宜表而出之〕
punctuated:
哉！鳶飛魚躍之化，休休乎其自得，又豈可以形容盡之哉！此王道之所以為大也與！大抵王者至公無我，故政無迹而德不顯，功無形而民罔知。豈若伯者違道干譽，以忌之淺近致民之驩虞者，可同日語耶？孟軻氏立王伯之論，嚴理欲之分，為世道慮至深遠矣。有志於堯舜君民者，宜於此盡心焉。
易
文明以健，中正而應，君子正也。唯君子為能通天下之志。
賴汶
同考試官訓導陳批〔易經此題本平易正大，場中作者究理不精，多不知通天下之志乃爲利也，作多失旨。得旨〕〔之中，此作唯純，故用録出。〕
同考試官學正洪批〔發明君子之貞所以爲利，深合同人之旨。〕
考試官教諭高批〔講貫詳明，是見經學，宜表而出之。〕
translation_en:
…indeed! Under a transforming influence in which kites soar and fish leap, how freely and contentedly all find their fulfillment! How could any description exhaust it? This is what makes the kingly Way great! In general, the true king is utterly impartial and without selfishness. Thus his governance leaves no trace, his virtue makes no display, his achievements have no visible form, and the people are unaware of them. Could he possibly be spoken of in the same breath as a hegemon who departs from the Way to seek acclaim, winning the people’s delight through petty and shortsighted jealousy [?]? Meng Ke established the distinction between kingship and hegemony and strictly distinguished principle from selfish desire: his concern for the moral order of the world was profoundly far-reaching. Those who aspire to make their ruler like Yao and Shun and their people like the people of those sages should devote their minds fully to this.
Book of Changes
“Cultured and enlightened, yet strong; central and correct, and meeting with response: this is the correctness of the gentleman. Only the gentleman can bring into communion the aspirations of all under Heaven.”
Lai Wen
Associate Examiner Chen, Assistant Instructor, comments: 〔This topic from the Book of Changes is intrinsically straightforward, upright, and broad in scope. Candidates in the examination hall did not investigate its principles precisely; many failed to understand that bringing into communion the aspirations of all under Heaven is what constitutes ‘benefit.’ Their compositions mostly missed the purport. Among those that grasped〕〔it, this composition alone was pure in its understanding; therefore it was selected for inclusion.〕
Associate Examiner Hong, Instructor, comments: 〔It elucidates why the gentleman’s constancy constitutes ‘benefit,’ closely according with the meaning of the hexagram Fellowship with Others.〕
Examiner Gao, Instructor, comments: 〔Its exposition is thorough, detailed, and clear. It demonstrates learning in the Classics and deserves to be singled out for publication.〕

title: 弘治二年江西鄉試錄
text:
考試官教諭傅　批〔詞理精緻可觀〕
彖傳釋同人君子之貞而必言其所以利也盖
同人貴乎君子之正也使非君子其何以通天
下之志而大同也哉彖傳即卦之德體釋而言
之厥有旨矣昔夫子傳同人之彖謂夫同人之
于野亨涉川而利固本於乾行也然又必利於
君子之貞焉盖以卦德言之內離而其德文明
外乾而其德剛健文明則足以察乎物理剛健
則足以勝乎己私是謂君子之正也以卦體言
===
之六二以柔順中正而居下九五以剛健中正
而應之中正則在己無所偏應之則在彼有所
合是亦君子之正焉夫君子惟其正也是以天
下之人雖曰其志不能皆同也而所同者此理
君子為能通之而無彼此之異其與同人于宗
者懸殊矣天下之民雖曰其志不能皆一也而
所同者此道君子有以通之而無爾我之殊其
與同人于郊者迥異矣盖能通天下之志乃為
大同不然則是私情之合而已其何以致亨而
punctuated:
考試官教諭傅　批〔詞理精緻可觀〕

彖傳釋同人君子之貞，而必言其所以利也。盖同人貴乎君子之正也。使非君子，其何以通天下之志而大同也哉？彖傳即卦之德體釋而言之，厥有旨矣。昔夫子傳同人之彖，謂夫同人之于野，亨，涉川而利，固本於乾行也。然又必利於君子之貞焉。盖以卦德言之，內離而其德文明，外乾而其德剛健。文明則足以察乎物理，剛健則足以勝乎己私，是謂君子之正也。以卦體言之，六二以柔順中正而居下，九五以剛健中正而應之。中正則在己無所偏，應之則在彼有所合，是亦君子之正焉。夫君子惟其正也，是以天下之人，雖曰其志不能皆同也，而所同者此理。君子為能通之，而無彼此之異，其與同人于宗者懸殊矣。天下之民，雖曰其志不能皆一也，而所同者此道。君子有以通之，而無爾我之殊，其與同人于郊者迥異矣。盖能通天下之志，乃為大同。不然，則是私情之合而已，其何以致亨而
translation_en:
Examiner Fu, Instructor, comments: 〔The language and reasoning are refined and worthy of attention.〕

In explaining the gentleman’s constancy in Fellowship with Others (Tongren), the Commentary on the Judgments necessarily states why it is beneficial. For fellowship with others prizes the gentleman’s rectitude. Without being a gentleman, how could one bring the aspirations of all under Heaven into communion and achieve universal fellowship? The Commentary on the Judgments explains this through the hexagram’s virtues and structure, and its meaning is profound.

When the Master composed his commentary on the judgment of Fellowship with Others, he said that fellowship with others in the open country brings success, and that crossing the river is beneficial: these certainly rest upon the activity of Qian. Yet benefit must also lie in the gentleman’s constancy. Speaking of the hexagram’s virtues, its inner trigram is Li, whose virtue is cultured illumination; its outer trigram is Qian, whose virtue is strength and vigor. Cultured illumination suffices to discern the principles of things, while strength and vigor suffice to overcome one’s selfishness. This is what is meant by the gentleman’s rectitude.

Speaking of the hexagram’s structure, the six in the second place occupies the lower position with yielding compliance, centrality, and correctness; the nine in the fifth place responds to it with strength and vigor, centrality, and correctness. Centrality and correctness mean that there is no partiality within oneself; correspondence means that there is accord with the other. This, too, is the gentleman’s rectitude.

Precisely because the gentleman is upright, although the aspirations of the people under Heaven cannot all be the same, what they share is this principle. The gentleman alone can bring them into communion, removing distinctions between one side and another. How far this differs from fellowship with others within one’s clan! Although the aspirations of the people under Heaven cannot all be one, what they share is this Way. The gentleman has the means to bring them into communion, removing distinctions between you and me. How greatly this differs from fellowship with others in the outskirts!

title: 弘治二年江西鄉試錄
text:
利涉哉大抵天下之事非一人之心思智力所
獨能不可不與人同也然求其所以同者亦惟
心焉耳不同其心而求夫形跡之相似則始交
而終離朝合而暮去矣其何以成天下之事哉
經則曰利君子之貞傳則曰通天下之志其以
此夫
聖人立象以盡意設卦以盡情僞繫辭焉
以盡其言變而通之以盡利鼓之舞之以
盡神
同考試官訓導陳　批〔利場之設欲明經取士爲其能經無一定之見能用經中語發明精切如此篇者殆不多見取冠本經何忝〕
〔易乃理學之宗明之本難似此題卜卦下非偏倖而作者尚能〕
同考試官學正洪　批〔發揮聖人作易之源易用之妙非深於易者不能〕
考試官教諭高　批〔理明詞暢宜錄〕
考試官教諭傅　批〔易理難明此作得旨可取〕
punctuated:
利涉哉？大抵天下之事，非一人之心思智力所獨能，不可不與人同也。然求其所以同者，亦惟心焉耳。不同其心，而求夫形跡之相似，則始交而終離，朝合而暮去矣，其何以成天下之事哉？經則曰：「利君子之貞。」傳則曰：「通天下之志。」其以此夫！
聖人立象以盡意，設卦以盡情僞，繫辭焉以盡其言，變而通之以盡利，鼓之舞之以盡神。
同考試官訓導陳，批〔利場之設，欲明經取士，爲其能經無一定之見，能用經中語發明精切如此篇者，殆不多見。取冠本經，何忝？〕
〔易乃理學之宗，明之本難。似此題卜卦下，非偏倖，而作者尚能〕
同考試官學正洪，批〔發揮聖人作易之源、易用之妙，非深於易者不能。〕
考試官教諭高，批〔理明詞暢，宜錄。〕
考試官教諭傅，批〔易理難明，此作得旨，可取。〕
translation_en:
…and make it advantageous to cross? Generally, the affairs of the world cannot be accomplished solely through one person's thought, wisdom, and strength: one must join with others. Yet the basis of such unity lies only in the heart. If people seek similarity in outward conduct without uniting their hearts, they will begin in fellowship but end in separation, joining in the morning and departing by evening. How could they accomplish the affairs of the world? The Classic says, “It is advantageous for the gentleman to remain steadfast.” The Commentary says, “To comprehend the aspirations of all under Heaven.” Surely this is the reason!
The sages established images to express their meaning fully, arranged the hexagrams to express fully the true and the false, and appended statements to express their words fully. They transformed things and enabled them to proceed, thereby realizing benefit to the fullest; they roused and inspired people, thereby fully manifesting their spiritual efficacy.
Associate Examiner Chen, Assistant Instructor, comments: 〔The examination arena [?] was established to select men who understand the Classics. As for their ability to interpret the Classics without fixed views [?], one seldom sees anyone use the words of a Classic to elucidate its meaning as precisely and incisively as this essay does. What cause for embarrassment could there be in ranking it first among the essays on this Classic?〕
〔The Book of Changes is the fountainhead of the learning of principle, and understanding it is inherently difficult. With a topic like this, “under divination and the hexagrams, not partial good fortune” [?], the author nevertheless manages to…〕
Associate Examiner Hong, Instructor, comments: 〔It expounds the origins of the sages' composition of the Book of Changes and the subtlety of its application. Only someone deeply versed in the Changes could accomplish this.〕
Examiner Gao, Instructor, comments: 〔The principles are clear and the language flows smoothly. It deserves to be selected.〕
Examiner Fu, Instructor, comments: 〔The principles of the Changes are difficult to understand. This essay grasps their purport and merits selection.〕

title: 弘治二年江西鄉試錄
text:
聖人之作易有以盡其藴而又妙於事焉盖聖
人之藴非作易無以盡之也而其見之於事又
豈不有以盡其妙哉大傳設爲問辭以嘆聖人
之意有不可得而見於此答之若曰言之所傳
者淺象之所示者深聖人畫一奇以象陽畫一
偶以象陰奇偶之象既立包含變化無有窮盡
聖人之意於是乎盡矣然有象則有卦聖人因
奇偶之象以設三十有二之陽卦即奇偶之畫
以設三十有二之陰卦陰陽之卦既設或愛惡
之相攻或遠近之相取天下之情僞於斯乎盡
矣夫有卦則有辭卦焉繫之以彖辭爻焉繫之
以爻辭彖以言其象爻以言其變則聖人之言
又不於此而盡乎聖人之作易盡其藴也如此
===
若推而見之於事凡有爲也或得失之未定則
因其變而通之使吉凶以明而爲之無不宜焉
凡有行也或憂虞之未決則隨其變而通之使
悔吝以著而行之無不順焉利不盡於變通之
中乎變既通矣將見事之吉者皷之舞之使
punctuated:
聖人之作易，有以盡其藴，而又妙於事焉。盖聖人之藴，非作易無以盡之也，而其見之於事，又豈不有以盡其妙哉？大傳設爲問辭，以嘆聖人之意有不可得而見，於此答之若曰：言之所傳者淺，象之所示者深。聖人畫一奇以象陽，畫一偶以象陰，奇偶之象既立，包含變化，無有窮盡，聖人之意於是乎盡矣。然有象則有卦，聖人因奇偶之象，以設三十有二之陽卦；即奇偶之畫，以設三十有二之陰卦。陰陽之卦既設，或愛惡之相攻，或遠近之相取，天下之情僞於斯乎盡矣。夫有卦則有辭，卦焉繫之以彖辭，爻焉繫之以爻辭。彖以言其象，爻以言其變，則聖人之言又不於此而盡乎？聖人之作易，盡其藴也如此。
若推而見之於事，凡有爲也，或得失之未定，則因其變而通之，使吉凶以明，而爲之無不宜焉。凡有行也，或憂虞之未決，則隨其變而通之，使悔吝以著，而行之無不順焉。利不盡於變通之中乎？變既通矣，將見事之吉者，皷之舞之，使
translation_en:
In making the Book of Changes, the sages fully expressed what they held within, and also achieved wondrous efficacy in practical affairs. Indeed, without making the Changes, they would have had no means of fully expressing what they held within; and when this was manifested in affairs, how could they fail to realize its wondrous efficacy to the fullest? The Great Commentary poses a question, lamenting that the sages’ intent cannot be apprehended, and here answers it as if to say: what words convey is shallow; what images reveal is deep. The sages drew a single unbroken line to symbolize yang and a pair of broken segments to symbolize yin. Once the images of the odd and the even were established, they encompassed transformations without limit, and thus fully expressed the sages’ intent. Yet where there are images, there are hexagrams. Drawing upon the images of the odd and the even, the sages established thirty-two yang hexagrams; using these same odd and even lines, they established thirty-two yin hexagrams. Once the yin and yang hexagrams were established, whether love and hatred contended with one another or the distant and the near drew one another into association, the genuine and the false throughout the world were fully expressed therein. Now, where there are hexagrams, there are statements. To the hexagrams they appended hexagram judgments, and to the lines they appended line statements. The judgments speak of their images, and the line statements speak of their transformations: are not the sages’ words fully expressed here as well? Such was the way in which the sages, in making the Changes, fully expressed what they held within.
When this is extended and manifested in practical affairs, whenever one undertakes something and gain or loss remains uncertain, one follows its transformations and carries them through, making good and ill fortune clear, so that everything undertaken is appropriate. Whenever one acts and anxieties remain unresolved, one follows its transformations and carries them through, making regret and humiliation evident, so that every action proceeds smoothly. Are not benefits fully realized through transformation and adaptation? 迅者鼓之舞之使之勇於退避脫然以無係而

translation_en:
…them to delight in advancing, eagerly undertaking action, without anyone knowing the subtle workings involved. In affairs that are swift [?], they are stirred and inspired to withdraw courageously, freeing themselves of attachments, without anyone fathoming the workings involved. Is not spiritual efficacy, then, fully expressed in this stirring and inspiring? Thus, before the Changes was composed, the sages’ refined intentions and subtle applications were stored within their own minds; once the Changes was composed, these became manifest in the myriad affairs. The Great Commentary presents questions and answers to instruct people, and its purport is clear. Nevertheless, although the sages’ composition of the Changes left nothing unexpressed, if we investigate what makes it the Changes, it amounts to nothing beyond yin and yang. These are what constitute its images; these are what constitute its hexagrams; these are what its appended statements articulate; and these, too, are what enable adaptation to change and stir and inspire the people. Apart from yin and yang, therefore, there is no means of perceiving the Changes. If the Changes could not be perceived, yin and yang might cease to operate. Hence it is said: “Qian and Kun are the hidden store of the Changes. Once Qian and Kun are arrayed, the Changes is established within them.”

title: 弘治二年江西鄉試錄
text:
同考試官教諭鄭　批〔揭書出題雖易實難作者於精一處講雖明白多昧所以執中之意此作得之〕
考試官教諭高　批〔説出舜授禹所以執中之心可取〕
考試官教諭傳　批〔得旨〕
能擇而守之則中斯執矣盖中之所執不可不
擇而守之也能擇而守則中之執在是矣昔帝
舜於禹而告之曰天下之大治之有道不過一
中而已中之所在不精以察之則雜於形氣之
私可乎故凡一念之發必察其果發於形氣乎
===
發於義理乎真知其發於形氣則敬以摧折之
雖念慮之微無少雜焉灼見其發於義理則敬
以體驗之雖毫釐之際無少差焉如是其精可
也徒察而守之不一則義理之未純正得乎又
必持守之而念念不忘允蹈之而安安不移使
前之摧折者常敬以克之而不使其少有凝滯
前之體驗者常敬以擴之而不使其少有壅閼
如是其一得矣既察之而理欲判然又守之而
道心常在則形諸動靜云為之際以至禮樂刑
punctuated:
同考試官教諭鄭　批〔揭書出題，雖易實難。作者於精一處講雖明白，多昧所以執中之意，此作得之。〕
考試官教諭高　批〔説出舜授禹所以執中之心，可取。〕
考試官教諭傳　批〔得旨。〕
能擇而守之，則中斯執矣。盖中之所執，不可不擇而守之也。能擇而守，則中之執在是矣。昔帝舜於禹而告之曰：「天下之大，治之有道，不過一中而已。中之所在，不精以察之，則雜於形氣之私，可乎？故凡一念之發，必察其果發於形氣乎，發於義理乎。真知其發於形氣，則敬以摧折之，雖念慮之微，無少雜焉；灼見其發於義理，則敬以體驗之，雖毫釐之際，無少差焉。如是其精，可也。徒察而守之不一，則義理之未純正，得乎？又必持守之而念念不忘，允蹈之而安安不移，使前之摧折者，常敬以克之，而不使其少有凝滯；前之體驗者，常敬以擴之，而不使其少有壅閼。如是其一，得矣。既察之而理欲判然，又守之而道心常在，則形諸動靜云為之際，以至禮樂刑
translation_en:
Associate Examiner Zheng, Instructor, comments: 〔Choosing a topic from the Documents may seem easy, but is actually difficult. Although writers explain discrimination and singleness clearly, they often fail to understand how these enable one to hold fast to the mean. This essay grasps that meaning.〕
Examiner Gao, Instructor, comments: 〔It brings out the intention behind Shun’s teaching to Yu on holding fast to the mean. Commendable.〕
Examiner Chuan [?], Instructor, comments: 〔It grasps the essential meaning.〕
If one can distinguish and then hold fast to what one has discerned, the mean will be maintained. For holding fast to the mean necessarily requires discrimination and steadfast adherence. The ability to distinguish and adhere is precisely what holding fast to the mean consists in. In former times, Emperor Shun addressed Yu, saying: “Vast though the realm is, there is a way to govern it, and this amounts to nothing more than the mean. If you do not investigate with discrimination where the mean lies, it will become mixed with the selfish impulses of bodily form and vital energy. Can that be acceptable? Thus, whenever a thought arises, you must examine whether it truly arises from bodily form and vital energy or from moral principle. When you know for certain that it arises from bodily form and vital energy, use reverent attentiveness to subdue it, allowing no admixture of selfishness even in the most subtle thoughts. When you see clearly that it arises from moral principle, use reverent attentiveness to experience and verify it, allowing no deviation even in the slightest particular. Such discrimination is adequate. But if you merely examine and do not maintain singleness in holding fast, moral principle will remain impure and incorrect. Can that suffice? You must also hold fast to it, never forgetting it from one thought to the next, and faithfully put it into practice, remaining settled and unwavering. What you previously subdued, constantly overcome through reverent attentiveness, allowing it not the slightest lingering hold; what you previously experienced and verified, constantly expand through reverent attentiveness, allowing it not the slightest obstruction. In this way, singleness is attained. Once examination has clearly distinguished principle from selfish desire, and steadfast adherence keeps the moral mind ever present, this will find expression in activity and stillness, in speech and action, extending even to rites, music, punishments …

也堯之授舜舜之授禹言有詳畧而精微之理
敬畏之心一也故雖知其功德之盛而猶欲其
戰戰兢兢無敢逸豫而謹之於一念之初也歟

大臣述前聖無逸之休，而臣益相戒無逸之切。盖無逸而猶戒逸者，大臣保治之心也。古之君
translation_en:
…the implementation of meritorious works [?], there will naturally be neither excess nor deficiency, and one will truly be able to hold fast to the mean. Generally speaking, the single word “mean” is the essential principle of the transmission of the mind, while the single word “reverence” is the essential principle of the learning of the sages. In Yao’s transmission to Shun and Shun’s transmission to Yu, the words varied in fullness and brevity, but the subtle principle and the reverent, apprehensive mind were one. Thus, although they knew the greatness of their successors’ achievements and virtue, did they not still wish them to remain trembling and cautious, never daring to indulge in ease or pleasure, and vigilant at the very inception of a thought?

“The men of antiquity still admonished and instructed one another, protected and favored one another, and taught and counseled one another.”
Hu Jiang

Comment by Associate Examiner Liao, Instructor: 〔Among the scripts assigned to this examining room, this one succeeds in grounding its discussion of admonition and instruction, protection and favor, and teaching and counsel in Heaven’s Mandate and the common people. Moreover, it earnestly insists on freedom from idleness, every phrase more pressing than the last. It should be recorded as a model for later students.〕

Comment by Associate Examiner Qiu, Instructor: 〔The chapter “Against Idleness” embraces, above, the subtle mysteries of Heaven’s Mandate and, below, the hardships of the common people. The Duke of Zhou’s intention in recounting what he had heard lies within this.〕

Comment by Associate Examiner Zheng, Instructor: 〔Many candidates in the examination identify the “men of antiquity” as Yao, Shun, Yu, and Tang. This is decidedly not the Duke of Zhou’s original intention in addressing King Cheng. This essay takes the three honored Shang kings and King Wen as its subject, closely matching the passage’s original purport. It should be selected to head the scripts in this examining room.〕

Comment by Examiner Gao, Instructor: 〔The Duke of Zhou admonishing his ruler against idleness appears vividly before our eyes.〕

Comment by Examiner Fu, Instructor: 〔Every sentence admonishes the ruler to remain diligent amid ease. Admirable, admirable!〕

A great minister recounts the excellence of the former sages’ freedom from idleness, while ministers urge one another ever more earnestly against idleness. Indeed, to remain free from idleness and yet still warn against it expresses a great minister’s resolve to preserve good government. The rulers of antiquity…

title: 弘治二年江西鄉試錄
text:
臣如此其保治無窮之心爲何如周公述所聞
以告成王若謂殷之三宗周之文王上焉天命
而嚴恭寅畏徽柔懿恭以致享國之永下焉小
民而祇懼嘉靖懷保惠鮮以成咸和之治德業
之盛如此無逸可知矣其臣猶且相與訓誡之
惟恐其不畏天命而耽樂之從焉告戒之惟恐
其不知民依而遊田之盤焉豈特訓告而已又
必相與維持而調護之保養而將順之使天命
延長而君身之獲福小民無怨而君德之迪哲
===
也又豈特保惠而已又必相與左右規正之賛
襄成就之使天命之寅畏者益寅畏而德之愈
盛也小民之咸和者益咸和而業之愈盛也周
公述此以告成王何其切哉嘗考周召之於成
王所陳在敬所戒在逸蓋敬則不逸逸則不敬
無逸之效而曆年之延長享國之壽永係焉召
公以敬陳於前周公以無逸戒於後不如是不
足爲周召
詩
punctuated:
臣如此，其保治無窮之心爲何如？周公述所聞以告成王，若謂殷之三宗、周之文王，上焉天命，而嚴恭寅畏、徽柔懿恭，以致享國之永；下焉小民，而祇懼嘉靖、懷保惠鮮，以成咸和之治。德業之盛如此，無逸可知矣。其臣猶且相與訓誡之，惟恐其不畏天命而耽樂之從焉；告戒之，惟恐其不知民依而遊田之盤焉。豈特訓告而已？又必相與維持而調護之，保養而將順之，使天命延長而君身之獲福，小民無怨而君德之迪哲也。又豈特保惠而已？又必相與左右規正之，賛襄成就之，使天命之寅畏者益寅畏而德之愈盛也，小民之咸和者益咸和而業之愈盛也。周公述此以告成王，何其切哉！嘗考周召之於成王，所陳在敬，所戒在逸。蓋敬則不逸，逸則不敬。無逸之效，而曆年之延長、享國之壽永係焉。召公以敬陳於前，周公以無逸戒於後，不如是不足爲周召。

詩
translation_en:
…ministers acted thus: how boundless was their resolve to preserve good government! The Duke of Zhou recounted what he had heard to instruct King Cheng, as though saying: the three ancestral kings of Yin and King Wen of Zhou, in their relation to Heaven’s Mandate above, were solemnly reverent and respectfully apprehensive, admirably gentle and nobly deferential, thereby securing long reigns. In their relation to the common people below, they were reverently cautious, brought about well-being and peace, cherished and protected the people, and bestowed kindness upon those in distress, thereby achieving government under which all lived in harmony. Such was the abundance of their virtue and accomplishments that their freedom from idleness is evident.

Yet their ministers still joined together to admonish them, fearing only that they might cease to stand in awe of Heaven’s Mandate and give themselves over to pleasure. They warned them, fearing only that they might fail to understand what the people depended upon and indulge excessively in excursions and hunting. Was it merely a matter of admonishing them? They also had to join together to sustain and safeguard them, nurture them and assist them in pursuing what was right, so that Heaven’s Mandate would endure and the ruler himself receive blessings, while the common people would have no grievances and the ruler’s virtue would advance toward wisdom.

Nor was it merely a matter of protecting and benefiting them. They also had to join together to attend upon and correct them, assist them and bring their endeavors to completion, so that their reverent apprehension of Heaven’s Mandate would deepen and their virtue flourish still more, and the common people’s universal harmony would increase and their achievements flourish still more. How earnest was the Duke of Zhou in recounting these things to instruct King Cheng!

I have examined how the dukes of Zhou and Shao dealt with King Cheng: what they set before him centered on reverence, and what they warned him against was idleness. For where there is reverence there is no idleness; where there is idleness there is no reverence. The prolongation of his years and the enduring length of his reign depended upon the effects of freedom from idleness. The Duke of Shao first set reverence before him; the Duke of Zhou afterward admonished him against idleness. Had they not acted thus, they would not have been worthy of being the dukes of Zhou and Shao.

Book of Odes

translation_en:
There are those to rely on and those to assist, those with filial devotion and those with virtue, to guide and to support. The gracious and joyous gentleman is the model for the four quarters. Dignified and lofty, like a jade tablet and a jade half-tablet, he has an excellent reputation and excellent standing. The gracious and joyous gentleman is the guiding cord for the four quarters. The phoenixes fly, their wings rustling; they gather and alight here. In abundant array, the king has many worthy officers: it is the gentleman who employs them, and they love the Son of Heaven.

Jiang Cong.

Associate Examiner Chen, Instructor, comments: “This brings out the Duke of Shao’s loyalty in offering admonition, a loyalty that overflows the words. Surely an accomplished writer.”

Associate Examiner Lin, Instructor, comments: “The essays on the Book of Poetry assigned to this examining section number in the thousands. If they are not tedious and overelaborate, they are stale and confused, making them tiresome to read. Late in the process I obtained this paper. Its writing is vigorous and robust, its diction and tone expansive as spring. The intent of the Duke of Shao’s admonition at that time seems palpably present [?], giving my feelings a welcome release. Who could say it is inappropriate to promote it to the foremost rank?”

Associate Examiner Zhang, Instructor, comments: “An essay interpreting the Book of Poetry should be gentle, generous, balanced, and harmonious. This composition is fluent and its reasoning clear, neither forced nor strained. Its author has a deep understanding of the Book of Poetry. It is therefore included to serve as a model for later students.”

Examiner Gao, Instructor, comments: “Smooth and well ordered; worthy of inclusion.”

Examiner Fu, Instructor, comments: “It attains the proper form for composing a policy exposition [?].”

In offering admonition, the great minister first speaks of the benefit that worthy men bring by assisting their ruler, and then uses poetic imagery to evoke their hearts’ loyalty to him. Indeed, great is the benefit worthy men bring to a state! If the ruler can truly employ them, how could they fail, every one of them, to cherish loyal and loving hearts and help bring his virtue to completion…

title: 弘治二年江西鄉試錄
text:

以致之之由意謂致福固在於脩德脩德莫先
於用賢彼賢才有可爲依者有可爲輔者莫非
倚重之老成有孝於親者有得於已者無非慈
祥之善類以之引導於前而啓沃是資以之輔
相於側而彌縫是賴爾豈弟君子則德無不脩
矣四方豈不儀刑於爾乎然君德之脩抑何以
見之耶其體貌則顒顒卬卬而極其尊嚴其德
行則如圭如璋而極其純潔播而爲令聞也德
===
音秩秩之甚善著而爲令望也威儀抑抑之可
覿爾豈弟君子則德無不全矣四方豈不繫屬
於爾乎人君得賢自輔如此然賢者豈無忠君
之心耶故托興之曰鳳凰于飛則翽翽其羽而
亦集爰止矣吾王之賢才藹藹然充盛一馮翼
之傳濟濟乎衆多一孝德之輩命之以引導彼
則維王所命而興媚茲一人之誠孰不欲君德
之進於光明乎使之以輔翼彼則維王所使而
懷左右厥辟之念孰不欲君德之全其懿美乎
punctuated: 業哉！昔召公戒成王，旣歆之以福祿之盛，復告以致之之由。意謂致福固在於脩德，脩德莫先於用賢。彼賢才，有可爲依者，有可爲輔者，莫非倚重之老成；有孝於親者，有得於已者，無非慈祥之善類。以之引導於前，而啓沃是資；以之輔相於側，而彌縫是賴。爾豈弟君子，則德無不脩矣，四方豈不儀刑於爾乎？然君德之脩，抑何以見之耶？其體貌則顒顒卬卬，而極其尊嚴；其德行則如圭如璋，而極其純潔。播而爲令聞也，德音秩秩之甚善；著而爲令望也，威儀抑抑之可覩。爾豈弟君子，則德無不全矣，四方豈不繫屬於爾乎？人君得賢自輔如此，然賢者豈無忠君之心耶？故托興之曰：「鳳凰于飛，則翽翽其羽，而亦集爰止矣。」吾王之賢才，藹藹然充盛，一馮翼之傳；濟濟乎衆多，一孝德之輩。命之以引導，彼則維王所命，而興媚茲一人之誠，孰不欲君德之進於光明乎？使之以輔翼，彼則維王所使，而懷左右厥辟之念，孰不欲君德之全其懿美乎？
translation_en:
…and achievements!

In former times, when the Duke of Shao admonished King Cheng, he first inspired him with the prospect of abundant blessings and emoluments, then explained how these could be attained. His meaning was that obtaining blessings certainly depended on cultivating virtue, and that in cultivating virtue nothing took precedence over employing worthy men. Among these worthy men were those upon whom the ruler could depend and those who could assist him—all mature and experienced men worthy of his trust. There were those filial toward their parents and those who had attained virtue within themselves—all kindly and benevolent men. Placed before him as guides, they would provide instruction that opened and nourished his mind; placed beside him as assistants, they could be relied upon to remedy deficiencies. You, the gracious and amiable lord, would thus leave no aspect of virtue uncultivated. Would not the people of the four quarters take you as their model?

But how would the cultivation of the ruler’s virtue become apparent? His bearing would be stately and lofty, supremely dignified; his virtuous conduct would be like the gui tablet and zhang scepter of jade, supremely pure. As it spread abroad and became a fine reputation, the harmonious report of his virtue would be most excellent; as it became manifest and won him high esteem, his measured and dignified deportment would be visible to all. You, the gracious and amiable lord, would thus possess virtue complete in every respect. Would not the people of the four quarters attach themselves to you?

Such is the benefit when a ruler obtains worthy men to assist him. Yet could those worthy men lack hearts loyal to their ruler? Hence the admonition evokes its meaning through an image: “The phoenixes fly, their wings rustling, and together they alight and settle.” Our king’s worthy men flourish in abundance, a company of supporters [?]; numerous and impressive, they are a company of men of filial virtue. When commanded to guide him, they obey only the king’s command and sincerely cherish this One Man. Who among them would not wish the ruler’s virtue to advance toward brilliance? When charged with assisting him, they undertake only the king’s assignments and cherish the intention of supporting their sovereign on either side. Who among them would not wish the ruler’s virtue to attain its full excellence and beauty?

translation_en:
…When a ruler employs worthy men in this way to help perfect his virtue and achievements, could the arrival of blessings and emoluments be difficult [?]? Nevertheless, it was by widely seeking wise men that Cheng Tang was able to be magnanimous and benevolent and establish the foundations of his dynasty; it was by broadly recruiting outstanding men that Gaozong avoided improper or excessive rewards and revitalized the work of dynastic restoration. From antiquity, none who founded a dynasty or preserved its achievements established good government without relying on worthy men. Duke Kang considered that King Cheng, still young and inexperienced and presiding over a time of full prosperity, might fail to give this matter due attention. Thus, while accompanying him on his excursion to the winding hill, he offered words of admonition and urged this course upon him. His sole purpose was to have the king employ worthy men and cultivate virtue as the foundation for bringing blessings. Ah! A man such as Duke Kang may indeed be called one who serves his ruler according to the Way!
“Wen and Wu received the Mandate; the Duke of Shao was their supporting pillar. Do not say, ‘I am but a young man’; emulate the Duke of Shao.”

王者之命大臣必推其世功而勉以繼之也蓋
前人之功正後人之所當繼也今王者命大臣
而欲其克纘世功如此其勉以忠孝之意何至
哉昔宣王命召穆公平淮南之夷詩人美之至
此則述王命之詞意謂誕膺天命以撫方夏文
王之受命也保右命爾燮伐大商非武王之受
命乎昔我文武受命之日非無佐命元勳也惟
===
爾祖康公敷政南國而興王之業由之以基當
受命之時非無開國元老也惟爾祖康公闢國
百里而宣化之功由之以廣嘗建夫疆理之績
矣是非周之屏翰乎爾虎先世之功如此今我
命爾來旬而託之以經營者毋曰以予小子之
故効勞王家也當知經營乃爾之世功纘舊服
者自爾善述之事爾當懋建夫經之營之之大
功使奕葉相承無愧於敷治之功可焉我之命

王者之命大臣，必推其世功而勉以繼之也。蓋前人之功，正後人之所當繼也。今王者命大臣，而欲其克纘世功如此，其勉以忠孝之意何至哉！昔宣王命召穆公平淮南之夷，詩人美之。至此，則述王命之詞，意謂：「誕膺天命以撫方夏，文王之受命也；保右命爾，燮伐大商，非武王之受命乎？昔我文武受命之日，非無佐命元勳也，惟爾祖康公敷政南國，而興王之業由之以基。當受命之時，非無開國元老也，惟爾祖康公闢國百里，而宣化之功由之以廣。嘗建夫疆理之績矣，是非周之屏翰乎？爾虎先世之功如此，今我命爾來旬，而託之以經營者，毋曰以予小子之故効勞王家也。當知經營乃爾之世功，纘舊服者，自爾善述之事。爾當懋建夫經之營之之大功，使奕葉相承，無愧於敷治之功可焉。我之命
