When a king commissions a great minister, he invariably invokes the achievements of that minister’s lineage and urges him to carry them forward. For the achievements of predecessors are precisely what their successors ought to continue. Here the king commissions a great minister and wishes him thus to perpetuate his ancestral achievements: how profound is his intention to encourage loyalty and filial devotion!

Formerly, King Xuan commanded Duke Mu of Shao to pacify the Yi peoples south of the Huai River, and the poet praised him. At this point, the poem recounts the words of the royal commission, whose meaning is: “To receive Heaven’s mandate in full and bring peace to the central lands—this was King Wen’s reception of the mandate. ‘Heaven protected and aided you, and commanded you harmoniously to attack great Shang’—was this not King Wu’s reception of the mandate? In former times, when our kings Wen and Wu received the mandate, there were certainly other outstanding servants who assisted them in receiving it; yet it was your ancestor, Duke Kang, who spread good government through the southern lands, thereby laying the foundation for the enterprise of raising our royal house. When they received the mandate, there were certainly other venerable ministers who helped found the state; yet it was your ancestor, Duke Kang, who opened up a domain a hundred li across, thereby extending the work of spreading the royal transforming influence. He established achievements in marking boundaries and ordering the land. Was he not a bulwark of Zhou?

極也厥後于盂之役會中華執盟主而在會者
俛然莫之敢校焉迨至如楚有役偃然而朝諸
侯中國玉帛交見於楚庭矣甚至于虢有會肆
然而長齊晉中州牧伯咸在其下風矣勢形於
伐鄭禍稔於將來固非一朝一夕之故也書法
雖同立義則異聖人慮患何其深哉吁同一舉
號也一則譏其僭王一則惡其猾夏同一稱人
punctuated: 之意，蓋謂中國而夷狄則狄之，引之推之，可遠也。故始見於經，則本其僭竊之罪，正其夷狄之名，著王法焉。於聘魯，則嘉其慕義，接之以禮，與之而不拒也。於伐鄭，則懲其不恪，威之以刑，膺夷狄也。黜之則必比諸夷狄，進之則漸同於中國，正大義，重絕人焉。詞之同異，義各有在，聖人立法何其謹哉！自是楚勢日強，鄭復見伐。楚之勢不減於昔也敗蔡之勢，楚之暴有甚於向也伐鄭之暴，而楚之心則非前日聘魯之心焉。是一役也，《春秋》亦以人書，同於來聘，何哉？聖人之意，蓋謂夷狄浸強，勢傾中國，其患未有紀極也。厥後于盂之役，會中華，執盟主，而在會者俛然莫之敢校焉。迨至如楚有役，偃然而朝諸侯，中國玉帛交見於楚庭矣。甚至于虢有會，肆然而長齊晉，中州牧伯咸在其下風矣。勢形於伐鄭，禍稔於將來，固非一朝一夕之故也。書法雖同，立義則異，聖人慮患何其深哉！吁！同一舉號也，一則譏其僭王，一則惡其猾夏；同一稱人
translation_en:
…the sage’s intention was presumably that a state of the central realm which behaved as a barbarian should be treated as barbarian: drawing it forward or pushing it away, one could keep it at a distance [?]. Thus, when Chu first appears in the Classic, its offense of usurping a title supplies the basis for assigning it its proper designation as barbarian, thereby making manifest the law of the true king. When it sent an embassy to Lu, the text commended its inclination toward righteousness and received it with ritual propriety, acknowledging rather than rejecting it. When it attacked Zheng, the text punished its lack of respect and overawed it with penalties, chastising the barbarians. In demoting it, the text necessarily ranked it with the barbarians; in advancing it, the text gradually accorded it the same standing as the central states. It rectified the great principles of righteousness and treated the severing of ties with others as a grave matter. Whether its wording was alike or different, each usage had its own significance. How scrupulous the sage was in establishing these rules!

Thereafter Chu’s power grew daily, and Zheng again suffered attack. Chu’s power was no less than its former power when it defeated Cai [?]; its violence exceeded that of its earlier attack on Zheng [?]; and its intentions were no longer those it had held when sending an embassy to Lu. Yet for this campaign the Spring and Autumn Annals also used the designation “men,” just as for the embassy. Why? The sage’s intention was presumably that the barbarians were steadily growing stronger, their power threatening to overwhelm the central states, and that the harm they would cause had no foreseeable limit. Subsequently, at the gathering at Yu, Chu assembled the central states and seized the leader of the covenant, while those attending bowed submissively, none daring to resist. Then, when there was a journey to Chu, it complacently received the feudal lords in audience, and jade and silk from the central states appeared in succession at Chu’s court. It went so far that, at the meeting at Guo, Chu brazenly took precedence over Qi and Jin, and the regional leaders of the central realm all stood beneath it. Its power took visible form in the attack on Zheng, while the resulting calamity ripened in the years to come: certainly this was not the work of a single morning or evening. Though the wording of the record was the same, the significance it established differed. How profound was the sage’s concern for future calamity!

Ah! In both cases the state’s designation was used: in one, to censure its usurpation of the royal title; in the other, to condemn its disruption of the Xia realm. In both cases the designation “men” was used…

title: 弘治二年江西鄉試錄
text:
也一則嘉其慕義一則著其浸強春秋謹華夷
之辨抑夷狄存中國之意槩可見矣大抵春秋
之文類例不一故有詞同而事異亦有詞異而
事同如化工隨物賦形如山嶽徙步異狀安可
持一槩之說專一曲之見以論聖人作經之旨
哉故曰春秋非聖人莫能修之
夏公會宰周公齊侯宋子衛侯鄭伯許男
曹伯于葵丘〔僖公九年〕
同考試官教諭謝　批〔作者惑於小傳於胡傳進退之節出入均勞之義多無定見是篇考據明白措詞〕
===
考試官教諭高　批〔春秋以道名分此作得之簡當必嘗用心於經學者〕
考試官教諭傅　批〔得春秋明人臣貴無常尊之義〕
春秋於王臣職任之重唯待以臣禮之常此葵
丘之會而不殊會宰周公聖人之意見矣且夫
齊桓主伯宅心尊安一旦尋于洮之盟為葵丘
banxin: 文　二十一　三冬
punctuated:
也，一則嘉其慕義，一則著其浸強。《春秋》謹華夷之辨，抑夷狄、存中國之意，槩可見矣。大抵《春秋》之文，類例不一，故有詞同而事異，亦有詞異而事同。如化工隨物賦形，如山嶽徙步異狀，安可持一槩之說、專一曲之見，以論聖人作經之旨哉？故曰：「春秋非聖人莫能修之。」
夏，公會宰周公、齊侯、宋子、衛侯、鄭伯、許男、曹伯于葵丘。〔僖公九年〕
同考試官教諭謝批〔作者惑於小傳，於胡傳進退之節、出入均勞之義，多無定見。是篇考據明白，措詞〕
考試官教諭高批〔春秋以道名分，此作得之，簡當，必嘗用心於經學者。〕
考試官教諭傅批〔得春秋明人臣貴無常尊之義。〕
《春秋》於王臣職任之重，唯待以臣禮之常。此葵丘之會而不殊會宰周公，聖人之意見矣。且夫齊桓主伯，宅心尊安，一旦尋于洮之盟，為葵丘
translation_en:
…too: in one instance it commends their inclination toward righteousness; in the other it reveals their growing strength. The intent of the Spring and Autumn Annals—to distinguish carefully between the Chinese and the non-Chinese peoples, restrain the latter, and preserve the central states—can thus broadly be discerned. In general, the textual conventions of the Annals are not uniform: identical wording may describe different circumstances, and different wording may describe identical circumstances. Like nature’s creative workings, which give each thing its particular form, or mountains, which change their appearance as one moves, how could the sage’s purpose in composing the classic be assessed by adhering to a single generalization or insisting upon a partial view? Thus it is said: “None but a sage could compile the Spring and Autumn Annals.”
“In summer, the duke met with Minister Zhou, Duke of Zhou, the Marquis of Qi, the Viscount of Song, the Marquis of Wei, the Earl of Zheng, the Baron of Xu, and the Earl of Cao at Kuiqiu.” 〔Ninth year of Duke Xi.〕
Comment by Associate Examiner Xie, Instructor: 〔Writers are misled by the minor commentaries [?], and often lack a settled understanding of the principles in Hu’s Commentary concerning the proper limits of advancement and withdrawal, and the equal sharing of service at court and away from it. This essay is clear in its examination of the evidence; its wording [comment incomplete].〕
Comment by Examiner Gao, Instructor: 〔The Spring and Autumn Annals articulates titles and distinctions of status. This composition grasps that principle and is concise and apt. Its author must have devoted serious attention to classical learning.〕
Comment by Examiner Fu, Instructor: 〔It grasps the principle elucidated in the Spring and Autumn Annals that a subject, however exalted, has no permanently privileged standing.〕
In treating royal ministers whose offices and responsibilities are weighty, the Spring and Autumn Annals accords them only the ordinary ritual treatment appropriate to subjects. At this meeting at Kuiqiu, it does not distinguish the meeting with Minister Zhou, Duke of Zhou, by a separate formula: here the sage’s intention becomes apparent. Now Duke Huan of Qi presided as hegemon, setting his heart on honoring the royal house and securing its peace. On one occasion, renewing the covenant made at Tao, he held the gathering at Kuiqiu…

title: 弘治二年江西鄉試錄
text:
之會適天子有事于文武賜胙于齊桓而宰周
公實將命下臨焉夫謂之宰周公者以冢宰之
貴兼三公之尊統百官而均四海作股肱而司
耳目其職端揆之職也其任師保之任也職任
之重如此春秋宜殊會之可也今乃祇序于諸
侯之上何哉蓋人臣則有進退之節出入均勞
之義彼宰周公也今雖進為三公宰輔矣安保
久於其位而不退乎今雖入乎朝廷之內矣安
知常在於內而不出乎職雖端揆也可進可退
===
而非常有之職任雖師保也或出或入而非常
有之任非若王世子貴有常尊之可比矣苟殊
會之則臣疑於君其可訓邪故唯序宰周公於
諸侯之上而不以殊會為文其明人臣之義何
如哉吁繼人臣之貴無寵異之詞聖人謹分之
意其嚴矣乎雖然會不殊會固所以尊君而抑
臣矣然是會之事則尤有可稱者焉宰孔之獎
伯主明王禁宣揚乎政教視之賵仲子聘桓公
者孰優而孰劣齊桓之尊禮王臣不敢瀆盟謹
punctuated: 之會，適天子有事于文武，賜胙于齊桓，而宰周公實將命下臨焉。夫謂之宰周公者，以冢宰之貴兼三公之尊，統百官而均四海，作股肱而司耳目。其職端揆之職也，其任師保之任也。職任之重如此，《春秋》宜殊會之可也。今乃祇序于諸侯之上，何哉？蓋人臣則有進退之節、出入均勞之義。彼宰周公也，今雖進為三公宰輔矣，安保久於其位而不退乎？今雖入乎朝廷之內矣，安知常在於內而不出乎？職雖端揆也，可進可退，而非常有之職；任雖師保也，或出或入，而非常有之任。非若王世子貴有常尊之可比矣。苟殊會之，則臣疑於君，其可訓邪？故唯序宰周公於諸侯之上，而不以殊會為文，其明人臣之義何如哉！吁！繼人臣之貴，無寵異之詞，聖人謹分之意，其嚴矣乎！雖然，會不殊會，固所以尊君而抑臣矣。然是會之事，則尤有可稱者焉。宰孔之獎伯主，明王禁，宣揚乎政教，視之賵仲子、聘桓公者，孰優而孰劣？齊桓之尊禮王臣，不敢瀆盟，謹
translation_en:
…the meeting at Kuiqiu. It happened that the Son of Heaven was offering sacrifices to Kings Wen and Wu and bestowed sacrificial meat upon Duke Huan of Qi. The Grand Steward, Duke of Zhou, came down in person bearing the royal command. He is called the Grand Steward, Duke of Zhou, because he combined the eminence of the Grand Steward with the dignity of the Three Dukes. He directed the hundred officials and brought order throughout the realm, serving as the ruler’s limbs and overseeing his eyes and ears. His office was that of chief minister; his responsibility was that of preceptor and guardian. With an office and responsibilities of such weight, it would seem appropriate for the Spring and Autumn Annals to distinguish his participation by separately writing “met with” before his title. Why, then, does it merely place him before the regional lords in the list?

A minister must observe the proper rules of advancement and withdrawal and the principle of sharing service equally, whether serving at court or outside it. Although this Grand Steward, Duke of Zhou, had now risen to be one of the Three Dukes and a chief minister, how could he be certain of remaining long in that position without withdrawing? Although he now served within the royal court, how could he know that he would always remain there and never serve outside it? Though his office was that of chief minister, he could advance or withdraw: it was not an office permanently his. Though his responsibility was that of preceptor and guardian, he might serve outside or within the court: it was not a responsibility permanently his. He could not be compared to the royal heir apparent, whose exalted standing carried an enduring dignity. If his participation were distinguished by a separate “met with,” the minister would appear to rival the ruler. Could that serve as a model? Thus the text merely places the Grand Steward, Duke of Zhou, above the regional lords, without distinguishing him by a separate “met with.” How clearly this reveals the proper standing of a minister! Ah! In recording [?] a minister’s eminence, it uses no expression of special favor. How strict was the Sage’s intention to preserve distinctions of rank!

Nevertheless, withholding a separate “met with” in recording the meeting certainly honors the ruler and restrains the minister. Yet the conduct of this particular meeting offers further grounds for praise. Steward Kong supported the hegemon, clarified the royal prohibitions, and proclaimed the principles of government and instruction. Compared with those who brought funeral gifts for Zhongzi or paid a diplomatic visit to Duke Huan of Lu, who was superior and who inferior? Duke Huan of Qi honored the royal minister with due ceremony and did not dare profane the covenant by involving him in it, scrupulously…

title: 弘治二年江西鄉試錄
text:
嚴乎名分視之盟子虎瀆單子者孰得而孰失
噫此齊桓所以獨盛於五伯而宰孔所以獨賢
於列御也歟
禮記
君天下曰天子朝諸侯分職授政任功曰
予一人
晏邑
同考試官教諭許　批〔題本平易場中作者多欠發揮此篇說理既明詞亦整潔佳作也錄之〕
===
考試官教諭髙　批〔經義發明殆盡〕
考試官教諭傅　批〔詞理明暢〕
人君臨御有總稱之辭聽治有自稱之辭盖人
君天下之主也其於臨御聽治之際豈得無總
稱自稱之辭哉記曲禮者謂夫人君誕膺天命
為天下君握乾闌坤而撫綏乎萬邦出震繼離
而統御乎四海兆民於是而歸心百官於是而
承式人君臨御如此而總稱之曰天子焉謂之
天子者以見父天母地而代天以理物為天下
punctuated:
嚴乎名分，視之盟子虎、瀆單子者，孰得而孰失？噫！此齊桓所以獨盛於五伯，而宰孔所以獨賢於列御也歟！

禮記
「君天下曰天子，朝諸侯、分職、授政、任功，曰予一人。」
晏邑
同考試官教諭許　批〔題本平易，場中作者多欠發揮。此篇說理既明，詞亦整潔，佳作也，錄之。〕
考試官教諭髙　批〔經義發明殆盡。〕
考試官教諭傅　批〔詞理明暢。〕

人君臨御有總稱之辭，聽治有自稱之辭。盖人君天下之主也，其於臨御聽治之際，豈得無總稱、自稱之辭哉？記曲禮者謂夫人君誕膺天命，為天下君，握乾闌坤而撫綏乎萬邦，出震繼離而統御乎四海。兆民於是而歸心，百官於是而承式。人君臨御如此，而總稱之曰天子焉。謂之天子者，以見父天母地而代天以理物，為天下
translation_en:
…strict in observing the distinctions of rank: compared with those who made a covenant with Zihu and treated Shanzi disrespectfully, who acted rightly and who wrongly? Ah! Is this why Duke Huan of Qi alone excelled among the Five Hegemons, and why Zai Kong alone was worthy among the royal officers?

Record of Rites
“When ruling all under Heaven, he is called the Son of Heaven; when receiving the feudal lords at court, allocating offices, entrusting governmental duties, and assigning responsibilities for accomplishments, he calls himself ‘I, the One Man.’”
Yan Yi 晏邑
Associate Examiner Xu, Instructor, comments: 〔The topic is straightforward, but most candidates in the examination hall failed to develop it adequately. This essay explains the principles clearly, and its language is orderly and polished. It is an excellent composition; record it.〕
Examiner Gao, Instructor, comments: 〔The meaning of the classic is elucidated almost exhaustively.〕
Examiner Fu, Instructor, comments: 〔The language and reasoning are clear and fluent.〕

The ruler has a general designation when exercising sovereignty and a term of self-reference when attending to government. For the ruler is the lord of all under Heaven: how could he lack a general designation and a term of self-reference when exercising sovereignty and attending to government? The compiler of “Summary of the Rules of Propriety” means that the ruler receives Heaven’s great mandate and becomes ruler of all under Heaven. Grasping Qian and encompassing Kun [?], he pacifies and comforts the myriad states; coming forth in Zhen and succeeding in Li—the trigrams of thunder and fire—he governs all within the Four Seas. The countless people thereupon give him their allegiance, and the hundred officials follow his model. Such is the ruler’s exercise of sovereignty, and his general designation is therefore “Son of Heaven.” Calling him “Son of Heaven” shows that he takes Heaven as his father and Earth as his mother, ordering all things on Heaven’s behalf, and becomes, for all under Heaven, …

title: 弘治二年江西鄉試錄
text:
之至尊乾父坤母而體天以行道極天下之至
貴不惟臣得以稱之而民亦得以稱之也若夫
負斧依而受四方諸侯之朝建六官而分天地
四時之職授政而有軍政稼政之異任功而有
王功民功之殊人君聽治如此而自稱之曰予
一人焉謂之予一人者以見受朝分職咸歸於
一人之總攬而非群臣所敢專授政任功悉聽
於一人之獨斷而非百辟所敢預雖致自謙之
辭而實寓自任之意也吁一總稱自稱之間而
===
截然有辨如此其致謹於名稱也何如哉抑論
禮莫大於分分莫大於名以下稱君當致其尊
故謂之天子如皇極之民稱其君曰天子作民
父母是已君之自稱常辭其尊故謂之予一人
如成湯誕告萬民自稱曰明聽予一人是已合
而觀之尤信
明則有禮樂幽則有鬼神
同考試官教諭許　批〔此題本言禮樂鬼神一理學者〕
符觀
punctuated:
之至尊；乾父坤母，而體天以行道，極天下之至貴。不惟臣得以稱之，而民亦得以稱之也。若夫負斧依而受四方諸侯之朝，建六官而分天地四時之職，授政而有軍政、稼政之異，任功而有王功、民功之殊，人君聽治如此，而自稱之曰「予一人」焉。謂之「予一人」者，以見受朝分職，咸歸於一人之總攬，而非群臣所敢專；授政任功，悉聽於一人之獨斷，而非百辟所敢預。雖致自謙之辭，而實寓自任之意也。吁！一總稱、自稱之間，而截然有辨如此，其致謹於名稱也何如哉！抑論禮莫大於分，分莫大於名。以下稱君，當致其尊，故謂之「天子」，如《皇極》之民稱其君曰「天子作民父母」，是已。君之自稱，常辭其尊，故謂之「予一人」，如成湯誕告萬民，自稱曰「明聽予一人」，是已。合而觀之，尤信。

明則有禮樂，幽則有鬼神。

同考試官教諭許，批〔此題本言禮樂鬼神一理，學者〕

符觀
translation_en:
…the most exalted under Heaven; taking Qian as his father and Kun as his mother, he embodies Heaven in carrying out the Way and reaches the utmost nobility under Heaven. Not only may his ministers address him by this title; the people may do so as well. As for sitting with his back to the axe-patterned screen to receive the court attendance of the regional lords from every quarter, establishing the six ministries and distributing their duties according to Heaven, Earth, and the four seasons, assigning governmental responsibilities differentiated into military and agricultural affairs, and entrusting meritorious undertakings distinguished as royal service and service to the people: such is the ruler’s conduct of government, and he refers to himself as “I, the One Man.” This designation shows that receiving court attendance and distributing offices all fall under the comprehensive direction of one man, and are matters that the assembled ministers dare not monopolize; assigning governmental responsibilities and entrusting meritorious undertakings all depend upon the sole decision of one man, and are matters in which the many officials dare not intervene. Although the expression conveys humility, it actually contains the intention of taking responsibility upon oneself. Ah! Between the general designation and the designation used of oneself, the distinction is so clear-cut: how scrupulous this care over names and titles is!

Moreover, in discussing ritual propriety, nothing is greater than distinctions of status; in distinctions of status, nothing is greater than names. When inferiors address their ruler, they should accord him the fullest honor, and therefore call him “Son of Heaven.” An example is the people’s designation of their ruler in “The August Ultimate”: “The Son of Heaven acts as father and mother to the people.” When the ruler refers to himself, he regularly disclaims his exalted position, and therefore calls himself “I, the One Man.” An example is Cheng Tang’s great proclamation to the myriad people, in which he refers to himself thus: “Listen attentively to me, the One Man.” Considered together, these examples make the point still more convincing.

“In the manifest realm there are rites and music; in the hidden realm there are ghosts and spirits.”

Comment by Associate Examiner Xu, Instructor: 〔“This topic originally speaks of rites, music, ghosts, and spirits as one principle. Students…”〕

Fu Guan 符觀

title: 弘治二年江西鄉試錄
text:
體認欠真率之究徒理到而詞達者僅見此篇
考試官教諭高　批　說禮樂鬼神一理處切當殆
究心於禮者
考試官教諭傅　批　簡明可觀
顯而為聖人之制作微而為造化之功用蓋禮
樂鬼神一理而已明之有禮樂非即幽之有鬼
神乎記者論禮樂成功合乎造化至此以為聖
人之禮樂即造化之鬼神但有幽明之分耳自
其明而在聖人制作者言之則謂之禮樂焉是
===
故禮有三千三百而與天地同節樂有五音六
律而與天地同和是制作在於聖人矣然禮主
於減鬼之屈也樂主於盈神之伸也禮樂闡鬼
神於有迹則有形之禮樂不異於無形之鬼神
非明則有禮樂而何自其幽而在造化功用者
言之則謂之鬼神焉是故氣靜而往為陰之靈

於造化矣然鬼歛而屈禮之減也神散而伸樂

無物不在所愛之中聖人之心大造之心
也蓋聖人參天地而爲三者也其心之仁
殆與天地上下同流曷嘗有所異哉人惟
我自我人自人夷狄禽獸自夷狄禽獸不
===
知夷狄禽獸主之者人也故一念所愛不
能徧及惟聖人也者以民吾同胞物吾與
也於吾人固愛之夷狄禽獸亦愛之舉天
下之物何者不在吾所愛之中也哉韓昌
黎原人而曰聖人一視同仁其亦真知聖
人之心者歟請申之高極其高明極其明
而無物不覆者天也愽極其愽厚極其厚
而無物不載者地也命於其兩間得五行
之秀者人也人知天之高明覆物以爲天

Nothing lies outside the scope of his love: the sage’s heart is the heart of the great creative power. The sage stands alongside Heaven and Earth to form a triad. The benevolence of his heart flows together with Heaven and Earth, above and below; how could there ever be any difference? Ordinary people merely regard themselves as themselves, other people as other people, and the Yi and Di peoples, birds, and beasts as the Yi and Di peoples, birds, and beasts. They do not understand that humans preside over the Yi and Di peoples, birds, and beasts; thus the love arising in a single thought cannot reach them all. Only the sage holds that “the people are my siblings, and all things are my companions.” He naturally loves our fellow human beings, and he also loves the Yi and Di peoples, birds, and beasts. Of all the things under Heaven, what could lie outside the scope of his love? Han Changli, in his inquiry into humanity, said: “The sage regards all alike with the same benevolence.” Was he not someone who truly understood the sage’s heart? Allow me to elaborate. That which is supremely high and supremely luminous, covering everything without exception, is Heaven. That which is supremely broad and supremely deep, bearing everything without exception, is Earth. Those given life between the two, who receive the finest essence of the Five Phases, are human beings. People recognize Heaven’s height and luminosity, covering all things, and take this to be Heaven…

title: 弘治二年江西鄉試錄
text:
而不知日月星辰之形於上者皆天也人
知地之博厚載物以為地而不知草木山
川之形於下者皆地也人知禀陰陽五行
之秀者為人而不知夷狄禽獸之類皆人
也以日月星辰與天為有異則天道悖而
日月星辰不得其行以山川草木與地為
有殊則地道悖而草木山川不得其平以
夷狄禽獸與人為有間故待人之心殊於
待己况夷狄乎愛己之心異於愛人况禽
===
獸乎是人道非人道而夷狄禽獸不得其
情是知天之為天日月星辰之主也地之
為地草木山川之主也人之為人夷狄禽
獸之主也然天地生物而厚於人天地生
人而厚於聖人聖人能體天地之心以為
心合天地之德以為德擴天地之量以為
量包含徧覆蕩蕩乎其難名含弘廣大浩
浩乎其莫測不視日月自日月星辰自星
辰而知日月星辰皆天也不視山川自山
punctuated: 而不知日月星辰之形於上者皆天也。人知地之博厚載物以為地，而不知草木山川之形於下者皆地也。人知禀陰陽五行之秀者為人，而不知夷狄禽獸之類皆人也。以日月星辰與天為有異，則天道悖，而日月星辰不得其行；以山川草木與地為有殊，則地道悖，而草木山川不得其平；以夷狄禽獸與人為有間，故待人之心殊於待己，况夷狄乎？愛己之心異於愛人，况禽獸乎？是人道非人道，而夷狄禽獸不得其情。是知天之為天，日月星辰之主也；地之為地，草木山川之主也；人之為人，夷狄禽獸之主也。然天地生物而厚於人，天地生人而厚於聖人。聖人能體天地之心以為心，合天地之德以為德，擴天地之量以為量，包含徧覆，蕩蕩乎其難名；含弘廣大，浩浩乎其莫測。不視日月自日月、星辰自星辰，而知日月星辰皆天也；不視山川自山
translation_en:
…yet they do not know that the sun, moon, and stars appearing above are all Heaven. People recognize Earth in its breadth and depth, bearing all things, yet do not know that the grasses, trees, mountains, and rivers appearing below are all Earth. People recognize as human those endowed with the finest essence of yin and yang and the Five Phases, yet do not know that foreign peoples, birds, and beasts are all part of humanity. If one regards the sun, moon, and stars as distinct from Heaven, Heaven’s Way is violated, and the sun, moon, and stars cannot follow their courses. If one regards mountains, rivers, grasses, and trees as separate from Earth, Earth’s Way is violated, and grasses, trees, mountains, and rivers cannot attain their proper balance. If one regards foreign peoples, birds, and beasts as divided from humanity, one consequently treats others with a heart different from that with which one treats oneself—how much more so foreign peoples! One loves oneself with a heart different from that with which one loves others—how much more so birds and beasts! Thus the human Way ceases to be the human Way, and foreign peoples, birds, and beasts cannot find fulfillment according to their natures.
From this we know that Heaven, in being Heaven, is the ruler of the sun, moon, and stars; Earth, in being Earth, is the ruler of grasses, trees, mountains, and rivers; and humanity, in being humanity, is the ruler of foreign peoples, birds, and beasts. Yet when Heaven and Earth bring forth living things, they favor human beings; when they bring forth human beings, they favor sages. The sage can embody the heart of Heaven and Earth as his own heart, unite with their virtue as his own virtue, and expand his capacity to equal theirs. Embracing all and sheltering everything, he is so vast as to defy naming; encompassing, capacious, broad, and great, he is so boundless as to be unfathomable. He does not regard the sun and moon as merely the sun and moon, or the stars as merely the stars, but knows that the sun, moon, and stars are all Heaven. He does not regard mountains and rivers as merely mountains…

text:
川草木自草木而知山川草木皆地也不
視夷狄自夷狄禽獸自禽獸而知夷狄禽
獸皆人也老吾老以及人之老幼吾幼以
及人之幼而吾人之老者幼者皆在所愛
矣親吾親以及人之親長吾長以及人之
長而吾人之親者長者皆在所愛矣綏以
德懷以恩視夷狄皆吾人而同其愛焉食
以時用以禮視禽獸皆吾人而溥其恩焉
故苗民之頑而必感之於文德誕敷之餘
===
魚鳥之微而不盡取於釣弋之際聖人溥
一視之仁如此由是天得其道而日月星
辰不失其行地得其道而山川草木皆得
其平人得其道而夷狄禽獸皆得其寧故
視夷狄如此視禽獸亦如此但於民也仁之
而弗親於禽獸也愛之而弗仁於夷狄也治
之以不治篤近舉遠無不得所主而主之矣
吁聖人以天地萬物為一體莫非己也此其
盡人物之性而極參贊之功歟稽古不虐
punctuated: 川、草木自草木，而知山川草木皆地也；不視夷狄自夷狄、禽獸自禽獸，而知夷狄禽獸皆人也。老吾老以及人之老，幼吾幼以及人之幼，而吾人之老者幼者皆在所愛矣。親吾親以及人之親，長吾長以及人之長，而吾人之親者長者皆在所愛矣。綏以德，懷以恩，視夷狄皆吾人，而同其愛焉；食以時，用以禮，視禽獸皆吾人，而溥其恩焉。故苗民之頑，而必感之於文德誕敷之餘；魚鳥之微，而不盡取於釣弋之際。聖人溥一視之仁如此。由是天得其道，而日月星辰不失其行；地得其道，而山川草木皆得其平；人得其道，而夷狄禽獸皆得其寧。故視夷狄如此，視禽獸亦如此。但於民也，仁之而弗親；於禽獸也，愛之而弗仁；於夷狄也，治之以不治。篤近舉遠，無不得所主而主之矣。吁！聖人以天地萬物為一體，莫非己也。此其盡人物之性，而極參贊之功歟？稽古，不虐
translation_en:
…rivers, or plants as merely plants, but recognizes that mountains, rivers, and plants are all earth. He does not regard the Yi and Di peoples as merely Yi and Di, or birds and beasts as merely birds and beasts, but recognizes that they all belong to the same body as humankind. He honors his own elders and extends this to the elders of others; he cares for his own young and extends this to the young of others. Thus all our elders and young are embraced by his love. He cherishes his own kin and extends this to the kin of others; he respects his own seniors and extends this to the seniors of others. Thus all our kin and seniors are embraced by his love. He brings peace through virtue and wins allegiance through kindness, regarding the Yi and Di as all belonging to our human community and extending the same love to them. He takes birds and beasts for food in due season and uses them according to ritual, regarding them as belonging to the same body as ourselves and extending his kindness universally to them. Thus, stubborn though the Miao people were, he would surely move them through the far-reaching dissemination of civil virtue; insignificant though fish and birds may be, he does not take them all when fishing with a hook or shooting with a corded arrow. Such is the sage’s universal extension of benevolence that regards all alike.

Through this, Heaven attains its Way, and the sun, moon, and stars do not stray from their courses; earth attains its Way, and mountains, rivers, and plants all attain their proper balance; humankind attains its Way, and the Yi and Di, birds and beasts, all attain tranquility. Thus he regards the Yi and Di in this manner, and birds and beasts likewise. Yet toward the people he exercises benevolence without treating them as kin; toward birds and beasts he exercises love without treating them with the benevolence due to people; and toward the Yi and Di he governs through noninterference. He shows devoted care for those nearby and brings those far away within his concern: none fails to find its proper master, who presides over it. Ah! The sage takes Heaven, earth, and the myriad things as one body; nothing is outside his own self. Is this not how he fully realizes the natures of people and things, and brings to the utmost his achievement in participating in and assisting the transforming work of Heaven and earth? translation_en:
…those with no one to turn to; he did not abandon the distressed and destitute. The Man and Yi all submitted; phoenixes appeared in stately bearing, and beasts danced. Here we can see Emperor Shun’s equal benevolence toward all. He cultivated virtue and loved the people, descended from his carriage and wept over an offender; the Sanmiao were brought fully into order, and birds and beasts all lived in harmony. Here we can envision the Great Yu’s equal benevolence toward all. Alas! Emperor Shun is far distant, and the Great Yu has passed away. Now a sage occupies the throne, perceptive and wise, strong and steadfast, balanced and upright. Through benevolence he nurtures all the people; through righteousness he sets all the people aright. We are assuredly among those he loves. The Man, Yi, Rong, and Di are all embraced through his conciliatory care; birds and beasts, too, are enabled to live in harmony. Which among these foreign peoples, birds, and beasts, then, falls outside his love? Fortunately, equal benevolence toward all is witnessed once again today.

Memorial

A memorial of thanks, composed as if for Zhu Xi upon his reappointment as Compiler of the Secret Archives under the Song dynasty. 〔Wu Shizhong〕
Examiner Gao, Instructor, comments: 〔The parallel phrasing follows proper rules.〕
Examiner Fu, Instructor, comments: 〔Classical and elegant.〕

title: 弘治二年江西鄉試錄
text:
清光之地詞臣論撰宜資名世之才訏意凡庸
復叨
寵異上膺
天命中切淵兢茲盖伏遇
仁孝夙成聰明首出
龍姿秀發煥天日之光華
帝德含弘擴乾坤之覆載念
祖宗遺大投艱之重心不忘危推帝王篤近舉
遠之仁治恒先内禮動定省隆
===
孝養於
重華惠事懷柔覃
恩威於朔漠喜直言之策正士登庸
禁道學之譏斯文有慶
不顯篤恭之妙
於昭天道之純乃不世出之
君資大有為之
聖也竊念臣熹賦質甚迂遭時獨異濫厠名於
科第忝藉譽於縉紳去
punctuated:
清光之地，詞臣論撰，宜資名世之才。訏意凡庸，復叨寵異，上膺天命，中切淵兢。茲盖伏遇仁孝夙成，聰明首出，龍姿秀發，煥天日之光華；帝德含弘，擴乾坤之覆載。念祖宗遺大投艱之重，心不忘危；推帝王篤近舉遠之仁，治恒先内。禮動定省，隆孝養於重華；惠事懷柔，覃恩威於朔漠。喜直言之策，正士登庸；禁道學之譏，斯文有慶。不顯篤恭之妙，於昭天道之純，乃不世出之君，資大有為之聖也。
竊念臣熹，賦質甚迂，遭時獨異，濫厠名於科第，忝藉譽於縉紳，去……
translation_en:
…a place illuminated by Your Majesty’s radiant presence. The deliberations and writings of literary officials should draw upon talents renowned in their age. Who would have expected [?] that one so commonplace as I would again receive exceptional favor? Receiving Heaven’s command from above, I feel inwardly the trembling apprehension of one standing over an abyss.
This has come about because I have humbly encountered Your Majesty, whose benevolence and filial devotion matured early and whose intelligence surpasses all others. Your dragonlike bearing shines forth with the brilliance of the sun in heaven; your imperial virtue embraces all, extending the sheltering and sustaining powers of Heaven and Earth. Mindful of the weighty charge your ancestors bequeathed—a great inheritance and arduous responsibilities—you never forget danger. Extending the benevolence of ancient emperors and kings, who cherished those near and brought those far away into service, you consistently give precedence to the inner realm in your government. Your conduct accords with ritual in attending your parent at evening and morning, bringing abundant filial care to Chonghua. Your beneficent undertakings conciliate distant peoples, spreading grace and majesty across the northern deserts. You welcome proposals expressed in frank speech, and upright men rise to office; you prohibit ridicule of the Learning of the Way, and this cultural tradition has cause for rejoicing. How illustrious is the subtle efficacy of your earnest reverence; how manifest the purity of Heaven’s Way! You are indeed a ruler seldom seen in successive ages, a sage endowed for great achievements.
I humbly reflect that I, your servant Xi, am by nature exceedingly impractical, yet have been uniquely fortunate in the age I have encountered. Undeservedly, my name was included among those successful in the examinations; unworthily, I enjoyed a reputation among the scholar-officials. Departing …

title: 弘治二年江西鄉試錄
text:
國數年分符千里當年齡之衰朽值衰戚之
交并冒干
斧扆之嚴得遂宮祠之請分已甘於投閑置
散望竟過於陟要躋華念昔
壽皇知遇之深恒嘆涓埃之未報幸茲
聖明臨御之始重辱
綸綍之遙臨夫
黃閣鸞坡匪乏通古今之宿學而
王堂鰲禁豈無飽經濟之真儒顧惟中秘之
清階爰授外臺之末抜欲風勵於四方之
===
士遠
恩獎於一介之臣祇服
訓辭已深識假寵崇儒之意勉思職業愧難酬
好賢向道之誠抽
蘭臺金匱之藏學如測海覩天祿石渠之富
道若望洋敢不益罄忠誠用圖報稱對揚
休命期畧効於三長敷暢遺經冀粗陳其一得
庶為
punctuated: 國數年，分符千里，當年齡之衰朽，值衰戚之交并，冒干斧扆之嚴，得遂宮祠之請。分已甘於投閑置散，望竟過於陟要躋華。念昔壽皇知遇之深，恒嘆涓埃之未報。幸茲聖明臨御之始，重辱綸綍之遙臨。夫黃閣鸞坡，匪乏通古今之宿學；而王堂鰲禁，豈無飽經濟之真儒？顧惟中秘之清階，爰授外臺之末抜，欲風勵於四方之士，遠恩獎於一介之臣。祇服訓辭，已深識假寵崇儒之意；勉思職業，愧難酬好賢向道之誠。抽蘭臺金匱之藏，學如測海；覩天祿石渠之富，道若望洋。敢不益罄忠誠，用圖報稱？對揚休命，期畧効於三長；敷暢遺經，冀粗陳其一得。庶為
translation_en:
…away from the capital for several years, I held the tally of authority over a thousand li. As age brought decrepitude, and decline and sorrow converged upon me, I ventured to petition Your Majesty’s august throne and obtained permission to take a temple sinecure. For my part, I had already resigned myself to an idle, unassigned position; advancement to an important and distinguished office thus exceeded my expectations. Remembering the profound recognition and favor bestowed upon me by the Retired Emperor, I have constantly lamented that I have not repaid even the tiniest fraction. Fortunately, at the beginning of Your sagacious Majesty’s reign, I have again been honored by an imperial command reaching me from afar.

The Yellow Hall and Phoenix Slope—the chief councillors’ offices and the Hanlin Academy—certainly lack no veteran scholars conversant with antiquity and the present; and can the Royal Hall [?] and the Ao precincts of the palace lack true Confucians thoroughly versed in statecraft? Yet a distinguished rank in the imperial library has been conferred upon this lowliest selection from the provincial administration, with the intention of inspiring scholars throughout the realm and extending favor and encouragement to this solitary servant far away. Reverently receiving your instructions, I already understand deeply your intention to honor Confucian learning through the bestowal of favor. Though I strive to attend to my official duties, I am ashamed that I can scarcely requite your sincerity in cherishing worthy men and turning toward the Way.

Drawing upon the collections of the Orchid Terrace and the Golden Coffer, I find that learning is like sounding the sea; beholding the riches of the Tianlu and Shiqu imperial libraries, I find that pursuing the Way is like gazing upon the boundless ocean. How could I fail to exhaust my loyalty and sincerity still further, seeking thereby to repay your favor fittingly? In gratefully carrying out your gracious command, I hope to offer some small service through the historian’s three strengths—talent, learning, and judgment. In expounding the transmitted classics, I hope to set forth, however roughly, what little insight I have gained, so that it may serve as…

title: 弘治二年江西鄉試錄
text:
治安之勸戒少吝
造化之生成身寄南都忽忽江湖之歲月心馳
北闕依依咫尺之
天顏尚冀
聖壽益增
皇靈丕振民物樂萬年之泰華夷大一統之尊
臣無任瞻
天仰
聖激切屏營之至謹奉
表稱謝以
聞
===
第叁場
策
第一問
呈世中
同考試官訓導陳　批〔五策皆詳而此策條答尤得〕
〔列聖敷教明刑之意末復歸之得人可謂知要者矣〕
同考試官學正洪　批〔敷揚〕
punctuated:
治安之勸戒，少吝造化之生成。身寄南都，忽忽江湖之歲月；心馳北闕，依依咫尺之天顏。尚冀聖壽益增，皇靈丕振，民物樂萬年之泰，華夷大一統之尊。臣無任瞻天仰聖、激切屏營之至，謹奉表稱謝以聞。
第叁場
策
第一問
呈世中
同考試官訓導陳，批〔五策皆詳，而此策條答尤得〕〔列聖敷教明刑之意，末復歸之得人，可謂知要者矣。〕
同考試官學正洪，批〔敷揚〕
translation_en:
…as exhortations and admonitions for peace and good government, [the phrase 少吝 is unclear] in relation to the creative and nurturing work of Heaven. My person resides in the Southern Capital, where the years beside rivers and lakes slip swiftly by; my heart hastens to the northern palace gates, lingering affectionately as though Your celestial countenance were but a few feet away. I still hope that Your Majesty’s sacred lifespan may grow ever longer and Your august power flourish greatly; that the people and all living things may enjoy ten thousand years of peace, and that Chinese and foreign peoples alike may exalt the majesty of the great unified realm. Your servant, gazing toward Heaven and looking up to Your sacred person, cannot contain his profound emotion and trembling awe. I respectfully submit this memorial to express my thanks for Your hearing.
Third Session
Policy Essays
First Question
Cheng Shizhong [?]
Associate Examiner Chen, Assistant Instructor, comments: 〔All five policy essays are detailed, but this essay’s answers, point by point, especially grasp〕〔the successive emperors’ intention in spreading instruction and making punishments clear. At the end, it again comes back to securing the right men. The author may indeed be said to understand the essentials.〕
Associate Examiner Hong, Instructor, comments: 〔Expounding and extolling〕…

title: 弘治二年江西鄉試錄
text:
聖朝教化之美詞意俱暢可謂善鳴
國家之盛者
考試官教諭高　批得
列聖所以垂教之意傑作也
考試官教諭傅　批〔策善荅所問〕
對立言垂教古今之聖同一道明刑弼教
先後之聖同一心葢教所以率乎民而刑
所以防乎民也既有以率之又有以防之
然則
===
帝王之心豈非同欲斯民之不違乎教而一遵
乎道也哉執事發策下詢首及
列聖之法古立教而期於教化之大行甚盛心
也愚生樂育是教有年矣請以一得之愚
為執事陳之夫天降下民作之君以治之
作之師以教之是以古之君天下者繼天
立極必立言以垂教明刑以弼教若唐虞
之使契為司徒以敷五教命臯陶為士師
以明五刑當時之民會極歸極刑期無刑
punctuated:
聖朝教化之美，詞意俱暢，可謂善鳴國家之盛者。
考試官教諭高，批：得列聖所以垂教之意，傑作也。
考試官教諭傅，批：〔策善荅所問〕
對：立言垂教，古今之聖同一道；明刑弼教，先後之聖同一心。葢教所以率乎民，而刑所以防乎民也。既有以率之，又有以防之，然則帝王之心，豈非同欲斯民之不違乎教，而一遵乎道也哉？執事發策下詢，首及列聖之法古立教，而期於教化之大行，甚盛心也。愚生樂育是教有年矣，請以一得之愚為執事陳之。夫天降下民，作之君以治之，作之師以教之。是以古之君天下者，繼天立極，必立言以垂教，明刑以弼教。若唐虞之使契為司徒，以敷五教；命臯陶為士師，以明五刑。當時之民，會極歸極，刑期無刑，
translation_en:
…the beauty of the sagely dynasty’s moral instruction. Both wording and meaning flow freely; this may be called an able celebration of the state’s flourishing.

Examiner Gao, Instructor, comments: “It captures the intent with which the successive sage emperors handed down their teachings. An outstanding work.”

Examiner Fu, Instructor, comments: 〔“The policy essay answers the question well.”〕

In reply: In setting forth words to transmit their teachings, the sages of antiquity and the present share one Way; in making punishments clear to support moral instruction, earlier and later sages share one mind. For moral instruction guides the people, while punishments restrain them. Once there are means both to guide and to restrain them, do not emperors and kings alike desire that these people never depart from the teachings and wholly follow the Way? You, honored examiners, have issued a policy question to inquire of us, beginning with how the successive sage emperors modeled themselves on antiquity in establishing their teachings, and hoping for the widespread implementation of moral instruction. A most admirable intention indeed! This humble student has for years enjoyed being nurtured by these teachings. Allow me to lay before you the little insight my ignorance affords.

Heaven brought forth the people below and established rulers to govern them and teachers to instruct them. Thus those who ruled all under Heaven in antiquity carried on Heaven’s work and established the supreme standard. They invariably set forth words to transmit their teachings and made punishments clear to support moral instruction. For example, in the time of Tang and Yu, Xie was appointed Minister of Education to propagate the five teachings, and Gao Yao was appointed Judge to make the five punishments clear. The people of that time gathered around and turned toward the supreme standard, and punishments aimed at bringing about a state in which no punishments were needed…

title: 弘治二年江西鄉試錄
text:
莫可尚已三代之隆其法寖備化行俗美
匹休唐虞下至漢唐宋雖有願治之君其
於敷教明刑之道不能無愧於古矣胡元
汚華綱常掃地天回泰運篤生
聖人我
太祖高皇帝膺天明命再闢乾坤肇修人紀汛
掃腥羶之陋習挽回中夏之淳風
御製大誥三編律令二書
奎章輝煥一日月之照臨即唐虞五教之敷
===
宸翰森嚴一雷霆之震肅即唐虞五刑之明
也
列聖繼作教戒迭申
太宗文皇帝之爲善陰隲孝順事實
宣宗章皇帝之五倫書善人孝子紀載無遺懿
行嘉言搜羅殆盡録其善所以戒夫惡而
垂教弼教之意昭如也
英宗睿皇帝之大明一統誌
punctuated:
莫可尚已。三代之隆，其法寖備，化行俗美，匹休唐虞。下至漢唐宋，雖有願治之君，其於敷教明刑之道，不能無愧於古矣。胡元汚華，綱常掃地。天回泰運，篤生聖人。我太祖高皇帝膺天明命，再闢乾坤，肇修人紀，汛掃腥羶之陋習，挽回中夏之淳風。御製《大誥》三編，律令二書。奎章輝煥，一日月之照臨，即唐虞五教之敷；宸翰森嚴，一雷霆之震肅，即唐虞五刑之明也。
列聖繼作，教戒迭申。太宗文皇帝之《爲善陰隲》《孝順事實》，宣宗章皇帝之《五倫書》，善人孝子紀載無遺，懿行嘉言搜羅殆盡。録其善，所以戒夫惡，而垂教弼教之意昭如也。
英宗睿皇帝之《大明一統誌》
translation_en:
…nothing could surpass it. At the height of the Three Dynasties, their institutions became increasingly complete; moral transformation spread and customs became admirable, matching the excellence of Tang and Yu. In the Han, Tang, and Song that followed, although there were rulers who aspired to good government, their ways of spreading instruction and clarifying punishments could not stand without shame before antiquity. The barbarian Yuan defiled Chinese civilization, casting the cardinal bonds and constant virtues to the ground. Heaven restored an auspicious course and brought forth a sage. Our Emperor Taizu Gao received Heaven’s manifest mandate, opened heaven and earth anew, and began restoring the norms of human relationships. He swept away the foul customs reeking of meat and mutton and restored the simple, wholesome ways of the Central Lands. He personally composed the three compilations of the Grand Pronouncements and the two works on statutes and ordinances. His resplendent imperial writings shone like the sun and moon: this was the dissemination of the five teachings as under Tang and Yu. His august brushwork inspired awe like thunder: this was the clarification of the five punishments as under Tang and Yu.
Successive sage emperors arose, repeatedly renewing instruction and admonition. Emperor Taizong Wen’s Doing Good and Hidden Recompense (Wei shan yin zhi) and True Accounts of Filial Obedience (Xiaoshun shishi), together with Emperor Xuanzong Zhang’s Book of the Five Relationships (Wulun shu), recorded good people and filial children without omission and gathered almost every instance of exemplary conduct and admirable speech. Recording their goodness served to warn against evil; the intention to transmit moral instruction and reinforce it was plainly evident.
Emperor Yingzong Rui’s Comprehensive Gazetteer of the Great Ming (Da Ming yitong zhi)…

title: 弘治二年江西鄉試錄
text:
憲宗純皇帝之續資治通鑑綱目紀名宦人物
而昭
盛世之人文跡宋元行事而法儒先之衮鉞
考諸古所以示乎今而垂教彌教之意秩
如也
聖聖相承同
心體道
皇極攸建
祖訓丕揚深仁厚澤有以浹洽乎人心盛德至
善有以甄陶乎士類教化以行而風俗以
美矣然而邪枉之民或遠乎聲教奸宄之
輩或罹乎典刑此豈教刑之未至與唐虞
之世尚有四凶鄒魯之間且有盜跖况我
皇明一統之大者乎茲欲黎民於變民協于中
惟在敷教明刑者之得人耳誠使司教者
得人如契之敬敷在寬仰遵
列聖垂教之道於凡
制作之所以率乎民者益申明之俾家傳而
punctuated:
憲宗純皇帝之續資治通鑑綱目，紀名宦人物而昭盛世之人文，跡宋元行事而法儒先之衮鉞。考諸古，所以示乎今，而垂教彌教之意秩如也。
聖聖相承，同心體道，皇極攸建，祖訓丕揚。深仁厚澤，有以浹洽乎人心；盛德至善，有以甄陶乎士類。教化以行，而風俗以美矣。然而邪枉之民或遠乎聲教，奸宄之輩或罹乎典刑，此豈教刑之未至與？唐虞之世尚有四凶，鄒魯之間且有盜跖，况我皇明一統之大者乎？茲欲黎民於變，民協于中，惟在敷教明刑者之得人耳。誠使司教者得人，如契之敬敷在寬，仰遵列聖垂教之道，於凡制作之所以率乎民者，益申明之，俾家傳而
translation_en:
…Emperor Xianzong Chun’s Continuation of the Outline and Details of the Comprehensive Mirror for Aid in Government records distinguished officials and notable figures, displaying the cultural accomplishments of a flourishing age; it traces the deeds of the Song and Yuan dynasties, taking as its standard the praise and blame of earlier Confucian masters. Examining antiquity to instruct the present, it clearly sets forth the intent to transmit and extend moral instruction [?].
Sage sovereign has succeeded sage sovereign, united in embodying the Way. The imperial standard has been established, and the ancestral injunctions widely proclaimed. Profound benevolence and abundant beneficence have permeated the people’s hearts; consummate virtue and perfect goodness have molded the scholars. Moral instruction has spread, and customs have consequently improved. Yet some wayward people remain beyond the reach of imperial moral influence, and some evildoers incur the prescribed punishments. Can this mean that instruction and punishment have not been fully applied? Even in the age of Tang Yao and Yu Shun there were the Four Evildoers, and even in Zou and Lu there was Robber Zhi. How much more must this be so across the vast unified realm of our august Ming! If we now wish the common people to be transformed and brought into harmony with the mean, all depends on finding the right men to disseminate instruction and administer punishments with discernment. If those charged with instruction are indeed the right men, like Xie, who reverently spread instruction with forbearance, they will reverently follow the successive sage sovereigns’ way of transmitting instruction. They will further elucidate all the institutions and enactments intended to guide the people, so that these may be handed down in every household and…

title: 弘治二年江西鄉試錄
text:
人誦則綱常日著而民同歸於有覺何邪
枉之慮乎司刑者得入如皐陶之惟明
克允上體
列聖弼教之心於凡
制作之所以防乎民者益遵行之俾家喻而
戶曉則法禁日明而民不陷於無知何莠
宄之足患乎方今
聖天子在上以重華之德敦維新之化居廊廟
者咸藹藹之吉人釐百工者悉濟濟之多
===
士嘉謨嘉猷日獻于
重瞳善政善教覃敷於四海固無俟於章句
腐儒之迂談矣然而區區芹曝之誠不能
自已惟執事其進教也
第二問
汪俊
同考試官教諭廖 批〔古人忠孝之外儒先皆有定論此策得之而又知善處之要佳士也〕
同考試官教諭丘 批〔忠孝一策〕〔欲風勵士類深〕
punctuated:
人誦，則綱常日著，而民同歸於有覺，何邪枉之慮乎？司刑者得入，如皐陶之惟明克允，上體列聖弼教之心，於凡制作之所以防乎民者益遵行之，俾家喻而戶曉，則法禁日明，而民不陷於無知，何莠宄之足患乎？方今聖天子在上，以重華之德敦維新之化，居廊廟者咸藹藹之吉人，釐百工者悉濟濟之多士。嘉謨嘉猷日獻于重瞳，善政善教覃敷於四海，固無俟於章句腐儒之迂談矣。然而區區芹曝之誠不能自已，惟執事其進教也。

第二問
汪俊

同考試官教諭廖批〔古人忠孝之外，儒先皆有定論。此策得之，而又知善處之要，佳士也。〕

同考試官教諭丘批〔忠孝一策〕〔欲風勵士類深〕
translation_en:
…and recited by everyone, then the cardinal relationships and constant virtues will become clearer each day, and the people will all attain understanding. What concern need there be about the wicked and perverse? If the right men are obtained to administer punishments [?], men who, like Gao Yao, are discerning and truly just, who embody the intentions of the successive sage emperors in supporting moral instruction, and who observe ever more faithfully all the established institutions intended to restrain the people, making them understood in every family and known in every household, then legal prohibitions will become clearer each day, and the people will not fall into wrongdoing through ignorance. What cause for anxiety need there be about malefactors [?]?

Now the sagely Son of Heaven reigns above, fostering the transforming influence of renewal through the virtue of Chonghua [Shun]. Those who occupy the court are all worthy men in abundance; those who administer the many offices are a distinguished multitude of scholars. Excellent plans and counsels are presented daily to the double-pupiled sovereign [an allusion to Shun], and good government and sound instruction spread throughout the realm. There is surely no need for the circuitous discourse of a pedantic scholar preoccupied with textual minutiae. Yet I cannot restrain my humble sincerity in offering these paltry contributions, like gifts of celery or the warmth of the sun. I ask only that you, the presiding officials, grant me further instruction.

Second Policy Question
Wang Jun
