Associate Examiner Qiu, Instructor, comments: 〔A policy essay on loyalty and filial piety.〕〔It seeks to encourage and inspire scholars, deeply …〕

title: 弘治二年江西鄉試錄
text:
立心之微忽得此作能不令人歎服
同考試官教諭鄭　批〔中有識見而文采稚宜在前列〕
考試官教諭高　批〔考據明白而予奪得宜可取〕
考試官教諭傅　批〔發以忠孝之節吾於子是望〕
有立身之大節有處事之大權事不失其
權斯身不失其節大節固不可虧也大權
尤不可失也毫釐有差則爲千里之謬矣
臣子欲立忠孝之節而可不知輕重之權
乎然君親不容於偏重忠孝或難於兩全
===
危急存亡之際出處去就之時處之亦難
矣苟不權其輕重爲善處之術而或得此
失彼能無貽誚天下而取譏後世哉愚也
思所以立身而欲盡臣子之職亦嘗究心
於此矣請因明問而求教焉彼楚執其母
而脅以歸漢者王陵也無棄君急親之理
固爾矣然亦當求所以致母之道也使或
智無所施焉漢不可絕而權歸楚以得母
徐圖與漢或可也坐於事漢而使母有伏
punctuated:
立心之微，忽得此作，能不令人歎服！

同考試官教諭鄭，批〔中有識見而文采稚，宜在前列。〕

考試官教諭高，批〔考據明白而予奪得宜，可取。〕

考試官教諭傅，批〔發以忠孝之節，吾於子是望。〕

有立身之大節，有處事之大權。事不失其權，斯身不失其節。大節固不可虧也，大權尤不可失也。毫釐有差，則爲千里之謬矣。臣子欲立忠孝之節，而可不知輕重之權乎？然君親不容於偏重，忠孝或難於兩全。危急存亡之際，出處去就之時，處之亦難矣。苟不權其輕重爲善處之術，而或得此失彼，能無貽誚天下而取譏後世哉？愚也思所以立身，而欲盡臣子之職，亦嘗究心於此矣。請因明問而求教焉。彼楚執其母而脅以歸漢者，王陵也。無棄君急親之理，固爾矣；然亦當求所以致母之道也。使或智無所施焉，漢不可絕，而權歸楚以得母，徐圖與漢，或可也。坐於事漢而使母有伏
translation_en:
…the subtleties of one's moral intentions. Suddenly encountering this composition, how could one fail to admire it!

Associate Examiner Zheng, an Instructor, comments: 〔There is discernment here, although the literary finish is immature; it deserves a place among the leading entries.〕

Examiner Gao, an Instructor, comments: 〔The examination of historical evidence is clear, and approval and disapproval are appropriately assigned. Worth accepting.〕

Examiner Fu, an Instructor, comments: 〔Give expression to the integrity of loyalty and filial piety: this is what I expect of you.〕

There are cardinal principles of integrity by which one conducts oneself, and there is the essential exercise of discretion in handling affairs. If one exercises discretion correctly in affairs, one preserves one's personal integrity. Cardinal principles must certainly not be compromised, but discretion must especially not be misapplied. A discrepancy of the smallest fraction leads to an error of a thousand li. Can subjects and sons seek to establish their integrity in loyalty and filial piety without understanding how to weigh competing obligations? Yet neither ruler nor parent may be favored to the neglect of the other, and loyalty and filial piety may be difficult to fulfill together. At moments of peril, when survival or destruction hangs in the balance, and when one must decide whether to enter service or withdraw, to leave or remain, handling matters is indeed difficult. Unless one weighs the relative importance of obligations to find a sound way of acting, one may fulfill one duty while failing another. How could one then escape the world's reproaches and the criticism of later generations? In my humble efforts to determine how to conduct myself and fulfill the duties of a subject and son, I too have devoted thought to this matter. Allow me to seek instruction in response to your illuminating question.

The man whose mother Chu seized, threatening him to return to Han [?], was Wang Ling. Certainly, there was no justification for abandoning his ruler to hasten to his parent's aid. Yet he should also have sought a way to recover his mother. If there were no stratagem he could employ, then, although his ties to Han could not be severed, he might perhaps provisionally have gone over to Chu to recover his mother and gradually planned to rejoin Han. To remain fixed on serving Han and expose his mother to the danger of falling upon …

title: 弘治二年江西鄉試錄
text:
劍之虞不過乎賊奪其母而招以城降者
趙苞也無降城全母之義固審矣亦當求
所以生母之方也使或計無所出焉城不
可降而亟降身以全母後圖報復亦可也
勇於決戰而棄母於賊鋒之下不甚乎武
帝有事南越而卜式有父子俱死之願若
可壯矣然不過投其好大喜功之心以為
褒寵眷遇之地父逢其君而子狥其父也
父子之忠孝安在成帝詔討蘇峻而卞壼
===
有父子死難之節信可尚矣是皆出於天
理民彝之懿而無要譽市直之私父死於
忠而子死於孝也父子之忠孝何加李密
陳情乞養孝則得矣固辭徵辟之勤而終
不出者得非恥事二姓之意自在數于袁
攀百號泣孝亦得矣甘於潔身之義而終
不仕者得非痛父非罪之心不平數毛義
奉檄而喜似有奔競富貴之態然家貧親
老者顧不可不為祿仕也義之喜不過權
punctuated: 劍之虞，不過乎？賊奪其母而招以城降者，趙苞也。無降城全母之義，固審矣，亦當求所以生母之方也。使或計無所出焉，城不可降，而亟降身以全母，後圖報復，亦可也。勇於決戰，而棄母於賊鋒之下，不甚乎？武帝有事南越，而卜式有父子俱死之願，若可壯矣。然不過投其好大喜功之心，以為褒寵眷遇之地，父逢其君而子狥其父也。父子之忠孝安在？成帝詔討蘇峻，而卞壼有父子死難之節，信可尚矣。是皆出於天理民彝之懿，而無要譽市直之私，父死於忠而子死於孝也。父子之忠孝何加？李密陳情乞養，孝則得矣。固辭徵辟之勤而終不出者，得非恥事二姓之意自在數于？袁攀百號泣，孝亦得矣。甘於潔身之義而終不仕者，得非痛父非罪之心不平數？毛義奉檄而喜，似有奔競富貴之態。然家貧親老者，顧不可不為祿仕也。義之喜，不過權
translation_en:
…the danger of falling upon a sword—was this not going too far? The man whose mother the rebels seized, seeking thereby to induce him to surrender his city, was Zhao Bao. Certainly, surrendering the city to save his mother would not have been right; yet he should also have sought a means of keeping her alive. Had he been unable to devise any other plan, while the city could not be surrendered, he might have promptly surrendered himself to save his mother, and afterward planned his revenge. Would that not also have been permissible? To press boldly for a decisive battle and abandon his mother to the rebels’ blades—was this not excessive?

When Emperor Wu undertook operations against Nanyue, Bu Shi expressed the wish that father and son should both die in the undertaking. This might seem heroic. Yet it merely catered to the emperor’s appetite for grand ventures and military achievements, making these an avenue to praise, favor, and gracious treatment: the father flattered his ruler, and the son followed his father. Where were their loyalty and filial devotion? When Emperor Cheng ordered the campaign against Su Jun, Bian Kun and his sons displayed their integrity by dying in the crisis. This indeed deserves esteem. Their conduct arose entirely from the excellence of Heaven’s principles and the enduring moral norms of humanity, without any selfish desire to win renown or purchase a reputation for uprightness. The father died for loyalty, and the sons died for filial devotion. What could surpass the loyalty and filial devotion of this father and his sons?

Li Mi set forth his circumstances and begged to be allowed to care for his elder: in filial devotion, he acted rightly. He firmly declined repeated summons to office and ultimately did not come forward. Was this not because he harbored a sense of shame at serving two ruling houses [?]? Yuan Pan [?] cried and wept [?]; he too acted rightly in filial devotion. He willingly upheld the duty of keeping himself unsullied and never took office. Was this not because his anguish over his father’s undeserved punishment remained unappeased [?]?

Mao Yi rejoiced upon receiving an official summons, seemingly displaying an eagerness to pursue wealth and rank. Yet someone whose family is poor and whose parent is aged cannot avoid taking office for its stipend. Yi’s joy was merely a matter of expediency …

title: 弘治二年江西鄉試錄
text:
宜以藉升斗之禄而為養親之具耳若何
而来君子之譏温嶠絕裾而去似有慷慨
立功之志然母養無託者故不可以身許
國也嶠之去不過徼倖以投富貴之機而赴
功名之會耳若何而免春秋之責數子忠
孝之或得或失固不俟贅言而白矣茲
必欲忠孝兩全而立臣子之節君親不背
而合會通之宜求若孔子所謂殺身成仁
而守死善道亦惟權其事勢之重輕何如
耳使息重於法耶則屈法以伸息法重於
息耶則割息以正法如舜之竊負而逃不
害其為孝禹之繼脩鯀績不失其為忠斯
可為萬世之則也然權亦不可輕與焉雖
志學適道者尚未之能爾而況區區於功
名富貴之徒可與之言歟此鯫生未敢輕
議而竊欲從事於學也執事其教之
第三問
江淙
punctuated:
宜，以藉升斗之禄而為養親之具耳，若何而来君子之譏？温嶠絕裾而去，似有慷慨立功之志，然母養無託者，故不可以身許國也。嶠之去，不過徼倖以投富貴之機，而赴功名之會耳，若何而免《春秋》之責？數子忠孝之或得或失，固不俟贅言而白矣。茲必欲忠孝兩全而立臣子之節，君親不背而合會通之宜，求若孔子所謂殺身成仁而守死善道，亦惟權其事勢之重輕何如耳。使息重於法耶，則屈法以伸息；法重於息耶，則割息以正法。如舜之竊負而逃，不害其為孝；禹之繼脩鯀績，不失其為忠。斯可為萬世之則也。然權亦不可輕與焉，雖志學適道者尚未之能爾，而況區區於功名富貴之徒，可與之言歟？此鯫生未敢輕議，而竊欲從事於學也。執事其教之！

第三問

江淙
translation_en:
…an expedient, merely to obtain a modest stipend as a means of supporting his parent. Why should this invite the gentleman’s censure? Wen Jiao tore off his robe’s skirt and departed, seemingly displaying a fervent determination to accomplish great deeds. Yet, having no one to entrust with his mother’s support, he could not properly pledge himself to the state. Jiao’s departure was merely a gamble on an opportunity for wealth and rank, a rush toward an occasion for achievement and fame. How could he escape the censure of the Spring and Autumn Annals? Whether these men succeeded or failed in loyalty and filial piety is already clear, without further elaboration.

If one insists on fulfilling both loyalty and filial piety, establishing the integrity proper to a minister and a son, betraying neither ruler nor parent, and finding the fitting way to reconcile their claims—seeking what Confucius called sacrificing one’s life to achieve humaneness and holding fast to the good Way unto death—then everything depends on weighing the relative importance of the circumstances. If familial affection [?] outweighs the law, bend the law to give affection its due; if the law outweighs affection [?], set affection aside to uphold the law. Thus Shun’s secretly carrying his father away on his back did not impair his filial piety, while Yu’s continuing and completing Gun’s work did not compromise his loyalty. These may serve as models for all ages.

Yet the capacity to exercise such discretion should not be lightly credited to anyone. Even those devoted to learning and advancing along the Way may not yet possess it; how much less can one discuss it with those preoccupied with achievement, fame, wealth, and rank? This humble student therefore dares not pronounce lightly upon it, but wishes privately to devote himself to learning. May you, honored sir, instruct me!

Third Question

Jiang Cong

title: 弘治二年江西鄉試錄
text:
同考試官教諭陳　批〔時務一策場中作者率多冗泛求其切當而鑿然可行者僅見此篇〕
同考試官教諭林　批〔區處四事卓有所見且皆歸之得人誠可謂識時務者〕
同考試官教諭張　批〔斟酌時政能合於古而宜於今如此策者場中蓋不多見〕
考試官教諭高　批〔此策有考據有識見有區畫所謂俊傑舍子其誰〕
考試官教諭傅　批〔處置時務犁然當乎人心蓋有志於用世之學者宜置首選〕
===
讀率由舊章之詩則知事不可不稽諸古
讀天下隨時之易則知事不可不宜於今
蓋不稽諸古則狃於今而不法俗吏之見
也不宜於今則泥於古而不通迂儒之談
也考之古而不悖酌之今而可行則天下
之事斯無弊矣執事發策以舉賢才隆治
道敦教化善風俗下詢承學而欲闡合古
宜今之論是皆時政之大者顧愚何足以
punctuated:
同考試官教諭陳，批〔時務一策，場中作者率多冗泛，求其切當而鑿然可行者，僅見此篇。〕
同考試官教諭林，批〔區處四事，卓有所見，且皆歸之得人，誠可謂識時務者。〕
同考試官教諭張，批〔斟酌時政，能合於古而宜於今，如此策者，場中蓋不多見。〕
考試官教諭高，批〔此策有考據，有識見，有區畫，所謂俊傑，舍子其誰？〕
考試官教諭傅，批〔處置時務，犁然當乎人心，蓋有志於用世之學者，宜置首選。〕
讀「率由舊章」之《詩》，則知事不可不稽諸古；讀「天下隨時」之《易》，則知事不可不宜於今。蓋不稽諸古，則狃於今而不法，俗吏之見也；不宜於今，則泥於古而不通，迂儒之談也。考之古而不悖，酌之今而可行，則天下之事斯無弊矣。執事發策，以舉賢才、隆治道、敦教化、善風俗，下詢承學，而欲闡合古宜今之論，是皆時政之大者。顧愚何足以
translation_en:
Associate Examiner Chen, Instructor, comments: “On this policy question concerning current affairs, most candidates have written prolix and vague answers. In seeking one that is pertinent and demonstrably practicable, I have found only this essay.”

Associate Examiner Lin, Instructor, comments: “His handling of the four matters displays exceptional insight, and he makes all of them depend ultimately on securing the right men. He may truly be called someone who understands the affairs of the time.”

Associate Examiner Zhang, Instructor, comments: “He weighs current governance in a way that accords with antiquity and suits the present. Few policy essays like this have been seen in the examination.”

Examiner Gao, Instructor, comments: “This policy essay offers supporting evidence, discernment, and practical plans. If you are not what is called an outstanding talent, who is?”

Examiner Fu, Instructor, comments: “His proposals for handling current affairs clearly accord with people’s minds. He evidently aspires to learning that can be put to use in public service and should be ranked first.”

Reading ‘Follow the established statutes’ in the Book of Odes, one understands that affairs must be examined against antiquity; reading ‘All under Heaven adapts to the times’ in the Book of Changes, one understands that affairs must suit the present. For to neglect examining antiquity is to become habituated to present practices and lack proper standards—the outlook of a commonplace official. To fail to suit the present is to cling rigidly to antiquity and lack adaptability—the talk of a pedantic scholar. If measures do not conflict with antiquity when tested against it, and are practicable when weighed against present circumstances, then affairs throughout the realm will be free of defects.

You have issued a policy question concerning the advancement of worthy talent, the enhancement of good government, the strengthening of moral instruction, and the improvement of customs. You have deigned to consult us students, seeking an exposition of how to accord with antiquity while suiting the present. These are all major matters of contemporary governance. Yet how could an ignorant person such as I be qualified to…

title: 弘治二年江西鄉試錄
text:
知之然有一得之見求執事而求教焉科
目之制成周鄉舉里選以升其秀選俊造
其法備矣迨後若漢有茂材辟名孝弟力
田諸科唐有六科三科之制宋有三科三
選之目因時沿革固皆足以得人而論其
至當則莫善於成周也我
朝稽古圖治而於科目尤加崇重三年一大
比既鄉試矣而又會試于春官既會試矣
而又進試于
===
大廷考之經術以觀其學繼之論策以探其
才是即成周鄉舉里選升其秀選俊造之
意也司文衡者誠於文之純正典雅者取之而
浮華者不錄險怪者不錄則貢士進士所得
皆實學而人材之盛何患其不比隆於成
周乎考課之法有虞三載考績三考黜陟
幽明其法至矣迨後若漢自丞相以下皆
得奉職奏事考課功能唐有四善二十七
最之制宋有三條七事之評以時損益
punctuated:
知之？然有一得之見，求執事而求教焉。科目之制，成周鄉舉里選，以升其秀，選俊造，其法備矣。迨後，若漢有茂材、辟名、孝弟、力田諸科，唐有六科、三科之制，宋有三科、三選之目，因時沿革，固皆足以得人，而論其至當，則莫善於成周也。我朝稽古圖治，而於科目尤加崇重，三年一大比，既鄉試矣，而又會試于春官；既會試矣，而又進試于大廷。考之經術，以觀其學；繼之論策，以探其才。是即成周鄉舉里選，升其秀，選俊造之意也。司文衡者，誠於文之純正典雅者取之，而浮華者不錄，險怪者不錄，則貢士、進士所得皆實學，而人材之盛，何患其不比隆於成周乎？

考課之法，有虞三載考績，三考黜陟幽明，其法至矣。迨後，若漢自丞相以下，皆得奉職奏事，考課功能；唐有四善二十七最之制，宋有三條七事之評，以時損益，
translation_en:
…understand these matters? Yet I have one insight to offer, and I approach you to seek instruction. As for the system of recruitment categories, in the Zhou dynasty candidates were recommended by their townships and selected by their villages: the outstanding were advanced, and those of exceptional talent and accomplishment were chosen. Its procedures were comprehensive. In later times, the Han had such categories as Outstanding Talent, Recruitment of the Renowned [?], Filial and Fraternal Conduct, and Diligence in Agriculture; the Tang had systems of six categories and three categories; and the Song had classifications of three categories and three selections. Adapting inherited practices to their times, all these were certainly capable of obtaining worthy men. Yet, judged by their utmost suitability, none surpassed the Zhou system. Our dynasty consults antiquity in seeking good government and accords particular honor and importance to examination recruitment. A great examination is held every three years. After the Provincial Examination, candidates take the Metropolitan Examination at the Ministry of Rites; after the Metropolitan Examination, they advance to examination at the imperial court. They are examined in classical learning to assess their scholarship, followed by discourses and policy essays to probe their abilities. This embodies precisely the intent of the Zhou practice of township recommendation and village selection, advancing the outstanding and choosing those of exceptional talent and accomplishment. If those responsible for judging compositions truly select writing that is sound, correct, dignified, and elegant, rejecting the florid and superficial as well as the strained and bizarre, then those obtained as tribute scholars and metropolitan graduates (jinshi) will all possess genuine learning. Why should we worry that the abundance of talent will not rival the flourishing age of Zhou?

As for the system of evaluating officials, under Yu, achievements were assessed every three years; after three assessments, the ineffective were demoted and the capable promoted. This system attained perfection. In later times, under the Han, all officials from the Counsellor-in-Chief downward could report on their discharge of duties, and their achievements and abilities were evaluated. The Tang had a system of four virtues and twenty-seven categories of outstanding performance; the Song had evaluations under three headings and seven matters. These were reduced or expanded to suit the times…

title: 弘治二年江西鄉試錄
text:
皆足以知人而昭論其至要則莫若於有□
也我
朝法古爲治而於考課尤爲注意旣三年一
考以稽殿冣之績又三年一
朝以行黜陟之典參考語以察其賢否用
旌異以別其淑慝是即有虞三載考績王
考黜陟幽明之意也掌銓衡者誠於人之
廉愼公勤者陟之而苛虐者必黜貪懦者
必黜則百司庶職所在皆眞材而治道之
===
隆何患其不媲美於有虞乎教化不敦士
習之不厚也古者人人君子比屋可封豈
不易復矣茲欲厚士習以敦教化必有其
道董子曰正心以正朝廷正朝廷以正百
官在
君相倡導何如耳今
聖天子嗣大歷服之初屢行甄別淑慝之典其
爲世道計至矣使進退人才者奉行
德意而凡進用之際必如古之爵罔及惡德
punctuated:
皆足以知人而昭，論其至要，則莫若於有□也。我朝法古爲治，而於考課尤爲注意。旣三年一考，以稽殿冣之績，又三年一朝，以行黜陟之典。參考語以察其賢否，用旌異以別其淑慝，是即有虞三載考績、王考黜陟幽明之意也。掌銓衡者誠於人之廉愼公勤者陟之，而苛虐者必黜，貪懦者必黜，則百司庶職所在皆眞材，而治道之隆，何患其不媲美於有虞乎？

教化不敦，士習之不厚也。古者人人君子，比屋可封，豈不易復矣？茲欲厚士習以敦教化，必有其道。董子曰：「正心以正朝廷，正朝廷以正百官。」在君相倡導何如耳。今聖天子嗣大歷服之初，屢行甄別淑慝之典，其爲世道計至矣。使進退人才者奉行德意，而凡進用之際，必如古之爵罔及惡德
translation_en:
…all are sufficient to discern men’s qualities and make them manifest [?]. Yet, considering what is most essential, nothing surpasses the practice of You □ [?]. Our dynasty models its government on antiquity and pays particular attention to evaluations of officials. Every three years it conducts an evaluation to examine the worst and best performance; every three years it also holds a court audience to carry out dismissals and promotions. It consults evaluative reports to ascertain officials’ worthiness and confers special recognition to distinguish the good from the wicked. This embodies the intent of the practice under You Yu: assessing achievements every three years and, after “royal assessments” [?], dismissing the benighted and promoting the enlightened. If those responsible for personnel selection truly promote the honest, cautious, impartial, and diligent, invariably dismissing the cruel and oppressive as well as the corrupt and cowardly, then every office and post will be filled with genuine talent. Why should we fear that the excellence of government will fail to rival that of You Yu?

That moral instruction is not firmly established results from the lack of integrity in scholars’ conduct. In antiquity, everyone was a gentleman, and household after household was worthy of enfeoffment. Could this not readily be restored? If we now wish to improve scholars’ conduct and thereby strengthen moral instruction, there must be a way to do so. Master Dong said: “Rectify the heart in order to rectify the court; rectify the court in order to rectify all officials.” It depends only on how the ruler and his chief ministers take the lead. Now, at the beginning of his succession to the great imperial charge [?], our sagely Son of Heaven has repeatedly carried out measures to distinguish the good from the wicked. His concern for the moral order of the age is most thorough. If those who promote and dismiss men of talent carry out his virtuous intentions, then whenever they advance someone to office, they must follow the ancient principle that rank must never be bestowed upon those of evil character…

title: 弘治二年江西鄉試錄
text:
惟賢而無公車上書之私官不及私昵
惟其能而無終南捷徑之誚兩及柑門者
却以素定有如王旦一謁大資者却以不
求有如程顥則禮義廉耻之風行而奔競
躁進者自無矣教化有不敦乎風俗不淳
左道之為害也韓愈人其人火其書廬其
居勢不易為矣茲欲袪左道以正風俗必
有其術孟子曰經正則庶民興庶民興斯
無邪慝矣
===
君相崇尚何如耳今
聖天子嗣登大寳之初節下沙汰僧道之令其
為吾道慮深矣使典司政本者仰體
聖心於凡經畫之際敷陳古道而闢度之分不
舉講明正學而私創之禁必嚴欲除其弊
先從其徒斥之如李吉甫欲排其非必反
其是闢之如李泰伯則君臣父子之道明
而緇衣黄冠者自廢矣風俗有不善乎是
皆時政之大者愚以為合於古宜於今而
punctuated: 惟賢，而無公車上書之私；官不及私昵，惟其能，而無終南捷徑之誚。兩及柑門者，却以素定，有如王旦；一謁大資者，却以不求，有如程顥。則禮義廉耻之風行，而奔競躁進者自無矣，教化有不敦乎？風俗不淳，左道之為害也。韓愈人其人，火其書，廬其居，勢不易為矣。茲欲袪左道以正風俗，必有其術。孟子曰：「經正則庶民興，庶民興斯無邪慝矣。」君相崇尚何如耳。今聖天子嗣登大寳之初，節下沙汰僧道之令，其為吾道慮深矣。使典司政本者仰體聖心，於凡經畫之際，敷陳古道，而闢度之分不舉；講明正學，而私創之禁必嚴。欲除其弊，先從其徒斥之，如李吉甫；欲排其非，必反其是闢之，如李泰伯。則君臣父子之道明，而緇衣黄冠者自廢矣，風俗有不善乎？是皆時政之大者，愚以為合於古、宜於今，而
translation_en:
…only the worthy, without the favoritism associated with submitting petitions through the official carriage office; and let offices go not to private favorites but only to the capable, without incurring the reproach of taking the “shortcut through Zhongnan.” Those who twice approached the Gan Gate [?] should be refused on the grounds that the decision had already been settled, as in the case of Wang Dan; one who paid a visit to the Grand Academician should decline to seek advancement, as in the case of Cheng Hao. Then a spirit of ritual propriety, righteousness, integrity, and shame would prevail, and those who scramble competitively and impatiently for advancement would disappear of themselves. Could moral instruction then fail to flourish?

That customs are impure is due to the harm wrought by heterodox ways. Han Yu’s proposal to return their people to lay status, burn their books, and turn their dwellings into ordinary homes would, under the circumstances, be difficult to carry out. To dispel heterodox ways and rectify customs now, there must be a method. Mencius said: “When the guiding principles are correct, the common people rise to goodness; when the common people rise to goodness, there is no perversity or wickedness.” It depends simply on what the ruler and his chief ministers esteem. At the beginning of his succession to the imperial throne, our sagely Son of Heaven repeatedly issued orders to purge the ranks of Buddhist monks and Daoist priests. Deep indeed is his concern for our Way! Let those responsible for the foundations of government reverently embody the imperial intention. In all their planning, let them expound the ancient Way, so that provisions for permitting ordination are not put into effect [?]; let them elucidate orthodox learning and strictly enforce the prohibition on privately founding religious establishments. To eliminate the abuses, they should begin by expelling their adherents, as Li Jifu did; to reject their errors, they must turn back to what is right and thereby refute them, as Li Taibo did. Then the proper relationships between ruler and minister and between father and son would become clear, and the black-robed monks and yellow-capped Daoist priests would disappear of themselves. Could customs then fail to improve? These are all major matters of present governance. In my humble judgment, they accord with antiquity and suit the present, and…

title: 弘治二年江西鄉試錄
text:
行之在人如此若夫施爲緩急之序因時□
損益之宜又在任治道之責者潤澤焉不
識執事以爲何如
第四問
楊烱
同考試官教諭謝　批〔此策作者多漫無要據是篇文愨意到若老將用兵紀律森嚴而奇正迭出終□〕
節制其策場之巨擘乎
考試官教諭高　批〔有考覈有斷制如燭照數計〕
===
畧無所遺傑作也宜置優選
考試官教諭傅　批〔五策皆佳而將相一策尤詳明蠻雖砡之閟府藏而琦奇錯雜照耀人目且終有取於孔明非素〕
有定見者能之耶
論將相於三代之下當觀其迹而原其心
也夫勲庸之成敗才能之得失皆迹而德
之優劣則心也心術不同君子不以心而
混其迹迹有不一君子豈以迹而間其心
哉故觀其迹而原其心則人物之拳衡定
punctuated:
行之在人如此。若夫施爲緩急之序，因時□損益之宜，又在任治道之責者潤澤焉。不識執事以爲何如？

第四問
楊烱

同考試官教諭謝　批〔此策作者多漫無要據，是篇文愨意到，若老將用兵，紀律森嚴而奇正迭出，終□〕節制，其策場之巨擘乎！

考試官教諭高　批〔有考覈，有斷制，如燭照數計〕，畧無所遺，傑作也，宜置優選。

考試官教諭傅　批〔五策皆佳，而將相一策尤詳明，蠻雖砡之閟府藏而琦奇錯雜，照耀人目，且終有取於孔明，非素〕有定見者能之耶？

論將相於三代之下，當觀其迹而原其心也。夫勲庸之成敗、才能之得失，皆迹，而德之優劣則心也。心術不同，君子不以心而混其迹；迹有不一，君子豈以迹而間其心哉？故觀其迹而原其心，則人物之拳衡定
translation_en:
…Putting these measures into practice depends on people in this way. As for the order of urgency in their implementation, and the appropriate reductions and additions according to the times [one character illegible], those charged with governing must further refine them. I wonder what you think of this.

Fourth Question
Yang Jiong

Comment by Associate Examiner Xie, Instructor: 〔Most who answered this policy question wrote diffusely, without essential supporting grounds. This essay is sincere in expression and fully developed in thought, like a veteran general deploying troops: discipline is stringent, while unconventional and conventional tactics alternate, throughout [illegible]〕 under control. Surely this is a master of the policy-examination arena!

Comment by Examiner Gao, Instructor: 〔There is investigation and verification; there is judgment and decision. It is like illuminating things with a candle and reckoning them by number〕: virtually nothing is overlooked. A masterpiece, deserving a place among the superior selections.

Comment by Examiner Fu, Instructor: 〔All five policy essays are excellent, but the one on generals and chief ministers is particularly detailed and clear. [The following wording is garbled, apparently comparing the essay to a treasury of precious stones:] rare gems mingle together, dazzling the eye. Moreover, in the end he finds something worthy of emulation in Kongming. Could anyone who had not long〕 held settled views accomplish this?

In discussing generals and chief ministers after the Three Dynasties, one should examine their deeds and trace their underlying intentions. Success or failure in meritorious service, and the strengths or shortcomings of ability, all belong to their outward deeds; superiority or inferiority in virtue belongs to the heart. Where their intentions differ, the gentleman does not let those intentions obscure distinctions among their deeds. Where their deeds differ, how could the gentleman let those deeds create distinctions among their underlying intentions? Thus, by examining their deeds and tracing their intentions, the standard for weighing men is established…

title: 弘治二年江西鄉試錄
text:
矣執事發策秋闈舉漢唐以下之將相爲
問而且及於愚生之所取法請爲執事陳
之三代將相如周呂如伊傅才德兼全勲
庸表著固無容以議爲也漢唐而下豈無
得失乎宋庠執政人稱長者懷慎居位坐
鎮雅俗起兵常山忠義奮發者顔真卿也
節度涇原奉身清儉者非段秀實乎而宋
庠無所建明懷慎事積不決真卿功烈不
就秀實處死未善其德皆優而才有不逮
===
矣薛宣身兼數器達於從政元忠慷慨論
事無所屈折而匈奴畏之號曰飛將軍者
李廣也群盜退避號曰張鐵山者非張俊
乎而薛宣政無大體元忠與時俯仰李廣
失道自殺張俊附成和議其才雖長而勲
有不稱矣陳平誅呂安劉兆崇應變成務
不爲無功而平有受金之譏崇進日食之
諛霍光擁昭立宣韓信戰勝攻取不爲無
績而光則不學無術信則乘時徼利其勲
punctuated:
矣。執事發策秋闈，舉漢唐以下之將相爲問，而且及於愚生之所取法，請爲執事陳之。三代將相，如周呂，如伊傅，才德兼全，勲庸表著，固無容以議爲也。漢唐而下，豈無得失乎？宋庠執政，人稱長者；懷慎居位，坐鎮雅俗。起兵常山，忠義奮發者，顔真卿也；節度涇原，奉身清儉者，非段秀實乎？而宋庠無所建明，懷慎事積不決，真卿功烈不就，秀實處死未善，其德皆優，而才有不逮矣。
薛宣身兼數器，達於從政；元忠慷慨論事，無所屈折。而匈奴畏之，號曰「飛將軍」者，李廣也；群盜退避，號曰「張鐵山」者，非張俊乎？而薛宣政無大體，元忠與時俯仰，李廣失道自殺，張俊附成和議，其才雖長，而勲有不稱矣。陳平誅呂安劉，兆崇應變成務，不爲無功，而平有受金之譏，崇進日食之諛。霍光擁昭立宣，韓信戰勝攻取，不爲無績，而光則不學無術，信則乘時徼利，其勲
translation_en:
…is thereby settled. You, honored examiners, have issued policy questions at this autumn’s Provincial Examination, asking about generals and chief ministers from the Han and Tang onward, and also about those whom this humble student would take as models. Allow me to set forth my views. Among the generals and chief ministers of the Three Dynasties, such men as the Duke of Zhou and Lü Shang, Yi Yin and Fu Yue possessed both talent and virtue in full measure, and their meritorious achievements were manifest. There is assuredly no room for criticism of them. But from the Han and Tang onward, were there not both strengths and failings? When Song Xiang held the reins of government, people called him an elder of integrity. Huaishen, while in office, exerted a steadying influence over both the cultivated and the common people. It was Yan Zhenqing who raised troops at Changshan, fired by loyalty and righteousness. And was it not Duan Xiushi who, as Military Commissioner of Jingyuan, lived in purity and frugality? Yet Song Xiang advanced no constructive proposals; Huaishen allowed business to accumulate without decision; Zhenqing failed to bring his meritorious undertaking to fruition; and Xiushi did not handle the circumstances of his death well. All excelled in virtue, but their talents fell short.
Xue Xuan possessed many abilities and was accomplished in government. Yuanzhong spoke boldly on affairs, yielding to no pressure. It was Li Guang whom the Xiongnu feared and called the “Flying General.” And was it not Zhang Jun before whom bands of robbers withdrew, calling him “Zhang the Iron Mountain”? Yet Xue Xuan’s administration lacked a grasp of the essentials; Yuanzhong bent with the times; Li Guang lost his way and killed himself; and Zhang Jun lent his support to bringing about the peace agreement. Although their talents were considerable, their achievements did not measure up. Chen Ping destroyed the Lü clan and secured the Liu house; Zhao Chong [?; apparently Yao Chong] responded to changing circumstances and brought affairs to completion. They were certainly not without merit. Yet Ping was criticized for accepting gold, and Chong offered flattery concerning a solar eclipse. Huo Guang supported Emperor Zhao and enthroned Emperor Xuan; Han Xin won battles and captured his objectives. They were certainly not without achievements. Yet Guang lacked learning and sound methods, while Xin exploited the circumstances to seek personal advantage. Their achievements…

title: 弘治二年江西鄉試錄
text:
雖偉而德不足以副其勲焉是數公者心
迹之短長昭然矣若夫蕭何以謹信守
管籥而進不知止其能免嗜利無恥之譏
馬援頴白首死邊事而老不知休其能觧
薏苡明珠之謗陶侃忠勤似諸葛光弼戰
功齊子儀而蘇峻之亂遷延不至代宗出
幸擁衆不朝恤難勤王之緩師者二公盖
有不能辭其責矣李晟收復乎京城德裕
制御乎藩鎮而私憾延賞不知自責奏貶
===
僧孺立黨自私克伐慾欲之必行者二公
盖有不能免所譏矣張浚志在恢復終
身不主和議而殺曲端逐趙鼎或謂其不
及諸葛之忠王旦慎守法度無所變更而
奉天書受美珠或有以失節馮道為比若
此者才德勲庸亦皆槩見矣而君子猶為
之不滿盖春秋之法責備賢者而瑕瑜不
掩公論攸存烏可以心而或遺其迹哉諸
葛亮王者之佐也而陳壽譏其短於將畧
punctuated: 雖偉，而德不足以副其勲焉。是數公者，心迹之短長昭然矣。若夫蕭何以謹信守管籥，而進不知止，其能免嗜利無恥之譏？馬援頴白首死邊事，而老不知休，其能觧薏苡明珠之謗？陶侃忠勤似諸葛，光弼戰功齊子儀，而蘇峻之亂遷延不至，代宗出幸擁衆不朝，恤難勤王之緩師者，二公盖有不能辭其責矣。李晟收復乎京城，德裕制御乎藩鎮，而私憾延賞，不知自責；奏貶僧孺，立黨自私。克伐慾欲之必行者，二公盖有不能免所譏矣。張浚志在恢復，終身不主和議，而殺曲端、逐趙鼎，或謂其不及諸葛之忠。王旦慎守法度，無所變更，而奉天書、受美珠，或有以失節馮道為比。若此者，才德勲庸亦皆槩見矣，而君子猶為之不滿。盖春秋之法，責備賢者，而瑕瑜不掩，公論攸存，烏可以心而或遺其迹哉？諸葛亮，王者之佐也，而陳壽譏其短於將畧，
translation_en: …though their achievements were great, their virtue was insufficient to match them. The strengths and weaknesses of these men's intentions and conduct are thus plain. As for Xiao He, he guarded the keys with care and trustworthiness, yet did not know when to stop advancing: could he escape criticism for shamelessly coveting gain? Ma Yuan, [unclear character: 頴], died white-haired in frontier service, yet did not know when to retire in old age: could he dispel the slander that his job's tears were lustrous pearls? Tao Kan resembled Zhuge Liang in loyalty and diligence, and Li Guangbi equaled Guo Ziyi in military achievements. Yet during Su Jun's rebellion, Tao delayed and failed to arrive; when Emperor Daizong fled the capital, Li retained his troops and did not attend court. For their slowness in dispatching troops to relieve the crisis and aid the sovereign, these two men could hardly disclaim responsibility. Li Sheng recovered the capital, and Li Deyu brought the regional military commands under control. Yet the former privately resented Zhang Yanshang and failed to reproach himself; the latter memorialized for Niu Sengru's demotion and formed a faction to serve his own interests. For their insistence on giving effect to rivalry, boastfulness, and desires [?], these two men could hardly escape criticism. Zhang Jun set his heart on recovering the lost territory and never in his life advocated a negotiated peace. Yet he killed Qu Duan and drove out Zhao Ding, so some said that his loyalty fell short of Zhuge Liang's. Wang Dan carefully observed the established laws and institutions, changing nothing. Yet he reverently accepted the heavenly writings and received fine pearls, so some compared him to Feng Dao, who forfeited his integrity. In men such as these, talent, virtue, merit, and achievement are all broadly apparent, yet the gentleman still finds grounds for dissatisfaction. For the method of the Spring and Autumn Annals demands completeness of the worthy: neither flaws nor merits obscure the other, and impartial judgment is thereby preserved. How could one consider their intentions and overlook their conduct? Zhuge Liang was a helper fit for a true king, yet Chen Shou criticized his shortcomings in military strategy…

title: 弘治二年江西鄉試錄
text:
曾謂諸葛之才而短於是乎郭子儀社稷
之臣也而史氏謂其窮於奢欲曾謂子儀
之賢而肯為此乎裴度繫國輕重而篡述
主德忠智所寓也烏在其事類諂諛司馬
光恩濟斯民而盡革弊政惟恐不亟也何
在其勢之未可張巡捐軀以障江淮而或
罪其食盡及人巡非素有是心者也韓琦
定策以安社稷而或劾其濮議之非琦豈
真為不忠者哉李綱以一身而負天下之
===
望使得畢力於靖康之間帝轅何至於北
狩岳飛以忠勇而為金人所服使不陷身
於奸檜之手故物必復於中原若此者才
德勳庸亦可無愧矣而衆口猶為之不理
蓋君子所為衆人不識而成敗在天人物
自別豈可以迹而不究其心哉愚也有志
通經學古以待世用久矣而將相之時仕
豈草茅之所敢望乎然將來之志不能為
執事諦若郭汾陽之安於義命岳武穆之
punctuated:
曾謂諸葛之才而短於是乎？郭子儀社稷之臣也，而史氏謂其窮於奢欲，曾謂子儀之賢而肯為此乎？裴度繫國輕重，而篡述主德，忠智所寓也，烏在其事類諂諛？司馬光恩濟斯民，而盡革弊政，惟恐不亟也，何在其勢之未可？張巡捐軀以障江淮，而或罪其食盡及人，巡非素有是心者也。韓琦定策以安社稷，而或劾其濮議之非，琦豈真為不忠者哉？李綱以一身而負天下之望，使得畢力於靖康之間，帝轅何至於北狩？岳飛以忠勇而為金人所服，使不陷身於奸檜之手，故物必復於中原。若此者才德勳庸亦可無愧矣，而衆口猶為之不理。蓋君子所為，衆人不識，而成敗在天，人物自別，豈可以迹而不究其心哉？

愚也有志通經學古，以待世用久矣，而將相之時仕，豈草茅之所敢望乎？然將來之志，不能為執事諦。若郭汾陽之安於義命，岳武穆之
translation_en:
…Could anyone really maintain that a man of Zhuge Liang’s talents was deficient in this? Guo Ziyi was a minister who sustained the state, yet the historians say that he went to extremes in extravagance and desire. Could anyone really maintain that a man of Ziyi’s worth would willingly do such things? Pei Du’s presence or absence determined the strength of the state; his compiling accounts of his sovereign’s virtues [?] embodied his loyalty and wisdom. How did his conduct resemble flattery? Sima Guang bestowed benefits upon the people and abolished harmful policies wholesale, fearing only that he might act too slowly. On what grounds was the situation not yet suitable? Zhang Xun gave his life to shield the Jiang and Huai regions, yet some condemn him because, when provisions ran out, he resorted to eating people. This was never Zhang Xun’s original intention. Han Qi settled the succession to secure the state, yet some impeach him for his error in the controversy over the Prince of Pu. Was Han Qi truly disloyal? Li Gang alone bore the hopes of all under Heaven. Had he been allowed to exert his full strength during the Jingkang era, how could the imperial carriage have come to make its “northern hunt”—the emperor’s captivity in the north? Yue Fei’s loyalty and courage commanded even the respect of the Jin. Had he not fallen into the hands of the treacherous Qin Hui, the former possessions would surely have been recovered in the Central Plain. Such men could stand without shame for their talents, virtue, achievements, and service, yet the multitude still fails to do them justice. The multitude does not understand what exemplary men do; success and failure rest with Heaven, and men’s true stature must be distinguished separately. How can one judge their deeds without investigating their intentions?

I, in my ignorance, have long aspired to master the Classics and study antiquity, preparing to serve the world. Yet how could one still in private life dare aspire to service as a general or chief minister [?]? Nevertheless, I cannot clearly explain to you my aspirations for the future [?]. As for Guo Fenyang’s contentment with righteousness and Heaven’s decree, and Yue Wumu’s …

title: 弘治二年江西鄉試錄
text:
持正不屈周平生之所自許者而韓魏公
之知無不爲司馬公之身徇社稷亦豈非
平日之所服膺者乎至論其出處之正大
事業之光明庶幾乎三代之英若諸葛武
侯一人而已然豈後學易望其後塵也哉
狂斐之言幸進而教之
第五問
晏昇
同考試官教諭許　批〔江右地理人物宜諸士子之所熟知而荅者殊多遺漏此篇條對詳悉且文勢沛然宗數語〕
===
考試官教諭高　批〔善荅所問其積學有素者與〕
〔尤見抱負佳士也〕
考試官教諭傅　批〔策有所據非臆說者〕
彼禹貢閱職方知江右地理沿革之由考
文獻稽圖志知江右人物言行之實蓋地
理隨時而沿革人物因地而盛衰則夫江
右之人物後先傑出而流芳百世者一皆
地靈之所鍾爾豈以沿革而有間哉執事
punctuated:
持正不屈，周平生之所自許者，而韓魏公之知無不爲、司馬公之身徇社稷，亦豈非平日之所服膺者乎？至論其出處之正大、事業之光明，庶幾乎三代之英，若諸葛武侯一人而已。然豈後學易望其後塵也哉？狂斐之言，幸進而教之。

第五問
晏昇
同考試官教諭許　批〔江右地理人物，宜諸士子之所熟知，而荅者殊多遺漏。此篇條對詳悉，且文勢沛然，宗數語。〕
考試官教諭高　批〔善荅所問，其積學有素者與？〕〔尤見抱負，佳士也。〕
考試官教諭傅　批〔策有所據，非臆說者。〕

彼禹貢，閱職方，知江右地理沿革之由；考文獻，稽圖志，知江右人物言行之實。蓋地理隨時而沿革，人物因地而盛衰，則夫江右之人物，後先傑出而流芳百世者，一皆地靈之所鍾爾，豈以沿革而有間哉？執事
translation_en:
…upholding what is right without yielding: this is what I have pledged myself to throughout my life [the character 周 is doubtful]. As for Han, Duke of Wei, acting on everything he knew to be his duty, and Lord Sima sacrificing himself for the altars of soil and grain, have these not also been principles I have always cherished? When it comes to rectitude and greatness in entering office or withdrawing from it, and brilliance in achievement, approaching the outstanding men of the Three Dynasties, perhaps Zhuge, Marquis of Wu, alone qualifies. Yet how could a later student easily hope to follow in his footsteps? I venture to submit these rash and ill-considered words, hoping for your instruction.

Fifth Question
Yan Sheng
Associate Examiner Xu, School Instructor, comments: 〔The geography and notable people of Jiangyou ought to be familiar to all the candidates, yet their answers contain a great many omissions. This essay responds point by point in thorough detail, and its writing flows abundantly. The final phrase, 宗數語, is unclear [?].〕
Examiner Gao, School Instructor, comments: 〔He answers the questions well. Surely he is someone with a longstanding foundation of accumulated learning?〕〔His aspirations are especially evident: a fine scholar.〕
Examiner Fu, School Instructor, comments: 〔This policy essay rests on evidence, rather than conjecture.〕

[Consulting?] the Tribute of Yu and reading the Offices of the Regions, one learns the reasons behind the successive changes in Jiangyou’s geography; examining documentary sources and consulting illustrated gazetteers, one learns the facts about the words and deeds of Jiangyou’s notable people. Geography changes with the times, while the flourishing or decline of notable people depends on their locality. Thus, all those outstanding people who have emerged in Jiangyou, one after another, and whose good names endure for a hundred generations, embody the concentrated spiritual potency of the land. How could changes in territorial arrangements interrupt this? You, sir, …

title: 弘治二年江西鄉試錄
text:
發策以地理人物下詢承學其注望之意
深矣請條陳之江右為天下之巨藩山川
擅四方之形勝襟帶江湖而延袤千有餘
里控引荆粵而統領十有三郡絃誦相聞
衣冠萃止為東南一都會地靈人傑信不
誣矣以地理言之分服之制古未有也帝
堯疆理天下制甸侯綏要荒而始有五服
之名大禹水土既平又因地域遠近以弼
成五服之制周改為侯甸男采衛蠻夷鎮
===
蕃之九服名雖不同而實不出於五服也
江右則在衛要二服之間九州之名古所
有也帝舜紹堯致治肇十有二州因冀州
之地廣而分為幽并因青州之地餘而析
為營州大禹治水作貢亦因其舊合幽并
之地歸於冀以營州之地復於青是十有
二州之肇名雖不一而實不出於九州也
江右則跨荆揚二州之界秦併六國分天下
為三十六郡各有所隸此則南郡九江章
punctuated:
發策，以地理人物下詢承學，其注望之意深矣。請條陳之。江右為天下之巨藩，山川擅四方之形勝，襟帶江湖而延袤千有餘里，控引荆粵而統領十有三郡。絃誦相聞，衣冠萃止，為東南一都會。地靈人傑，信不誣矣。
以地理言之，分服之制，古未有也。帝堯疆理天下，制甸侯綏要荒，而始有五服之名。大禹水土既平，又因地域遠近，以弼成五服之制。周改為侯甸男采衛蠻夷鎮蕃之九服，名雖不同，而實不出於五服也。江右則在衛要二服之間。九州之名，古所有也。帝舜紹堯致治，肇十有二州，因冀州之地廣而分為幽并，因青州之地餘而析為營州。大禹治水作貢，亦因其舊，合幽并之地歸於冀，以營州之地復於青。是十有二州之肇，名雖不一，而實不出於九州也。江右則跨荆揚二州之界。秦併六國，分天下為三十六郡，各有所隸，此則南郡、九江、章
translation_en:
…you have issued a policy question, graciously asking us students about geography and notable people; the expectations you place upon us are profound indeed. Allow me to set out the particulars. Jiangyou is a great bulwark of the realm. Its mountains and rivers give it an outstanding strategic configuration; rivers and lakes gird it, and it extends for more than a thousand li. It commands the approaches to Jing and Yue and encompasses thirteen prefectures. The sounds of strings and recitation carry from place to place, and men of learning and office gather here, making it a metropolitan center of the southeast. That this land’s numinous qualities produce outstanding people is surely no empty claim.
Speaking of geography, the system of dividing the realm into service zones did not exist in earliest antiquity. Emperor Yao demarcated the realm and established the Dian, Hou, Sui, Yao, and Huang zones: thus the names of the Five Service Zones first arose. After the Great Yu had brought the waters and lands into order, he likewise took account of distance to help complete this system. The Zhou changed these into nine zones: Hou, Dian, Nan, Cai, Wei, Man, Yi, Zhen, and Fan. Although the names differed, in substance they did not depart from the Five Service Zones. Jiangyou lay between the Wei and Yao zones.
The names of the Nine Provinces existed in antiquity. Emperor Shun succeeded Yao in governing the realm and first established twelve provinces. Because Jizhou was extensive, he divided off Youzhou and Bingzhou; because Qingzhou had land to spare, he separated out Yingzhou. When the Great Yu controlled the floods and instituted tribute, he likewise followed the earlier arrangement, returning the lands of Youzhou and Bingzhou to Jizhou and restoring Yingzhou’s territory to Qingzhou. Thus, although the establishment of twelve provinces produced different names, in substance the arrangement did not depart from the Nine Provinces. Jiangyou straddled the boundary between Jingzhou and Yangzhou. When Qin annexed the six states, it divided the realm into thirty-six commanderies, each territory having its own administrative affiliation. This region fell under Nan Commandery, Jiujiang, and Zhang[?]…

title: 弘治二年江西鄉試錄
text:
郡之所隸也漢有天下又分爲十二部各
置刺史此則楊州刺史之所領也唐更漢
制分天下爲十道而此則江南西道焉所
以分道者因山川之形便耳元置中書省
又分十二行省而此則江西行省焉所以
分省者因天下之事繁耳以人物言之若
盱江十賢則有陳彭年之上表獻箴詳練
儀制李覯之博通經史天下知名天資警
敏而一覽輒記者曾子固也身居翰苑而
===
文重當時者曾子宣也曾子開立朝端嚴
殊有大臣之體王無咎好書力學填爲學
者之師安貧守道志希古人極諫將兵文
名盛著吕黄公鄧潤甫之可嘉也博學淹
貫彈劾不回刑獄詳明時皆稱賞朱京朱
彥之可尚也廬陵之四忠一節則有歐陽
脩文章蓋世匡朔盡心而獲文忠之謚胡
銓力排和議乞斬姦檜而有忠簡之稱節
義不屈罵賊而死謚之以忠襄者楊邦乂
punctuated:
郡之所隸也。漢有天下，又分爲十二部，各置刺史，此則楊州刺史之所領也。唐更漢制，分天下爲十道，而此則江南西道焉。所以分道者，因山川之形便耳。元置中書省，又分十二行省，而此則江西行省焉。所以分省者，因天下之事繁耳。
以人物言之，若盱江十賢，則有陳彭年之上表獻箴，詳練儀制；李覯之博通經史，天下知名。天資警敏而一覽輒記者，曾子固也；身居翰苑而文重當時者，曾子宣也。曾子開立朝端嚴，殊有大臣之體；王無咎好書力學，填爲學者之師。安貧守道，志希古人；極諫將兵，文名盛著，吕黄公、鄧潤甫之可嘉也。博學淹貫，彈劾不回；刑獄詳明，時皆稱賞，朱京、朱彥之可尚也。廬陵之四忠一節，則有歐陽脩文章蓋世，匡朔盡心，而獲文忠之謚；胡銓力排和議，乞斬姦檜，而有忠簡之稱。節義不屈，罵賊而死，謚之以忠襄者，楊邦乂
translation_en:
…was under the jurisdiction of these commanderies. When the Han possessed the realm, it further divided it into twelve regions, each with a Regional Inspector; this territory was under the Regional Inspector of Yangzhou. The Tang altered the Han system, dividing the realm into ten circuits; this territory constituted Jiangnan West Circuit. The circuits were divided simply according to the convenient configurations of mountains and rivers. The Yuan established the Secretariat and further divided the realm into twelve Branch Secretariats; this territory constituted the Jiangxi Branch Secretariat. The provinces were divided simply because the affairs of the realm were numerous and complex.
Speaking of notable men, among the Ten Worthies of Xujiang were Chen Pengnian, who submitted memorials and admonitions and was thoroughly versed in ceremonial institutions, and Li Gou, whose extensive mastery of the classics and histories made him renowned throughout the realm. Zeng Zigu was naturally alert and quick-witted, remembering whatever he read at a glance. Zeng Zixuan served in the Hanlin Academy, and his writings were highly esteemed in his day. Zeng Zikai was upright and dignified at court, possessing to an exceptional degree the bearing of a great minister. Wang Wujiu loved books and studied diligently, becoming [?] a teacher of scholars. Contentment in poverty, adherence to the Way, and the aspiration to emulate the ancients; forthright remonstrance, command of troops, and outstanding literary renown—these were the admirable qualities of Lü Huanggong [?] and Deng Runfu. Extensive and comprehensive learning and unwavering impeachment of wrongdoing; thorough understanding of penal cases, winning universal praise in their time—these were the estimable qualities of Zhu Jing and Zhu Yan.
Among Luling’s Four Loyal Men and One Man of Integrity was Ouyang Xiu, whose literary accomplishments surpassed his age and who devoted himself wholeheartedly to upholding the dynasty [?], earning the posthumous title Wenzhong, “Cultured and Loyal.” Hu Quan vigorously opposed peace negotiations and petitioned for the execution of the treacherous Qin Hui, earning the designation Zhongjian, “Loyal and Forthright.” The man who remained unyielding in integrity and righteousness, died cursing the rebels, and received the posthumous title Zhongxiang, “Loyal and Helpful,” was Yang Bangyi…

title: 弘治二年江西鄉試錄
text:
也博學宏詞力排雚倖謚之以文忠者周
必大也楊萬里憂憤邊釁不食而死謚之
以文節不亦宜乎之數君子賢聲眙著於
古今忠節貫徹乎天地何表表邪陶淵明
清風高節恥身後代劉遺民隱居樂道環
堵蕭然與夫周續之博通經緯讀易閑居
非潯陽之三隱乎劉敞學博文贍諷諫據
經劉攽博極群書不附執政性資俏直極
論新法之害者孔文仲也詆王氏學嘗論
===
科目之弊者孔武仲也與夫孔平仲之長
於史學尤工文詞非臨江之二劉三孔乎
之數君子或甘老於山林或持正於朝著
何錚錚邪徐孺下陳蕃之榻所以致之者
由其恭儉義讓清風高節而然耳豈不足
以動人之傾仰乎陳雷締膠漆之盟所以
慶之者由其輕財重義推舉相讓而然耳
豈不足以起人之敬慕乎江右之地理人
物其槩如此愚也生長於斯覽山川之勝
punctuated: 也。博學宏詞，力排雚倖，謚之以文忠者，周必大也。楊萬里憂憤邊釁，不食而死，謚之以文節，不亦宜乎？之數君子，賢聲眙著於古今，忠節貫徹乎天地，何表表邪！陶淵明清風高節，恥身後代；劉遺民隱居樂道，環堵蕭然；與夫周續之博通經緯，讀易閑居，非潯陽之三隱乎？劉敞學博文贍，諷諫據經；劉攽博極群書，不附執政；性資俏直，極論新法之害者，孔文仲也；詆王氏學，嘗論科目之弊者，孔武仲也；與夫孔平仲之長於史學，尤工文詞，非臨江之二劉三孔乎？之數君子，或甘老於山林，或持正於朝著，何錚錚邪！徐孺下陳蕃之榻，所以致之者，由其恭儉義讓、清風高節而然耳，豈不足以動人之傾仰乎？陳雷締膠漆之盟，所以慶之者，由其輕財重義、推舉相讓而然耳，豈不足以起人之敬慕乎？江右之地理人物，其槩如此。愚也生長於斯，覽山川之勝
translation_en:
…Such was he. Zhou Bida was broadly learned and accomplished in literary composition; he vigorously opposed powerful favorites [?] and received the posthumous title Wenzhong, “Cultured and Loyal.” Yang Wanli, distressed and indignant over hostilities on the frontier, refused food and died. Was it not fitting that he received the posthumous title Wenjie, “Cultured and Principled”? These gentlemen’s reputations for worthiness shone forth [?] through past and present, and their loyalty and integrity extended throughout Heaven and Earth. How outstanding they were!

Tao Yuanming possessed an unsullied character and lofty integrity, disdaining to serve a succeeding dynasty [?]. Liu Yimin lived in retirement, delighting in the Way, his humble dwelling bare and quiet. Together with Zhou Xuzhi, who was broadly versed in the canonical and apocryphal writings and read the Book of Changes in retirement, were they not the Three Recluses of Xunyang? Liu Chang possessed extensive learning and abundant literary talent, grounding his remonstrances in the classics. Liu Ban read widely across the whole range of books and did not attach himself to those in power. Kong Wenzhong was forthright by nature [?] and argued forcefully against the harm done by the New Policies. Kong Wuzhong criticized the learning of Wang and once discussed the defects of the examination system. Together with Kong Pingzhong, who excelled in historical scholarship and was especially accomplished in literary composition, were they not the Two Lius and Three Kongs of Linjiang? These gentlemen either willingly grew old among the mountains and forests or upheld rectitude at court. How unbending they were!

Xu Ru induced Chen Fan to lower his couch for him. What won him this reception was simply his reverence, frugality, righteousness, and deference, together with his unsullied character and lofty integrity. Were these not enough to move others to profound admiration? Chen and Lei formed a bond as firm as glue and lacquer. What made it worthy of celebration was simply that they valued righteousness above wealth, recommended one another, and yielded precedence to each other. Were these not enough to inspire respect and admiration?

Such, in broad outline, are the geography and notable people of Jiangyou. I, in my humble capacity, was born and raised here; beholding the splendid mountains and rivers…

title: 弘治二年江西鄉試錄
text:
仰先哲之風欲追前躅而流芳聲也素矣
豈敢自待以薄而負山川之秀哉
punctuated: 仰先哲之風，欲追前躅而流芳聲也，素矣。豈敢自待以薄，而負山川之秀哉？
translation_en: …I look up to the example of the worthies of old; my desire to follow in their footsteps and leave a fragrant reputation has long endured. How could I dare set low standards for myself and betray the splendid gifts of these mountains and rivers?

title: 弘治二年江西鄉試錄
text:
江西鄉試錄後序
皇明法古爲治三年一大比賓興
其賢能布列庶位阜成兆民
比隆唐虞三代帝王之治猗
歟盛哉弘治乙酉適當其期
江西巡按監察御史暨布按
二司重臣協議禮聘文學之
===
臣主典考試而監臨提調監
試之官率諸職事矢心秉公
合十三郡就試之士鎖院而
三試之詳考較公去取遵
定制取其文之中式者得九十
五人旣第其氏名復選文理
純正者載之於錄將獻諸
punctuated:
江西鄉試錄後序

translation_en:
Postface to the Record of the Jiangxi Provincial Examination

Our august Ming dynasty models its governance on antiquity. Every three years it holds a great examination, honoring and advancing the worthy and able, distributing them among the various offices, and thereby enriching and perfecting the lives of the myriad people. Its flourishing governance equals that of the emperors and kings of Tang, Yu, and the Three Dynasties. Ah, how magnificent!

In the yiyou year of the Hongzhi reign [?], the appointed time duly arrived. The Regional Inspector of Jiangxi, an Investigating Censor, together with the senior officials of the Provincial Administration Commission and the Provincial Surveillance Commission, deliberated jointly and ceremonially invited officials distinguished in literary learning to preside over the examination. The Supervising Official, Proctor, and officials overseeing the examination led all those charged with its duties in pledging to act impartially. They assembled the examination candidates from the thirteen prefectures, sealed the examination compound, and examined them in three sessions. They assessed and compared the papers carefully, accepted or rejected them impartially, and followed the established regulations. Ninety-five men were selected whose compositions met the prescribed standards. title: 弘治二年江西鄉試錄
text:
天府傳播四方以垂永久與試
選者一何榮哉行當升於春
官與天下士角藝爭雄駸駸
乎嚮用而職位之受有日矣
其可不思所以副其實稱其
名哉異日有職也必用其材
以脩政立事有位也必顯其
===
德以建勳樹業上裨於
朝廷下有益於生民斯名實相
符科目有光矣或尸位素飡
罔知報
國遠道千譽不務恤民甚至隳
名檢而事貪墨得罪於名數
見訾於公論辱孰甚焉於科
punctuated: 天府，傳播四方，以垂永久。與試選者，一何榮哉！行當升於春官，與天下士角藝爭雄，駸駸乎嚮用，而職位之受有日矣。其可不思所以副其實、稱其名哉？異日有職也，必用其材以脩政立事；有位也，必顯其德以建勳樹業。上裨於朝廷，下有益於生民，斯名實相符，科目有光矣。或尸位素飡，罔知報國，遠道千譽，不務恤民，甚至隳名檢而事貪墨，得罪於名數，見訾於公論，辱孰甚焉？於科
translation_en:
…to the imperial repository, to be circulated throughout the realm and preserved for all time. How glorious it is for those selected through this examination! Soon they will advance to the Ministry of Rites, there to compete in literary skill and vie for distinction with scholars from throughout the realm. They will steadily approach appointment, and the day when they receive official posts will come. How can they fail to consider how to make their actual accomplishments worthy of their reputation? When they hold office in the future, they must employ their talents to improve government and accomplish its work; when they attain rank, they must manifest their virtue by performing meritorious service and establishing lasting achievements. Above, they will aid the court; below, they will benefit the people. Thus reputation and reality will accord, and the examination system will be honored.

If, however, they occupy office idly and draw salaries without service, knowing nothing of repaying the state; if they stray from the Way and seek praise [?], neglecting the people's welfare; or even abandon their good name and standards of conduct and engage in corruption, offending against the established order of status [?] and earning the censure of public opinion—what disgrace could be greater? What benefit would this bring to the examination…

title: 弘治二年江西鄉試錄
text:
目何益俊論校文之列故序
於小錄之後以爲諸士之戒
尚擇而勉之
山東兗州府沂州郯城縣儒
學教諭高俊謹序
punctuated:
目何益？俊論校文之列，故序於小錄之後，以爲諸士之戒，尚擇而勉之。
山東兗州府沂州郯城縣儒學教諭高俊謹序。
translation_en:
…what benefit does this bring to the examination system? I, Jun, was among those charged with evaluating the examination essays [?], and therefore have written this postface to the brief record as an admonition to the candidates. May they choose what is right and diligently pursue it.
Respectfully written by Gao Jun, Instructor of the Confucian School of Tancheng County, Yizhou Subprefecture, Yanzhou Prefecture, Shandong.
